And Noah rejoiced that this portion came forth for Shem and for his sons, and he remembered all that he had spoken with his mouth in prophecy; for he had said: 'Blessed be the Lord God of Shem And may the Lord dwell in the dwelling of Shem.' (8:18).

And he knew that the Garden of Eden is the holy of holies, and the dwelling of the Lord, and Mount Sinai the centre of the desert, and Mount Zion -the centre of the navel of the earth: these three were created as holy places facing each other. (8:19).
And he blessed the God of gods, who had put the word of the Lord into his mouth, and the Lord for evermore. (8:20).

And he knew that a blessed portion and a blessing had come to Shem and his sons to the generations for ever -the whole land of Eden and the whole land of the Red Sea, and the whole land of the east and India, and on the Red Sea and the mountains thereof, and all the land of Bashan, and all the land of Lebanon and the islands of Kaftur, and all the mountains of Sanir and 'Amana, and the mountains of Asshur in the north, and all the land of Elam, Asshur, and Babel, and Susan and Ma'edai, and all the mountains of Ararat, and all the region beyond the sea, which is beyond the mountains of Asshur towards the north, a blessed and spacious land, and all that is in it is very good. (8:21).

And for Ham came forth the second portion, beyond the Gihon towards the south to the right of the Garden, and it extends towards the south and it extends to all the mountains of fire, and it extends towards the west to the sea of 'Atel and it extends towards the west till it reaches the sea of Ma'uk -that (sea) into which everything which is not destroyed descends. (8:22).

And it goes forth towards the north to the limits of Gadir, and it goes forth to the coast of the waters of the sea to the waters of the great sea till it draws near to the river Gihon, and goes along the river Gihon till it reaches the right of the Garden of Eden. (8:23).
And this is the land which came forth for Ham as the portion which he was to occupy for ever for himself and his sons to their generations for ever. (8:24).

And for Japheth came forth the third portion beyond the river Tina to the north of the outflow of its waters, and it extends north- easterly to the whole region of Gog, and to all the country east thereof. (8:25).

And it extends northerly to the north, and it extends to the mountains of Qelt towards the north, and towards the sea of Ma'uk, and it goes forth to the east of Gadir as far as the region of the waters of the sea. (8:26).
And it extends until it approaches the west of Fara and it returns towards 'Aferag, and it extends easterly to the waters of the sea of Me'at. (8:27).
And it extends to the region of the river Tina in a north-easterly direction until it approaches the boundary of its waters towards the mountain Rafa, and it turns round towards the north. (8:28).

This is the land which came forth for Japheth and his sons as the portion of his inheritance which he should possess for himself and his sons, for their generations for ever; five great islands, and a great land in the north. (8:29).
But it is cold, and the land of Ham is hot, and the land of Shem is neither hot nor cold, but it is of blended cold and heat. (8:30).
crossRefs: Genesis 10:21-32: The sons of Shem down to Peleg, in whose days the earth was divided, the single remark this chapter builds an entire settlement of lands on.
Genesis 11:10-19: The line from Shem to Peleg with the years of each birth, which this chapter restates as jubilees and weeks.
Deuteronomy 32:8: When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance He set the bounds of the peoples, the division by lot this chapter narrates.
Genesis 2:10-14: The four rivers going out of Eden, Pishon and Gihon and Hiddekel and Euphrates, two of which are used here as boundary markers.
Acts 17:26: God made every nation of men from one and fixed the times appointed for them and the boundaries of their dwelling.

translationNotes.note: A generation between Arpachshad and Shelah. Genesis 11:12 has Arpachshad father Shelah directly; Luke 3:36 lists a Cainan between the two, as the Greek Old Testament does, and this chapter follows that longer line. Jubilees then adds what neither carries: that Kainam found a rock carved with the watchers' teaching on the omens of sun, moon and stars, copied it, and kept it from Noah.

Land was assigned by lot, a physical drawing of marked stones, and the result was treated as binding. Joshua 18:6-10 divides Canaan among the tribes that way at Shiloh, and Proverbs 16:33 says the lot is cast into the lap but its every decision is from the LORD. At 8:11 Noah's sons reach out and take the writing from their father's bosom.

translationNotes.term: The river Tina and the sea Me'at
translationNotes.note: The borders here are traced by real waters under old names. Tina is the Tanais, the river ancient geographers used as the line between Europe and Asia, now the Don; Me'at is the Maeotis, the shallow sea it empties into, now the Sea of Azov. Gadir at the far west is Gades, modern Cadiz on the Atlantic coast of Spain, and the tongue of the Egyptian Sea is the eastern Mediterranean.

At 8:19 Noah names the garden of Eden as the holy of holies and the dwelling of the Lord, Mount Sinai as the centre of the desert, and Mount Zion as the centre of the navel of the earth, all three facing one another. Ezekiel 38:12 uses that same navel image of a people dwelling in the middle of the earth. Genesis sets out no such arrangement.

Caphtor, the island home the Philistines came from. Amos 9:7 says the LORD brought the Philistines up from Caphtor as He brought Israel from Egypt, and Jeremiah 47:4 calls them the remnant of the country of Caphtor. At 8:21 its islands are counted inside Shem's portion.

stories.keyTakeaway: Kainam copies a rock carving that holds the Watchers' teaching about the sun, moon and stars. The earth is then divided by lot among Shem, Ham and Japheth and the borders are traced river by river. Shem draws the middle, which holds Eden, Sinai and Zion, three holy places facing each other.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 9
summaryBullets: And Ham divided amongst his sons, and the first portion came forth for Cush towards the east, and to the west of him for Mizraim, and to the west of him for Put, and to the west of him [and to the west thereof] on the sea for Canaan. (9:1).

And Shem also divided amongst his sons, and the first portion came forth for Ham and his sons, to the east of the river Tigris till it approachcs the east, the whole land of India, and on the Red Sea on its coast, and the waters of Dedan, and all the mountains of Mebri and Ela, and all the land of Susan and all that is on the side of Pharnak to the Red Sea and the river Tina. (9:2).
And for Asshur came forth the second Portion, all the land of Asshur and Nineveh and Shinar and to the border of India, and it ascends and skirts the river. (9:3).

And for Arpachshad came forth the third portion, all the land of the region of the Chaldees to the east of the Euphrates, bordering on the Red Sea, and all the waters of the desert close to the tongue of the sea which looks towards Egypt, all the land of Lebanon and Sanir and 'Amana to the border of the Euphrates. (9:4).

And for Aram there came forth the fourth portion, all the land of Mesopotamia between the Tigris and the Euphrates to the north of the Chaldees to the border of the mountains of Asshur and the land of 'Arara. (9:5).
And there came forth for Lud the fifth portion, the mountains of Asshur and all appertaining to them till it reaches the Great Sea, and till it reaches the east of Asshur his brother. (9:6).
And Japheth also divided the land of his inheritance amongst his sons. (9:7).

And the first portion came forth for Gomer to the east from the north side to the river Tina; and in the north there came forth for Magog all the inner portions of the north until it reaches to the sea of Me'at. (9:8).
And for Madai came forth as his portion that he should posses from the west of his two brothers to the islands, and to the coasts of the islands. (9:9).
And for Javan came forth the fourth portion every island and the islands which are towards the border of Lud. (9:10).

And for Tubal there came forth the fifth portion in the midst of the tongue which approaches towards the border of the portion of Lud to the second tongue, to the region beyond the second tongue to the third tongue. (9:11).
And for Meshech came forth the sixth portion, all the region beyond the third tongue till it approaches the east of Gadir. (9:12).

And for Tiras there came forth the seventh portion, four great islands in the midst of the sea, which reach to the portion of Ham [and the islands of Kamaturi came out by lot for the sons of Arpachshad as his inheritance]. (9:13).

And thus the sons of Noah divided to their sons in the presence of Noah their father, and he bound them all by an oath, imprecating a curse on every one that sought to seize the portion which had not fallen (to him) by his lot. (9:14).

And they all said, 'So be it; so be it ' for themselves and their sons for ever throughout their generations till the day of judgment, on which the Lord God shall judge them with a sword and with fire for all the unclean wickedness of their errors, with which they have filled the earth with transgression and uncleanness and fornication and sin. (9:15).
crossRefs: Genesis 10:1-32: The table of nations, the peoples descended from the three sons of Noah, which this chapter turns into a map with borders and lots.
Joshua 18:1-10: Joshua sends men to write the land in seven portions and casts lots for the tribes at Shiloh, the same procedure this chapter puts in Noah's mouth.
Numbers 34:1-12: The border of Canaan traced point by point from the salt sea to the great sea, the same kind of boundary list applied to one inheritance.
Ezekiel 38:1-6: Gog with Magog, Meshech, Tubal, Gomer and Cush named together as a coalition out of the far north, the same names this chapter places on the map.
Acts 17:26: God made every nation of men from one and set the boundaries of their dwelling places.

translationNotes.note: The four sons of Ham at Genesis 10:6 are also the names of lands. Cush is Nubia, up the Nile above the first cataract in what is now Sudan. Mizraim is the standard Hebrew name for Egypt. Put is placed on the coast west of Egypt in Libya. Canaan is the strip from Sidon down to Gaza that Israel later enters.

Asshur is both a son of Shem and the city on the Tigris that gave Assyria its name. Nineveh, on the Tigris opposite modern Mosul, became the Assyrian capital; it is the city Jonah is sent to at Jonah 3:1-4 and the city Nahum 3:1-7 sees fall. Genesis 10:11 says Asshur went out of Shinar and built it.

The chapter measures coastlines in tongues, meaning a strip of land or water that runs out like a tongue. Isaiah 11:15 uses the image of the tongue of the Egyptian sea and Joshua 15:2 calls the southern point of the Salt Sea a tongue. Here the tongues are the peninsulas along the northern side of the Mediterranean, counted first, second and third from the east.

An alah is a curse tied to a sworn oath: the man swearing calls down harm on himself if he breaks it. Numbers 5:19-22 shows the form, with the woman answering Amen, Amen to a sworn curse, and Deuteronomy 29:12-14 puts all Israel under an oath and its curse. At 9:14-15 Noah binds every grandson this way and they answer So be it, twice.

stories.keyTakeaway: Each of Noah's sons divides his portion among his own sons, from Cush and Mizraim and Put and Canaan under Ham to the seven sons of Japheth. Noah then binds them all by an oath that calls down a curse on anyone who seizes a portion his lot did not give him.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 10
summaryBullets: And in the third week of this jubilee the unclean demons began to lead astray the children of the sons of Noah, and to make to err and destroy them. (10:1).
And the sons of Noah came to Noah their father, and they told him concerning the demons which were leading astray and blinding and slaying his sons' sons. (10:2).

And he prayed before the Lord his God, and said: 'God of the spirits of all flesh, who have shown mercy to me And have saved me and my sons from the waters of the flood, And have not caused me to perish as You didst the sons of perdition; For Your grace has been great towards me, And great has been Your mercy to my soul; Let Your grace be lift up upon my sons, And let not wicked spirits rule over them Lest they should destroy them from the earth. But do You bless me and my sons, that we may increase and Multiply and replenish the earth. And You know how Your Watchers, the fathers of these spirits, acted in my day: and as for these spirits which are living, imprison them and hold them fast in the place of condemnation, and let them not bring destruction on the sons of your servant, my God; for these are malignant, and created in order to destroy. And let them not rule over the spirits of the living; for You alone can exercise dominion over them. And let them not have power over the sons of the righteous from henceforth and for evermore.' And the Lord our God told us to bind all. And the chief of the spirits, Mastêmâ, came and said: 'Lord, Creator, let some of them remain before me, and let them harken to my voice, and do all that I shall say to them; for if some of them are not left to me, I shall not be able to execute the power of my will on the sons of men; for these are for corruption and leading astray before my judgment, for great is the wickedness of the sons of men.' And He said: Let the tenth part of them remain before him, and let nine parts descend into the place of condemnation.' crossRefs: Genesis 11:1-9: The whole earth of one language, the fired brick and bitumen tower at Shinar, and the LORD scattering the builders and confusing their speech.
Genesis 9:28-29: Noah lives three hundred and fifty years after the flood and dies at nine hundred and fifty, the figure this chapter repeats and then converts into jubilees and weeks.
Job 1:6-12: The accuser presents himself among the sons of God and is granted a limited permission with a limit set on it, the same kind of arrangement Mastema asks for here.
Zechariah 3:1-2: The accuser stands at the right hand of the high priest to accuse him and is rebuked by the LORD.
Revelation 20:1-3: An angel binds the dragon, shuts him in the abyss and seals it so the nations are not deceived, the same kind of confinement described here.

translationNotes.note: The word is an ordinary Hebrew noun for hostility or enmity, from the root satam, to bear a grudge; Hosea 9:7-8 uses it of the hatred shown to a prophet. Jubilees turns it into a name, the chief of the spirits, who at 10:8-9 asks that some spirits be left under him and is granted a tenth. The office Scripture describes is ha-satan, the accuser, at Job 1:6 and Zechariah 3:1.

At 10:10-13 an angel teaches Noah to treat every disease with herbs of the earth, and Noah writes it all in a book and gives it to Shem. Genesis records nothing of the kind. Written healing knowledge was familiar in the period: Sirach 38:1-8 tells the reader to honour the physician and says the LORD created medicines out of the earth.

The mortar at Genesis 11:3 is chemar, natural asphalt, which seeps to the surface in Mesopotamia and around the Dead Sea and hardens in the air. Genesis 14:10 calls the vale of Siddim full of pits of it, and Exodus 2:3 has the basket for Moses daubed with it. At 10:20 the builders fire their bricks and cement them with asphalt taken from the fountains of Shinar.

At 10:21 the tower is given as 5433 cubits and 2 palms high, with one wall thirteen stades long and the other thirty. A cubit runs about eighteen inches, so that height is roughly 8150 feet or 2480 metres. A stade is about six hundred feet or 185 metres, making the walls about a mile and a half and three and a half miles. Genesis 11:4 gives no measurements at all.

Genesis 11:9 explains the name from balal, to confuse, because the LORD confused the language of the earth there. In Akkadian the city's own name Bab-ilim means gate of god. Babel and Babylon are one word in Hebrew, so the same name covers the tower's city and the empire that later burns Jerusalem, Jeremiah 52:12-14.

stories.keyTakeaway: Demons lead Noah's grandsons astray. At Noah's prayer nine parts of the spirits are shut away and a tenth is left under Mastema, while an angel teaches Noah the medicines. Noah dies at nine hundred and fifty. Men build the tower at Shinar, the languages are confounded, and a wind throws it down.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 11
summaryBullets: And in the thirty-fifth jubilee, in the third week, in the first year [1681 A.M.] thereof, Reu took to himself a wife, and her name was 'Ôrâ, the daughter of 'Ûr, the son of Kesed, and she bare him a son, and he called his name Sêrôh, in the seventh year of this week in this jubilee. [1687 A.M.] (11:1).

And the sons of Noah began to war on each other, to take captive and to slay each other, and to shed the blood of men on the earth, and to eat blood, and to build strong cities, and walls, and towers, and individuals (began) to exalt themselves above the nation, and to found the beginnings of kingdoms, and to go to war people against people, and nation against nation, and city against city, and all (began) to do evil, and to acquire arms, and to teach their sons war, and they began to capture cities, and to sell male and female slaves. (11:2).

And 'Ûr, the son of Kesed, built the city of 'Ara of the Chaldees, and called its name after his own name and the name of his father. And they made for themselves molten images, and they worshipped each the idol, the molten image which they had made for themselves, and they began to make graven images and unclean simulacra, and malignant spirits assisted and seduced (them) into committing transgression and uncleanness. (11:3).

And the prince Mastêmâ exerted himself to do all this, and he sent forth other spirits, those which were put under his hand, to do all manner of wrong and sin, and all manner of transgression, to corrupt and destroy, and to shed blood upon the earth. (11:4).
For this reason he called the name of Sêrôh, Serug, for every one turned to do all manner of sin and transgression. (11:5).

And he grew up, and dwelt in Ur of the Chaldees, near to the father of his wife's mother, and he worshipped idols, and he took to himself a wife in the thirty-sixth jubilee, in the fifth week, in the first year thereof, [1744 A.M.] and her name was Melka, the daughter of Kaber, the daughter of his father's brother. (11:6).

And she bare him Nahor, in the first year of this week, and he grew and dwelt in Ur of the Chaldees, and his father taught him the researches of the Chaldees to divine and augur, according to the signs of heaven. (11:7).
And in the thirty-seventh jubilee in the sixth week, in the first year thereof, [1800 A.M.] he took to himself a wife, and her name was 'Ijaska, the daughter of Nestag of the Chaldees. (11:8).
And she bare him Terah in the seventh year of this week. [1806 A.M.] (11:9).

And the prince Mastêmâ sent ravens and birds to devour the seed which was sown in the land, in order to destroy the land, and rob the children of men of their labours. Before they could plough in the seed, the ravens picked (it) from the surface of the ground. (11:10).
And for this reason he called his name Terah because the ravens and the birds reduced them to destitution and devoured their seed. (11:11).

And the years began to be barren, owing to the birds, and they devoured all the fruit of the trees from the trees: it was only with great effort that they could save a little of all the fruit of the earth in their days. (11:12).

And in this thirty-ninth jubilee, in the second week in the first year, [1870 A.M.] Terah took to himself a wife, and her name was 'Edna, the daughter of 'Abram, the daughter of his father's sister. And in the seventh year of this week [1876 A.M.] she bare him a son, and he called his name Abram, by the name of the father of his mother; (11:13).
for he had died before his daughter had conceived a son. (11:14).

And the child began to understand the errors of the earth that all went astray after graven images and after uncleanness, and his father taught him writing, and he was two weeks of years old, [1890 A.M.] and he separated himself from his father, that he might not worship idols with him. (11:15).

And he began to pray to the Creator of all things that He might save him from the errors of the children of men, and that his portion should not fall into error after uncleanness and vileness. (11:16).

And the seed time came for the sowing of seed upon the land, and they all went forth together to protect their seed against the ravens, and Abram went forth with those that went, and the child was a lad of fourteen years. (11:17).

And a cloud of ravens came to devour the seed, and Abram ran to meet them before they settled on the ground, and cried to them before they settled on the ground to devour the seed, and said, ' Descend not: return to the place from where you came,' and they proceeded to turn back. (11:18).
And he caused the clouds of ravens to turn back that day seventy times, and of all the ravens throughout all the land where Abram was there settled there not so much as one. (11:19).
And all who were with him throughout all the land saw him cry out, and all the ravens turn back, and his name became great in all the land of the Chaldees. (11:20).

And there came to him this year all those that wished to sow, and he went with them until the time of sowing ceased: and they sowed their land, and that year they brought enough grain home and eat and were satisfied. (11:21).

And in the first year of the fifth week [1891 A.M.] Abram taught those who made implements for oxen, the artificers in wood, and they made a vessel above the ground, facing the frame of the plough, in order to put the seed thereon, and the seed fell down therefrom upon the share of the plough, and was hidden in the earth, and they no longer feared the ravens. (11:22).

And after this manner they made (vessels) above the ground on all the frames of the ploughs, and they sowed and tilled all the land, according as Abram commanded them, and they no longer feared the birds. (11:23).
crossRefs: Genesis 11:18-26: The line from Reu to Serug to Nahor to Terah to Abram, the same names this chapter fills out with wives, cities and dated years.
Joshua 24:2-3: Your fathers dwelt beyond the River and served other gods, and the LORD took Abraham from beyond the River, the idolatry this chapter sets out in detail.
Isaiah 47:12-13: The stargazers and monthly prognosticators of Babylon are told to stand up and save themselves, the sky reading Nahor is taught here.
Deuteronomy 18:10-12: Divination and augury are named among the practices the LORD detests, the two arts this chapter says Nahor was taught by his father.
Jeremiah 10:2-5: Do not learn the way of the nations or be dismayed at the signs of heaven, for their idols are like a scarecrow in a cucumber field and cannot speak.

translationNotes.note: Genesis 11:28 places Abram's family there and Genesis 15:7 has God say He brought Abram out of it. Ur was a Sumerian city on the lower Euphrates in what is now southern Iraq, and the great stepped tower at its centre was raised to Nanna, the moon god the city belonged to. At 11:3 this book says a man named Ur son of Kesed built the city and called it after himself.

The Kasdim were a people of southern Babylonia who later supplied Babylon with its kings. The same word came to double as the name for the men who read the sky, which is how Daniel 2:2 uses it, listing Chaldeans beside magicians and enchanters. This chapter uses the family sense at 11:3 and the sky-reading sense at 11:7.

Two named practices, not one vague one. Qesem is divination, deciding a question by lot, arrows or the liver of a sacrificed animal. Nachash is augury, reading omens off events. Deuteronomy 18:10-12 forbids both by name and calls those who do them detestable to the LORD. At 11:7 Nahor's father teaches him these arts by the signs of heaven, which Genesis does not report.

At 11:10-12 Mastema sends ravens that lift the seed off the ground before the plough can cover it, and at 11:11 the book explains Terah's name from those birds. Genesis 11:24-26 gives Terah only his father, his years and his three sons. Losing seed to birds was a real hazard of broadcast sowing, where grain is thrown by hand and ploughed under afterwards.

At 11:22-23 Abram has the woodworkers fit a vessel above the plough frame that drops seed onto the share so it goes straight under the soil. That is a seed drill. Ploughs of exactly that design, with a funnel and tube fixed to the beam, were used in Mesopotamia and appear on Babylonian seals and boundary stones. Genesis records nothing of it.

stories.keyTakeaway: Men make war, take slaves and set up molten images while Mastema sends out spirits to help them. Nahor is taught to divine by the signs of heaven, and ravens are sent to devour the sown seed. Abram at fourteen turns the ravens back and fits a seed box to the plough.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 12
summaryBullets: And it came to pass in the sixth week, in the seventh year thereof, [1904 A.M.] that Abram said to Terah his father, saying, 'Father!' (12:1).

And he said, 'Behold, here am I, my son.' And he said, 'What help and profit have we from those idols which you do worship, And before which you do bow yourself? For there is no spirit in them, For they are dumb forms, and a misleading of the heart. Worship them not: Worship the God of heaven, Who causes the rain and the dew to descend on the earth And does everything upon the earth, And has created everything by His word, And all life is from before His face. Why do you worship things that have no spirit in them? For they are the work of (men's) hands, And on your shoulders do you bear them, And you have no help from them, But they are a great cause of shame to those who make them, And a misleading of the heart to those who worship them: Worship them not.' And his father said to him, I also know it, my son, but what shall I do with a people who have made me to serve before them? And if I tell them the truth, they will slay me; for their soul cleaves to them to worship them and honour them. Keep silent, my son, lest they slay you.' And these words he spoke to his two brothers, and they were angry with him and he kept silent. And in the fortieth jubilee, in the second week, in the seventh year thereof, [1925 A.M.] Abram took to himself a wife, and her name was Sarai, the daughter of his father, and she became his wife. And Haran, his brother, took to himself a wife in the third year of the third week, [1928 A.M.] and she bare him a son in the seventh year of this week, [1932 A.M.] and he called his name Lot. And Nahor, his brother, took to himself a wife. And in the sixtieth year of the life of Abram, that is, in the fourth week, in the fourth year thereof, [1936 A.M.] Abram arose by night, and burned the house of the idols, and he burned all that was in the house and no man knew it. And they arose in the night and sought to save their gods from the midst of the fire. And Haran hasted to save them, but the fire flamed over him, and he was burnt in the fire, and he died in Ur of the Chaldees before Terah his father, and they buried him in Ur of the Chaldees. And Terah went forth from Ur of the Chaldees, he and his sons, to go into the land of Lebanon and into the land of Canaan, and he dwelt in the land of Haran, and Abram dwelt with Terah his father in Haran two weeks of years. And in the sixth week, in the fifth year thereof, [1951 A.M.] Abram sat up throughout the night on the new moon of the seventh month to observe the stars from the evening to the morning, in order to see what would be the character of the year with regard to the rains, and he was alone as he sat and observed. And a word came into his heart and he said: All the signs of the stars, and the signs of the moon and of the sun are all in the hand of the Lord. Why do I search (them) out? If He desires, He causes it to rain, morning and evening; And if He desires, He withholds it, And all things are in his hand.' And he prayed that night and said, 'My God, God Most High, You alone are my God, And You and Your dominion have I chosen. And You have created all things, And all things that are the work of your hands. Deliver me from the hands of evil spirits who have dominion over the thoughts of men's hearts, And let them not lead me astray from You, my God. And stablish You me and my seed for ever That we go not astray from henceforth and for evermore.' And he said, 'Shall I return to Ur of the Chaldees who seek my face that I may return to them, am I to remain here in this place? The right path before You prosper it in the hands of Your servant that he may fulfil (it) and that I may not walk in the deceitfulness of my heart, O my God.' And he made an end of speaking and praying, and behold the word of the Lord was sent to him through me, saying: 'Get you up from your country, and from your kindred and from the house of your father to a land which I will show you, and I shall make you a great and numerous nation. And I will bless you And I will make your name great, And you will be blessed in the earth, And in You shall all families of the earth be blessed, And I will bless them that bless you, And curse them that curse you. And I will be a God to you and your son, and to your son's son, and to all your seed: fear not, from henceforth and to all generations of the earth I am your God.' And the Lord God said: 'Open his mouth and his ears, that he may hear and speak with his mouth, with the language which has been revealed'; for it had ceased from the mouths of all the children of men from the day of the overthrow (of Babel). And I opened his mouth, and his ears and his lips, and I began to speak with him in Hebrew in the tongue of the creation. And he took the books of his fathers, and these were written in Hebrew, and he transcribed them, and he began from henceforth to study them, and I made known to him that which he could not (understand), and he studied them during the six rainy months. And it came to pass in the seventh year of the sixth week [1953 A.M.] that he spoke to his father and informed him, that he would leave Haran to go into the land of Canaan to see it and return to him. And Terah his father said to him; Go in peace: May the eternal God make your path straight. And the Lord [(be) with you, and] protect you from all evil, And grant to you grace, mercy and favour before those who see you, And may none of the children of men have power over you to harm you; Go in peace. And if you see a land pleasant to your eyes to dwell in, then arise and take me to you and take Lot with you, the son of Haran your brother as yours own son: the Lord be with you. And Nahor your brother leave with me till you returnest in peace, and we go with you all together.' (12:2).

Worship them not: Worship the God of heaven, Who causes the rain and the dew to descend on the earth And does everything upon the earth, And has created everything by His word, And all life is from before His face. And I will bless you And I will make your name great, And you will be blessed in the earth, And in You shall all families of the earth be blessed, And I will bless them that bless you, And curse them that curse you. And I will be a God to you and your son, and to your son's son, and to all your seed: fear not, from henceforth and to all generations of the earth I am your God.' And the Lord God said: 'Open his mouth and his ears, that he may hear and speak with his mouth, with the language which has been revealed'; for it had ceased from the mouths of all the children of men from the day of the overthrow (of Babel). And I opened his mouth, and his ears and his lips, and I began to speak with him in Hebrew in the tongue of the creation. And he took the books of his fathers, and these were written in Hebrew, and he transcribed them, and he began from henceforth to study them, and I made known to him that which he could not (understand), and he studied them during the six rainy months. And it came to pass in the seventh year of the sixth week [1953 A.M.] that he spoke to his father and informed him, that he would leave Haran to go into the land of Canaan to see it and return to him. And Terah his father said to him; Go in peace: May the eternal God make your path straight. And the Lord [(be) with you, and] protect you from all evil, And grant to you grace, mercy and favour before those who see you, And may none of the children of men have power over you to harm you; Go in peace. And if you see a land pleasant to your eyes to dwell in, then arise and take me to you and take Lot with you, the son of Haran your brother as yours own son: the Lord be with you. And Nahor your brother leave with me till you returnest in peace, and we go with you all together.' (12:23).
And I will be a God to you and your son, and to your son's son, and to all your seed: fear not, from henceforth and to all generations of the earth I am your God.' (12:24).

And the Lord God said: 'Open his mouth and his ears, that he may hear and speak with his mouth, with the language which has been revealed'; for it had ceased from the mouths of all the children of men from the day of the overthrow (of Babel). (12:25).
And I opened his mouth, and his ears and his lips, and I began to speak with him in Hebrew in the tongue of the creation. (12:26).

And he took the books of his fathers, and these were written in Hebrew, and he transcribed them, and he began from henceforth to study them, and I made known to him that which he could not (understand), and he studied them during the six rainy months. (12:27).

And it came to pass in the seventh year of the sixth week [1953 A.M.] that he spoke to his father and informed him, that he would leave Haran to go into the land of Canaan to see it and return to him. (12:28).

And Terah his father said to him; Go in peace: May the eternal God make your path straight. And the Lord [(be) with you, and] protect you from all evil, And grant to you grace, mercy and favour before those who see you, And may none of the children of men have power over you to harm you; Go in peace. And if you see a land pleasant to your eyes to dwell in, then arise and take me to you and take Lot with you, the son of Haran your brother as yours own son: the Lord be with you. And Nahor your brother leave with me till you returnest in peace, and we go with you all together.' (12:29).
And if you see a land pleasant to your eyes to dwell in, then arise and take me to you and take Lot with you, the son of Haran your brother as yours own son: the Lord be with you. (12:30).
And Nahor your brother leave with me till you returnest in peace, and we go with you all together.' (12:31).
crossRefs: Genesis 12:1-3: Get out of your country and from your kindred to a land I will show you, with the blessing and the cursing, the call this chapter places at the end of a night of prayer.
Genesis 11:27-32: Haran dies before his father Terah in Ur of the Chaldees, and Terah takes the family as far as Haran and settles there.
Isaiah 44:9-20: A man cuts a tree, burns half of it to warm himself and bake bread, and bows down to what is left, the argument against idols this chapter puts in Abram's mouth.
Psalm 115:4-8: Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men's hands, with mouths that do not speak and eyes that do not see, the same charge Abram brings to his father.
Joshua 24:14-15: Put away the gods your fathers served beyond the River and choose this day whom you will serve, the choice this chapter has Abram make and Terah refuse.

translationNotes.note: Elilim is one Hebrew word for idols and it sounds like both el, god, and a word for worthless, so the name itself is an insult. Genesis 11:28 says only that Haran died before his father in Ur. At 12:12-14 Jubilees says Abram set the idol house alight by night and that Haran died running in to pull the images out.

At 12:16-18 Abram sits out the whole night of the new moon of the seventh month watching the stars to work out what the coming year will bring in rain, then concludes that sun, moon and stars are all in the hand of the Lord and stops. The rains in that country fall between roughly October and April, so a reading taken at the turn of the seventh month is a forecast of the whole growing season.

At 12:25-26 the angel opens Abram's mouth and ears so that he can speak Hebrew, which the book says had gone out of human mouths since Babel. He then copies out his fathers' books, written in Hebrew, and studies them through the six rainy months. Genesis 11:1-9 records the confusion of language and says nothing about any tongue being given back to anyone.

The title Abram uses in his prayer at 12:19. Genesis 14:18-20 has Melchizedek bless Abram by El Elyon, possessor of heaven and earth, and Abram then answers the king of Sodom by the same name. The word elyon simply means highest, so the title sets this God over every other claimant by definition.

A real city on the Balikh river in what is now southern Turkey, sitting on the caravan road between Mesopotamia and Syria, and like Ur a centre of moon worship. Genesis 11:31-32 has Terah settle and die there. At 12:15 Abram stays with him two weeks of years, which on this book's reckoning is fourteen years.

stories.keyTakeaway: Abram tells Terah the idols are dumb forms with no spirit in them, and Terah agrees but fears the people. Abram burns the house of idols by night and Haran dies trying to save them. Watching the stars for rain, Abram turns from the signs to the God who makes them, and the call comes.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 13
summaryBullets: And Abram journeyed from Haran, and he took Sarai, his wife, and Lot, his brother Haran's son, to the land of Canaan, and he came into Asshur, and proceeded to Shechem, and dwelt near a lofty oak. (13:1).
And he saw, and, behold, the land was very pleasant from the entering of Hamath to the lofty oak. (13:2).
And the Lord said to him: 'To you and to your seed will I give this land.' (13:3).
And he built an altar there, and he offered thereon a burnt sacrifice to the Lord, who had appeared to him. (13:4).
And he removed from from there to the mountain . . . Bethel on the west and Ai on the east, and pitched his tent there. (13:5).

And he saw and behold, the land was very wide and good, and everything grew thereon -vines and figs and pomegranates, oaks and ilexes, and terebinths and oil trees, and cedars and cypresses and date trees, and all trees of the field, and there was water on the mountains. (13:6).
And he blessed the Lord who had led him out of Ur of the Chaldees, and had brought him to this land. (13:7).

And it came to pass in the first year, in the seventh week, on the new moon of the first month, 1954 A.M.] that he built an altar on this mountain, and called on the name of the Lord: 'You, the eternal God, are my God.' (13:8).
And he offered on the altar a burnt sacrifice to the Lord that He should be with him and not forsake him all the days of his life. (13:9).

And he removed from from there and went towards the south, and he came to Hebron and Hebron was built at that time, and he dwelt there two years, and he went (from there) into the land of the south, to Bealoth, and there was a famine in the land. (13:10).
And Abram went into Egypt in the third year of the week, and he dwelt in Egypt five years before his wife was torn away from him. (13:11).
Now Tanais in Egypt was at that time built- seven years after Hebron. (13:12).
And it came to pass when Pharaoh seized Sarai, the wife of Abram that the Lord plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, Abram's wife. (13:13).

And Abram was very glorious by reason of possessions in sheep, and cattle, and asses, and horses, and camels, and menservants, and maidservants, and in silver and gold exceedingly. And Lot also his brother's son, was wealthy. (13:14).

And Pharaoh gave back Sarai, the wife of Abram, and he sent him out of the land of Egypt, and he journeyed to the place where he had pitched his tent at the beginning, to the place of the altar, with Ai on the east, and Bethel on the west, and he blessed the Lord his God who had brought him back in peace. (13:15).

And it came to pass in the forty-first jubilee in the third year of the first week, [1963 A.M.] that he returned to this place and offered thereon a burnt sacrifice, and called on the name of the Lord, and said: 'You, the most high God, are my God for ever and ever.' (13:16).
And in the fourth year of this week [1964 A.M.] Lot parted from him, and Lot dwelt in Sodom, and the men of Sodom were sinners exceedingly. (13:17).
And it grieved him in his heart that his brother's son had parted from him; for he had no children. (13:18).

In that year when Lot was taken captive, the Lord said to Abram, after that Lot had parted from him, in the fourth year of this week: 'Lift up yours eyes from the place where you are dwelling, northward and southward, and westward and eastward. (13:19).

For all the land which you see I will give to you and to your seed for ever, and I will make your seed as the sand of the sea: though a man may number the dust of the earth, yet your seed shall not be numbered. (13:20).
Arise, walk (through the land) in the length of it and the breadth of it, and see it all; for to your seed will I give it.' And Abram went to Hebron, and dwelt there. (13:21).

And in this year came Chedorlaomer, king of Elam, and Amraphel, king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Sellasar, and Tergal, king of nations, and slew the king of Gomorrah, and the king of Sodom fled, and many fell through wounds in the vale of Siddim, by the Salt Sea. (13:22).
And they took captive Sodom and Adam and Zeboim, and they took captive Lot also, the son of Abram's brother, and all his possessions, and they went to Dan. (13:23).
And one who had escaped came and told Abram that his brother's son had been taken captive and (Abram) armed his household servants . . . (13:24).

. . . . for Abram, and for his seed, a tenth of the first fruits to the Lord, and the Lord ordained it as an ordinance for ever that they should give it to the priests who served before Him, that they should possess it for ever. (13:25).

And to this law there is no limit of days; for He has ordained it for the generations for ever that they should give to the Lord the tenth of everything, of the seed and of the wine and of the oil and of the cattle and of the sheep. (13:26).
And He gave (it) to His priests to eat and to drink with joy before Him. (13:27).
And the king of Sodom came to him and bowed himself before him, and said: 'Our Lord Abram, give to us the souls which you have rescued, but let the booty be yours.' (13:28).

And Abram said to him: 'I lift up my hands to the Most High God, that from a thread to a shoe-latchet I shall not take aught that is yours lest you should say, I have made Abram rich; save only what the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men who went with me -Aner, Eschol, and Mamre. These shall take their portion.' (13:29).
crossRefs: Genesis 12:10-20: Abram goes down into Egypt because of the famine, Sarai is taken into Pharaoh's house, and the LORD strikes Pharaoh and his house with great plagues on her account.
Genesis 13:14-18: After Lot parts from him Abram is told to lift up his eyes north, south, east and west and walk the length and breadth of the land, then he settles by the oaks of Mamre at Hebron.
Genesis 14:1-16: Chedorlaomer and the kings with him strike the cities of the plain, carry Lot off, and Abram arms his trained servants and pursues them as far as Dan.
Hebrews 7:1-4: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of the Most High God, meets Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings, and Abraham gives him a tenth of the spoils.
Numbers 18:21-24: The tithe in Israel is given to the Levites in return for their service, the permanent arrangement this chapter traces back to Abram.

translationNotes.note: Ma'aser means literally a tenth. Genesis 14:20 has Abram give Melchizedek a tenth of the spoil once, on one day. At 13:25-27 Jubilees turns that single act into a permanent ordinance binding his seed, on seed and wine and oil and cattle and sheep, given to the priests to eat before the LORD. Numbers 18:21-24 assigns Israel's tithe to the Levites.

Shechem sits in the pass between Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim in the hill country, about thirty miles north of Jerusalem, and whoever holds it holds the road through. Genesis 12:6 has Abram stop at the oak of Moreh there, his first stop in the land. Joshua 24:1 has all Israel gather at the same place generations later to renew the covenant.

Tanais is the Greek name for Zoan, an Egyptian city in the eastern Delta. Numbers 13:22 notes that Hebron was built seven years before Zoan, and at 13:12 this book states the same seven-year gap from the other end. Psalm 78:12 sets the wonders God did in Egypt in the field of Zoan.

translationNotes.term: The vale of Siddim by the Salt Sea
translationNotes.note: The Salt Sea is the Dead Sea, the lowest exposed ground on earth, its surface more than 1,300 feet below sea level and its water too salty for fish. Genesis 14:3 identifies the vale of Siddim with it, and Genesis 14:10 says the vale was full of bitumen pits, which is where the fleeing kings fell.

translationNotes.term: From a thread to a shoe latchet
translationNotes.note: A shoe latchet is the leather thong that ties a sandal on, and a loose thread is the least valuable thing in a tent. At 13:29 Abram swears he will take nothing of the king of Sodom's between those two limits, in the same words as Genesis 14:23, so that no man can ever say he made Abram rich.

stories.keyTakeaway: Abram goes down through Shechem to Bethel and Hebron, then into Egypt, where Sarai is taken from him and Pharaoh is struck with plagues. He comes back rich, Lot settles in Sodom, and after the four kings carry Lot off the chapter turns Abram's tenth into a standing law for the priests.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 14
summaryBullets: After these things, in the fourth year of this week, on the new moon of the third month, the word of the Lord came to Abram in a dream, saying: 'Fear not, Abram; I am your defender, and your reward will be exceeding great.' (14:1).

And he said: 'Lord, Lord, what will you give me, seeing I go from here childless, and the son of Maseq, the son of my handmaid, is the Dammasek Eliezer: he will be my heir, and to me you have given no seed.' (14:2).
And he said to him: 'This (man) will not be your heir, but one that will come out of yours own bowels; he will be yours heir.' (14:3).
And He brought him forth abroad, and said to him: 'Look toward heaven and number the stars if you are able to number them.' (14:4).
And he looked toward heaven, and beheld the stars. And He said to him: 'So shall your seed be.' (14:5).
And he believed in the Lord, and it was counted to him for righteousness. (14:6).

And He said to him: 'I am the Lord that brought you out of Ur of the Chaldees, to give you the land of the Canaanites to possess it for ever; and I will be God to you and to your seed after you.' (14:7).
And he said: 'Lord, Lord, whereby shall I know that I shall inherit (it)?' (14:8).
And He said to him: 'Take Me an heifer of three years, and a goat of three years, and a sheep of three years, and a turtle-dove, and a pigeon.' (14:9).
And he took all these in the middle of the month and he dwelt at the oak of Mamre, which is near Hebron. (14:10).

And he built there an altar, and sacrificed all these; and he poured their blood upon the altar, and divided them in the midst, and laid them over against each other; but the birds divided he not. (14:11).
And birds came down upon the pieces, and Abram drove them away, and did not suffer the birds to touch them. (14:12).

And it came to pass, when the sun had set, that an ecstasy fell upon Abram, and lo ! an horror of great darkness fell upon him, and it was said to Abram: 'Know of a surety that your seed shall be a stranger in a land (that is) not theirs, and they shall bring them into bondage, and afflict them four hundred years. (14:13).
And the nation also to whom they will be in bondage will I judge, and after that they shall come forth from there with much substance. (14:14).
And you will go to your fathers in peace, and be buried in a good old age. (14:15).
But in the fourth generation they shall return here; for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full.' (14:16).
And he awoke from his sleep, and he arose, and the sun had set; and there was a flame, and behold ! a furnace was smoking, and a flame of fire passed between the pieces. (14:17).

And on that day the Lord made a covenant with Abram, saying: 'To your seed will I give this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates, the Kenites, the Kenizzites, the Kadmonites, the Perizzites, and the Rephaim, the Phakorites, and the Hivites, and the Amorites, and the Canaanites, and the Girgashites, and the Jebusites. (14:18).
And the day passed, and Abram offered the pieces, and the birds, and their fruit offerings, and their drink offerings, and the fire devoured them. (14:19).
And on that day we made a covenant with Abram, according as we had covenanted with Noah in this month; and Abram renewed the festival and ordinance for himself for ever. (14:20).
And Abram rejoiced, and made all these things known to Sarai his wife; and he believed that he would have seed, but she did not bear. (14:21).
And Sarai advised her husband Abram, and said to him: 'Go in to Hagar, my Egyptian maid: it may be that I shall build up seed to you by her.' (14:22).
And Abram harkened to the voice of Sarai his wife, and said to her, 'Do (so).' And Sarai took Hagar, her maid, the Egyptian, and gave her to Abram, her husband, to be his wife. (14:23).

And he went in to her, and she conceived and bare him a son, and he called his name Ishmael, in the fifth year of this week [1965 A.M.]; and this was the eighty-sixth year in the life of Abram. (14:24).
crossRefs: Genesis 15:1-21: The promise of an heir, the counting of the stars, the divided animals, the horror of great darkness, the four hundred years and the smoking furnace passing between the pieces.
Jeremiah 34:18-19: The men who cut a calf in two and walked between its parts are held to what they swore, which is what passing between divided animals meant.
Romans 4:3-5: Abraham believed God and it was counted to him as righteousness, the sentence this chapter records at 14:6.
Exodus 12:40-41: The sojourning of the children of Israel was four hundred and thirty years, and they went out on the selfsame day it ended.
Galatians 3:16-18: The promise was spoken to Abraham and to his seed four hundred and thirty years before the law, and the law that came later does not cancel it.

translationNotes.note: Hebrew does not make a covenant, it cuts one, and this chapter shows why. The animals are halved and laid opposite each other and the parties walk between the pieces. Jeremiah 34:18-19 describes the identical ceremony with a calf and treats the walk as putting yourself under the fate of the animal if you break the terms. At 14:17 only the flame passes through, so only one side is bound.

Abram's steward, called of Damascus at Genesis 15:2. Adopting a servant as heir when there was no son is attested in Mesopotamian family contracts, and is exactly the arrangement Abram assumes at 14:2 and God refuses at 14:3. The book adds that he was the son of Maseq, a handmaid.

At 14:13 Abram is told his seed will be strangers in a land not theirs and afflicted four hundred years, the figure at Genesis 15:13. Exodus 12:40-41 gives the sojourning as four hundred and thirty years to the day. Stephen repeats the four hundred at Acts 7:6.

Three years old is a full-grown beast at its prime and its highest value, not a calf. The list at 14:9 matches Genesis 15:9 item for item: heifer, goat and ram each of three years, with a turtledove and a young pigeon. The two birds are what the law later allows a man to bring who cannot afford a lamb, Leviticus 5:7.

The Amorites were one people of Canaan, and the name is also used, as here, for the population of the land as a whole. At 14:16 the return is held back to the fourth generation because their iniquity is not yet full, the reason given at Genesis 15:16. Leviticus 18:24-28 says the land itself vomits out its inhabitants for those practices.

stories.keyTakeaway: The word comes to Abram in a dream: his heir will come out of his own body and his seed will be as the stars. He cuts the animals in half and drives off the birds, and in a great darkness hears that his seed will be strangers four hundred years. A flame passes between the pieces.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 15
summaryBullets: And in the fifth year of the fourth week of this jubilee, [1979 A.M.] in the third month, in the middle of the month, Abram celebrated the feast of the first-fruits of the grain harvest. (15:1).

And he offered new offerings on the altar, the first-fruits of the produce, to the Lord, an heifer and a goat and a sheep on the altar as a burnt sacrifice to the Lord; their fruit offerings and their drink offerings he offered upon the altar with frankincense. (15:2).
And the Lord appeared to Abram, and said to him: 'I am God Almighty; approve yourself before me and be you perfect. (15:3).
And I will make My covenant between Me and you, and I will multiply you exceedingly.' (15:4).

And Abram fell on his face, and God talked with him, and said: 'Behold my ordinance is with you, And you will be the father of many nations. Neither shall your name any more be called Abram, But your name from henceforth, even for ever, shall be Abraham. For the father of many nations have I made you. And I will make you very great, And I will make you into nations, And kings shall come forth from you. And I shall establish My covenant between Me and you, and your seed after you, throughout their generations, for an eternal covenant, so that I may be a God to you, and to your seed after you. <And I will give to you and to your seed after you> the land where you have been a sojourner, the land of Canaan, that you mayst possess it for ever, and I will be their God.' And the Lord said to Abraham: 'And as for you, do you keep my covenant, you and your seed after you: and circumcise you every male among you, and circumcise your foreskins, and it shall be a token of an eternal covenant between Me and you. And the child on the eighth day you will circumcise, every male throughout your generations, him that is born in the house, or whom you have bought with money from any stranger, whom you have acquired who is not of your seed. He that is born in your house shall surely be circumcised, and those whom you have bought with money shall be circumcised, and My covenant shall be in your flesh for an eternal ordinance. And the uncircumcised male who is not circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin on the eighth day, that soul shall be cut off from his people, for he has broken My covenant.' And God said to Abraham: 'As for Sarai your wife, her name shall no more be called Sarai, but Sarah shall be her name. And I will bless her, and give you a son by her, and I will bless him, and he shall become a nation, and kings of nations shall proceed from him.' And Abraham fell on his face, and rejoiced, and said in his heart: 'Shall a son be born to him that is a hundred years old, and shall Sarah, who is ninety years old, bring forth?' And Abraham said to God: 'O that Ishmael might live before you!' And God said: 'Yea, and Sarah also shall bear you a son, and you will call his name Isaac, and I will establish My covenant with him, an everlasting covenant, and for his seed after him. And as for Ishmael also have I heard you, and behold I will bless him, and make him great, and multiply him exceedingly, and he shall beget twelve princes, and I will make him a great nation. But My covenant will I establish with Isaac, whom Sarah shall bear to you, in these days, in the next year.' And He left off speaking with him, and God went up from Abraham. And Abraham did according as God had said to him, and he took Ishmael his son, and all that were born in his house, and whom he had bought with his money, every male in his house, and circumcised the flesh of their foreskin. And on the selfsame day was Abraham circumcised, and all the men of his house, <and those born in the house>, and all those, whom he had bought with money from the children of the stranger, were circumcised with him. This law is for all the generations for ever, and there is no circumcision of the days, and no omission of one day out of the eight days; for it is an eternal ordinance, ordained and written on the heavenly tablets. And every one that is born, the flesh of whose foreskin is not circumcised on the eighth day, belongs not to the children of the covenant which the Lord made with Abraham, but to the children of destruction; nor is there, moreover, any sign on him that he is the Lord's, but (he is destined) to be destroyed and slain from the earth, and to be rooted out of the earth, for he has broken the covenant of the Lord our God. For all the angels of the presence and all the angels of sanctification have been so created from the day of their creation, and before the angels of the presence and the angels of sanctification He has sanctified Israel, that they should be with Him and with His holy angels. And do you command the children of Israel and let them observe the sign of this covenant for their generations as an eternal ordinance, and they will not be rooted out of the land. For the command is ordained for a covenant, that they should observe it for ever among all the children of Israel. For Ishmael and his sons and his brothers and Esau, the Lord did not cause to approach Him, and he chose them not because they are the children of Abraham, because He knew them, but He chose Israel to be His people. And He sanctified it, and gathered it from amongst all the children of men; for there are many nations and many peoples, and all are His, and over all has He placed spirits in authority to lead them astray from Him. But over Israel He did not appoint any angel or spirit, for He alone is their ruler, and He will preserve them and require them at the hand of His angels and His spirits, and at the hand of all His powers in order that He may preserve them and bless them, and that they may be His and He may be theirs from henceforth for ever. And now I announce to you that the children of Israel will not keep true to this ordinance, and they will not circumcise their sons according to all this law; for in the flesh of their circumcision they will omit this circumcision of their sons, and all of them, sons of Beliar, will leave their sons uncircumcised as they were born. And there will be great wrath from the Lord against the children of Israel. because they have forsaken His covenant and turned aside from His word, and provoked and blasphemed, inasmuch as they do not observe the ordinance of this law; for they have treated their members like the Gentiles, so that they may be removed and rooted out of the land. And there will no more be pardon or forgiveness to them [so that there should be forgiveness and pardon] for all the sin of this eternal error. (15:5).

'Behold my ordinance is with you, And you will be the father of many nations. Neither shall your name any more be called Abram, But your name from henceforth, even for ever, shall be Abraham. For the father of many nations have I made you. And I will make you very great, And I will make you into nations, And kings shall come forth from you. And I shall establish My covenant between Me and you, and your seed after you, throughout their generations, for an eternal covenant, so that I may be a God to you, and to your seed after you. <And I will give to you and to your seed after you> the land where you have been a sojourner, the land of Canaan, that you mayst possess it for ever, and I will be their God.' And the Lord said to Abraham: 'And as for you, do you keep my covenant, you and your seed after you: and circumcise you every male among you, and circumcise your foreskins, and it shall be a token of an eternal covenant between Me and you. And the child on the eighth day you will circumcise, every male throughout your generations, him that is born in the house, or whom you have bought with money from any stranger, whom you have acquired who is not of your seed. He that is born in your house shall surely be circumcised, and those whom you have bought with money shall be circumcised, and My covenant shall be in your flesh for an eternal ordinance. And the uncircumcised male who is not circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin on the eighth day, that soul shall be cut off from his people, for he has broken My covenant.' And God said to Abraham: 'As for Sarai your wife, her name shall no more be called Sarai, but Sarah shall be her name. And I will bless her, and give you a son by her, and I will bless him, and he shall become a nation, and kings of nations shall proceed from him.' And Abraham fell on his face, and rejoiced, and said in his heart: 'Shall a son be born to him that is a hundred years old, and shall Sarah, who is ninety years old, bring forth?'
