crossRefs: Genesis 17:1-27: God Almighty appears, both names are changed, circumcision on the eighth day is commanded, Isaac is promised, and Abraham circumcises his whole household the same day.
Leviticus 12:3: On the eighth day the flesh of the child's foreskin shall be circumcised, the timing this chapter refuses to let anyone move by a single day.
Deuteronomy 32:8-9: The Most High gave the nations their inheritance and fixed their bounds, and the LORD's own portion is His people, the arrangement this chapter states at length.
1 Maccabees 1:60-61: Women who had their sons circumcised were put to death with the infants hung about their necks, which is what abandoning this sign came to cost.
Acts 7:8: God gave Abraham the covenant of circumcision, and so Abraham circumcised Isaac on the eighth day.

translationNotes.note: The name God gives Himself at 15:3, as at Genesis 17:1. Exodus 6:3 says God appeared to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob as El Shaddai but was not known to them by the name YHWH. English gets Almighty from the Greek and Latin translations; the root behind Shaddai cannot be established with certainty, so the traditional rendering is as far as the evidence goes.

The cutting away of the foreskin, commanded at Genesis 17:12 and again at Leviticus 12:3 on the eighth day of life. At 15:25-26 Jubilees hardens it: no delay and no leaving out one day out of the eight, and a boy left uncircumcised belongs to the children of destruction. Genesis 17:14 states the penalty as being cut off from his people.

Avram means exalted father. Genesis 17:5 gives the new name with its reason attached, father of a multitude of nations, which the Hebrew hears in the added syllable. Sarai becomes Sarah at Genesis 17:15, both forms meaning princess. A change of name marks a change of standing, as when Jacob becomes Israel at Genesis 32:28.

A nasi is a chief or the head of a tribe, not a king with a throne. At 15:20 Ishmael is promised twelve of them, as at Genesis 17:20, and Genesis 25:13-16 names all twelve and calls them twelve princes according to their nations, by their villages and their encampments.

At 15:31-32 the book says God placed spirits in authority over every nation to lead them astray, but appointed no angel or spirit over Israel and rules them Himself. Deuteronomy 32:8-9 says the Most High fixed the boundaries of the peoples and that the LORD's portion is His people. Daniel 10:13-20 speaks of a prince of the kingdom of Persia and a prince of Greece who withstand an angel.

stories.keyTakeaway: God appears as God Almighty, changes Abram's name to Abraham and Sarai's to Sarah, and gives circumcision on the eighth day as the sign of the covenant, with no delay allowed. Isaac is promised for the next year, and the chapter says spirits are set over the nations while God rules Israel Himself.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 16
summaryBullets: And on the new moon of the fourth month we appeared to Abraham, at the oak of Mamre, and we talked with him, and we announced to him that a son would be given to him by Sarah his wife. (16:1).
And Sarah laughed, for she heard that we had spoken these words with Abraham, and we admonished her, and she became afraid, and denied that she had laughed on account of the words. (16:2).
And we told her the name of her son, as his name is ordained and written in the heavenly tablets (i.e.) Isaac, (16:3).
And (that) when we returned to her at a set time, she would have conceived a son. (16:4).

And in this month the Lord executed his judgments on Sodom, and Gomorrah, and Zeboim, and all the region of the Jordan, and He burned them with fire and brimstone, and destroyed them until this day, even as [lo] I have declared to you all their works, that they are wicked and sinners exceedingly, and that they defile themselves and commit fornication in their flesh, and work uncleanness on the earth. (16:5).
And, in like manner, God will execute judgment on the places where they have done according to the uncleanness of the Sodomites, like to the judgment of Sodom. (16:6).
But Lot we saved; for God remembered Abraham, and sent him out from the midst of the overthrow. (16:7).
And he and his daughters committed sin upon the earth, such as had not been on the earth since the days of Adam till his time; for the man lay with his daughters. (16:8).

And, behold, it was commanded and engraven concerning all his seed, on the heavenly tablets, to remove them and root them out, and to execute judgment upon them like the judgment of Sodom, and to leave no seed of the man on earth on the day of condemnation. (16:9).
And in this month Abraham moved from Hebron, and departed and dwelt between Kadesh and Shur in the mountains of Gerar. (16:10).
And in the middle of the fifth month he moved from from there, and dwelt at the Well of the Oath. (16:11).
And in the middle of the sixth month the Lord visited Sarah and did to her as He had spoken and she conceived. (16:12).

And she bare a son in the third month, and in the middle of the month, at the time of which the Lord had spoken to Abraham, on the festival of the first fruits of the harvest, Isaac was born. (16:13).
And Abraham circumcised his son on the eighth day: he was the first that was circumcised according to the covenant which is ordained for ever. (16:14).

And in the sixth year of the fourth week we came to Abraham, to the Well of the Oath, and we appeared to him [as we had told Sarah that we should return to her, and she would have conceived a son. (16:15).

And we returned in the seventh month, and found Sarah with child before us] and we blessed him, and we announced to him all the things which had been decreed concerning him, that he should not die till he should beget six sons more, and should see (them) before he died; but (that) in Isaac should his name and seed be called: (16:16).

And (that) all the seed of his sons should be Gentiles, and be reckoned with the Gentiles; but from the sons of Isaac one should become a holy seed, and should not be reckoned among the Gentiles. (16:17).

For he should become the portion of the Most High, and all his seed had fallen into the possession of God, that it should be to the Lord a people for (His) possession above all nations and that it should become a kingdom and priests and a holy nation. (16:18).
And we went our way, and we announced to Sarah all that we had told him, and they both rejoiced with exceeding great joy. (16:19).

And he built there an altar to the Lord who had delivered him, and who was making him rejoice in the land of his sojourning, and he celebrated a festival of joy in this month seven days, near the altar which he had built at the Well of the Oath. (16:20).
And he built booths for himself and for his servants on this festival, and he was the first to celebrate the feast of tabernacles on the earth. (16:21).

And during these seven days he brought each day to the altar a burnt offering to the Lord, two oxen, two rams, seven sheep, one he-goat, for a sin offering, that he might atone thereby for himself and for his seed. (16:22).

And, as a thank-offering, seven rams, seven kids, seven sheep, and seven he-goats, and their fruit offerings and their drink offerings; and he burnt all the fat thereof on the altar, a chosen offering to the Lord for a sweet smelling savour. (16:23).

And morning and evening he burnt fragrant substances, frankincense and galbanum, and stackte, and nard, and myrrh, and spice, and costum; all these seven he offered, crushed, mixed together in equal parts (and) pure. (16:24).

And he celebrated this feast during seven days, rejoicing with all his heart and with all his soul, he and all those who were in his house, and there was no stranger with him, nor any that was uncircumcised. (16:25).

And he blessed his Creator who had created him in his generation, for He had created him according to His good pleasure; for He knew and perceived that from him would arise the plant of righteousness for the eternal generations, and from him a holy seed, so that it should become like Him who had made all things. (16:26).
And he blessed and rejoiced, and he called the name of this festival the festival of the Lord, a joy acceptable to the Most High God. (16:27).

And we blessed him for ever, and all his seed after him throughout all the generations of the earth, because he celebrated this festival in its season, according to the testimony of the heavenly tablets. (16:28).

For this reason it is ordained on the heavenly tablets concerning Israel, that they shall celebrate the feast of tabernacles seven days with joy, in the seventh month, acceptable before the Lord -a statute for ever throughout their generations every year. (16:29).

And to this there is no limit of days; for it is ordained for ever regarding Israel that they should celebrate it and dwell in booths, and set wreaths upon their heads, and take leafy boughs, and willows from the brook. (16:30).

And Abraham took branches of palm trees, and the fruit of goodly trees, and every day going round the altar with the branches seven times [a day] in the morning, he praised and gave thanks to his God for all things in joy. (16:31).
crossRefs: Genesis 18:1-15: Three men come to Abraham at the oaks of Mamre, the son is promised for the set time next year, and Sarah laughs behind the tent door and then denies it.
Genesis 19:1-29: Sodom and Gomorrah and the whole plain are overthrown with fire and brimstone, and Lot is brought out because God remembered Abraham.
Genesis 21:1-8: The LORD visits Sarah as He had said, Isaac is born at the set time, and Abraham circumcises him when he is eight days old.
Leviticus 23:39-43: Seven days of booths in the seventh month with the fruit of goodly trees, palm branches and willows of the brook, the feast this chapter says Abraham kept first.
Nehemiah 8:14-17: Israel finds the command to dwell in booths written in the law, goes out for olive, myrtle and palm branches, and keeps the feast with very great gladness.

translationNotes.note: Sukkot means booths, temporary shelters of cut branches. Leviticus 23:34-43 sets the feast at seven days from the fifteenth of the seventh month and gives its reason: Israel dwelt in booths when God brought them out of Egypt. At 16:20-21 this book has Abraham build booths at the Well of the Oath and calls him the first man on earth to keep the feast, which Genesis does not say.

Beersheba, at the southern edge of the settled land where the hills run out into the Negev desert. The name carries both well of the oath and well of seven, and Genesis 21:30-31 supplies both: Abraham gives Abimelech seven ewe lambs as witness that he dug the well, and the place is named because the two men swore there.

Leviticus 23:40 names four kinds to be carried: the fruit of goodly trees, branches of palm trees, boughs of thick trees, and willows of the brook. The palm branch is the lulav. At 16:31 Abraham carries them round the altar seven times every morning, a circuit that Leviticus does not describe.

At 16:24 Abraham burns seven fragrant substances morning and evening, crushed and mixed in equal parts: frankincense, galbanum, stacte, nard, myrrh, spice and costum. Exodus 30:34-38 gives the holy incense as four in equal parts and forbids anyone to copy it for private use. Nard is spikenard, an oil pressed from a Himalayan root, the ointment poured out on Jesus at Mark 14:3.

translationNotes.term: A kingdom and priests and a holy nation
translationNotes.note: At 16:18 the promise about Isaac's line uses the words spoken to all Israel at Sinai in Exodus 19:6, a kingdom of priests and a holy nation. Peter applies the same phrase to believers at 1 Peter 2:9. The point in each place is a whole people holding an office normally held by a few men.

stories.keyTakeaway: The angels announce Isaac at Mamre and Sarah laughs; Sodom is burned and Lot is brought out. Isaac is born in the third month and circumcised on the eighth day. Abraham then keeps seven days of feast at the Well of the Oath, builds booths, and circles the altar with branches each morning.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 17
summaryBullets: And in the first year of the fifth week Isaac was weaned in this jubilee, [1982 A.M.] and Abraham made a great banquet in the third month, on the day his son Isaac was weaned. (17:1).

And Ishmael, the son of Hagar, the Egyptian, was before the face of Abraham, his father, in his place, and Abraham rejoiced and blessed God because he had seen his sons and had not died childless. (17:2).

And he remembered the words which He had spoken to him on the day on which Lot had parted from him, and he rejoiced because the Lord had given him seed upon the earth to inherit the earth, and he blessed with all his mouth the Creator of all things. (17:3).

And Sarah saw Ishmael playing and dancing, and Abraham rejoicing with great joy, and she became jealous of Ishmael and said to Abraham, 'Cast out this bondwoman and her son; for the son of this bondwoman will not be heir with my son, Isaac.' (17:4).
And the thing was grievous in Abraham's sight, because of his maidservant and because of his son, that he should drive them from him. (17:5).

And God said to Abraham 'Let it not be grievous in your sight, because of the child and because of the bondwoman; in all that Sarah has said to you, harken to her words and do (them); for in Isaac shall your name and seed be called. (17:6).
But as for the son of this bondwoman I will make him a great nation, because he is of your seed.' (17:7).
And Abraham rose up early in the morning, and took bread and a bottle of water, and placed them on the shoulders of Hagar and the child, and sent her away. (17:8).
And she departed and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba, and the water in the bottle was spent, and the child thirsted, and was not able to go on, and fell down. (17:9).

And his mother took him and cast him under an olive tree, and went and sat her down over against him, at the distance of a bow-shot; for she said, 'Let me not see the death of my child,' and as she sat she wept. (17:10).
And an angel of God, one of the holy ones, said to her, 'Why weepest you, Hagar? Arise take the child, and hold him in yours hand; for God has heard your voice, and has seen the child.' (17:11).
And she opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water, and she went and filled her bottle with water, and she gave her child to drink, and she arose and went towards the wilderness of Paran. (17:12).
And the child grew and became an archer, and God was with him, and his mother took him a wife from among the daughters of Egypt. (17:13).
And she bare him a son, and he called his name Nebaioth; for she said, 'The Lord was near to me when I called upon him.' (17:14).

And it came to pass in the seventh week, in the first year thereof, [2003 A.M.] in the first month in this jubilee, on the twelfth of this month, there were voices in heaven regarding Abraham, that he was faithful in all that He told him, and that he loved the Lord, and that in every affliction he was faithful. (17:15).

And the prince Mastêmâ came and said before God, 'Behold, Abraham loves Isaac his son, and he delights in him above all things else; bid him offer him as a burnt-offering on the altar, and You will see if he will do this command, and You will know if he is faithful in everything in which You do try him. (17:16).

And the Lord knew that Abraham was faithful in all his afflictions; for He had tried him through his country and with famine, and had tried him with the wealth of kings, and had tried him again through his wife, when she was torn (from him), and with circumcision; and had tried him through Ishmael and Hagar, his maid-servant, when he sent them away. (17:17).
And in everything in which He had tried him, he was found faithful, and his soul was not impatient, and he was not slow to act; for he was faithful and a lover of the Lord. (17:18).
crossRefs: Genesis 21:9-21: Sarah demands the bondwoman and her son be cast out, the water in the skin is spent, God hears the boy crying, and Hagar's eyes are opened to a well.
Genesis 22:1-2: God tests Abraham and tells him to take his son, his only son Isaac, and offer him on one of the mountains, the command Mastema asks for at the end of this chapter.
Job 1:6-12: The accuser tells God that Job serves Him only because he is hedged about, and asks that he be touched, the same proposal put in the same form.
Genesis 16:7-14: The angel of the LORD finds Hagar by a spring in the wilderness the first time she runs, and she names the well after the God who sees her.
Genesis 25:13-16: Nebaioth is named as Ishmael's firstborn at the head of the twelve princes of his line.

translationNotes.note: Children were nursed far longer than now, commonly to two or three years old, so weaning marked the end of the most dangerous stretch of a child's life and was worth a feast, as at Genesis 21:8. In 2 Maccabees 7:27 a mother tells her son she nursed him three years, which gives the ordinary figure from the period itself.

A skin bag, usually a whole goatskin sewn shut and slung over the shoulder, the ordinary water container for travel. Genesis 21:14 has Abraham put bread and one of these on Hagar. A single skin holds a few days of water at most, which is why at 17:9 it runs dry before she is out of the wilderness of Beersheba.

The wilderness of Paran is the desert filling the central and eastern Sinai peninsula between Egypt and the Negev. Genesis 21:21 says Ishmael dwelt there and that his mother took him a wife out of Egypt. Numbers 13:3 has Moses send the twelve spies into Canaan from the wilderness of Paran.

At 17:17 the book lists what Abraham had already been tried with: his country, famine, the wealth of kings, the taking of his wife, circumcision, and the sending away of Hagar and Ishmael. At 19:8 the burial of Sarah is counted as the tenth. Genesis calls only one episode a test, at Genesis 22:1.

At 17:15-16 the chapter opens a scene in heaven before anything happens on the ground, with speech about Abraham's faithfulness and then Mastema's challenge. Job 1:6-12 has the identical shape, a court in heaven the man below knows nothing about. Genesis 22:1 gives only the bare statement that God tested Abraham.

stories.keyTakeaway: Isaac is weaned and Abraham holds a banquet. Sarah demands that Hagar and Ishmael be sent away, and in the wilderness an angel shows Hagar a well. Then voices in heaven speak of Abraham's faithfulness, and the prince Mastema asks God to command that Isaac be offered as a test.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 18
summaryBullets: And God said to him, 'Abraham, Abraham'; and he said, Behold, (here) am I.' (18:1).
And he said, Take your beloved son whom you lovest, (even) Isaac, and go to the high country, and offer him on one of the mountains which I will point out to you.' (18:2).

And he rose early in the morning and saddled his ass, and took his two young men with him, and Isaac his son, and clave the wood of the burnt offering, and he went to the place on the third day, and he saw the place afar off. (18:3).
And he came to a well of water, and he said to his young men, 'Abide you here with the ass, and I and the lad shall go (yonder), and when we have worshipped we shall come again to you.' (18:4).
And he took the wood of the burnt-offering and laid it on Isaac his son, and he took in his hand the fire and the knife, and they went both of them together to that place. (18:5).

And the Lord called Abraham by his name a second time from heaven, as he caused us to appear to speak to him in the name of the Lord. (18:14).

And he said: 'By Myself have I sworn, says the Lord, Because you have done this thing, And have not withheld your son, your beloved son, from Me, That in blessing I will bless you, And in multiplying I will multiply your seed As the stars of heaven, And as the sand which is on the seashore. And your seed shall inherit the cities of its enemies, And in your seed shall all nations of the earth be blessed; Because you have obeyed My voice, And I have shown to all that you are faithful to Me in all that I have said to you: Go in peace.' And he celebrated this festival every year, seven days with joy, and he called it the festival of the Lord according to the seven days during which he went and returned in peace. And accordingly has it been ordained and written on the heavenly tablets regarding Israel and its seed that they should observe this festival seven days with the joy of festival. (18:15).

crossRefs: Genesis 22:1-19: The three days' journey, the wood laid on Isaac, the question about the lamb, the angel's call from heaven, the ram caught in a thicket, and the oath God swears by Himself.
Exodus 13:13-15: Every firstborn donkey is redeemed with a lamb and every firstborn son of Israel is redeemed, which is substitution written into the law.
Psalm 132:13-14: The LORD chooses Zion and calls it His resting place forever, the mountain this chapter identifies with the place Abraham named.
Hebrews 11:17-19: By faith Abraham offered up Isaac, reckoning that God was able to raise him up even from the dead.
James 2:21-23: Abraham is called the friend of God, the same title this book records for him on the heavenly tablets.

translationNotes.note: Genesis 22:2 sends Abraham to the land of Moriah, and Genesis 22:14 has him name the place The LORD will see, saying that in the mount of the LORD it shall be seen. The books of Chronicles name Mount Moriah as the place where the temple was later built. At 18:13 Jubilees states the identification outright: that is Mount Zion.

translationNotes.term: A ram caught by his horns
translationNotes.note: An ayil is a full-grown male sheep, the standard animal for a burnt offering, Leviticus 1:10. At 18:12 it is caught by the horns in the thicket and offered in the place of Isaac. The law later builds the same exchange in: Exodus 13:13 has a firstborn donkey redeemed by a lamb and every firstborn son redeemed.

At 18:3 Abraham reaches the place on the third day, as at Genesis 22:4. He sets out from the Well of the Oath, Beersheba, and returns there at 18:17. Beersheba to Jerusalem is roughly forty-five miles along the ridge road, which is three days of walking with a loaded donkey, so the timing in the text matches the ground.

At 18:9 the angel and Mastema both stand watching, and at 18:12 Mastema is shamed when the knife is stopped. Genesis 22:1 says only that God tested Abraham, with no second party anywhere in the scene. The book has framed the whole episode as a challenge answered, the way Job 1:6-12 frames what happens to Job.

At 18:15 God swears by Himself, as at Genesis 22:16. An oath in that world named a higher power as guarantor, so an oath sworn by God's own name is the strongest form there is, because there is nothing above it to appeal to. Hebrews 6:13-14 quotes this oath and says God swore by Himself for exactly that reason.

stories.keyTakeaway: Abraham takes Isaac to the mountain, binds him and reaches for the knife, and the angel stops him while Mastema is put to shame. A ram caught by its horns is offered instead. The place is named because the Lord has seen, and this chapter says plainly that it is Mount Zion.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 19
summaryBullets: And in the first year of the first week in the forty-second jubilee, Abraham returned and dwelt opposite Hebron, that is Kirjath Arba, two weeks of years. (19:1).
And in the first year of the third week of this jubilee the days of the life of Sarah were accomplished, and she died in Hebron. (19:2).

And Abraham went to mourn over her and bury her, and we tried him [to see] if his spirit were patient and he were not indignant in the words of his mouth; and he was found patient in this, and was not disturbed. (19:3).
For in patience of spirit he conversed with the children of Heth, to the intent that they should give him a place in which to bury his dead. (19:4).

And the Lord gave him grace before all who saw him, and he besought in gentleness the sons of Heth, and they gave him the land of the double cave over against Mamre, that is Hebron, for four hundred pieces of silver. (19:5).

And they besought him saying, We shall give it to you for nothing; but he would not take it from their hands for nothing, for he gave the price of the place, the money in full, and he bowed down before them twice, and after this he buried his dead in the double cave. (19:6).
And all the days of the life of Sarah were one hundred and twenty-seven years, that is, two jubilees and four weeks and one year: these are the days of the years of the life of Sarah. (19:7).
This is the tenth trial with which Abraham was tried, and he was found faithful, patient in spirit. (19:8).

And he said not a single word regarding the rumour in the land how that God had said that He would give it to him and to his seed after him, and he begged a place there to bury his dead; for he was found faithful, and was recorded on the heavenly tablets as the friend of God. (19:9).

And in the fourth year thereof he took a wife for his son Isaac and her name was Rebecca [2020 A.M.] [the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Nahor, the brother of Abraham] the sister of Laban and daughter of Bethuel; and Bethuel was the son of Melca, who was the wife of Nahor, the brother of Abraham. (19:10).

And Abraham took to himself a third wife, and her name was Keturah, from among the daughters of his household servants, for Hagar had died before Sarah. And she bare him six sons, Zimram, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah, in the two weeks of years. (19:11).

crossRefs: Genesis 23:1-20: Sarah dies at Kirjath-arba, Abraham bargains with the sons of Heth and weighs out four hundred shekels of silver for the cave of Machpelah and the field around it.
Genesis 24:1-67: The servant is sent back to Abraham's kindred and brings home Rebecca, the daughter of Bethuel, as a wife for Isaac.
Genesis 22:20-24: The sons born to Nahor, Abraham's brother, are listed, ending with Bethuel who fathered Rebekah, which is how the family this chapter fetches a bride from is traced.
Genesis 25:24-28: The twins are born, Esau a hunter and a man of the field and Jacob a plain man dwelling in tents, and Isaac loves Esau while Rebekah loves Jacob.
Genesis 49:29-32: Jacob names the cave of Machpelah as the burial place of Abraham and Sarah, Isaac and Rebekah, and Leah.

translationNotes.note: Machpelah carries the sense of doubled, which is why the book calls it the double cave. It lies at Hebron, about twenty miles south of Jerusalem in the Judean hills. Genesis 23:17-20 records the purchase of the field, the cave and every tree in it, and Genesis 49:31 lists who was laid there.

Genesis 23:16 says four hundred shekels weighed out in the currency of the merchants; coinage did not yet exist, so silver was weighed on scales. A shekel runs about eleven grams, so four hundred is near ten pounds of silver. Jeremiah 32:9 buys an entire field at Anathoth for seventeen shekels, which shows what a price Abraham paid.

The Hittites. Genesis 23:10-18 has Abraham deal with them at the gate of the city, which is where legal business was done in front of witnesses. The Hittites ran an empire out of Anatolia that fought Egypt to a standstill at Kadesh, and their capital archive at Hattusa was excavated in 1906, which settled the question of whether such a people existed.

Genesis 25:1-4 names the same six sons. Midian among them is the people Moses lives with and marries into at Exodus 2:15-21, and Genesis 37:28 has Midianite traders carry Joseph down to Egypt. At 19:11 the book adds that Keturah came from Abraham's own household servants and that Hagar had died before Sarah.

At 19:9 Abraham is written on the heavenly tablets as the friend of God, ohev meaning one who loves. Isaiah 41:8 calls Israel the seed of Abraham my friend, and James 2:23 says the scripture was fulfilled and he was called the friend of God.

stories.keyTakeaway: Sarah dies at Hebron and Abraham buys the double cave from the sons of Heth for four hundred pieces of silver, refusing to take it as a gift; the book counts this his tenth trial. Rebecca is brought for Isaac, Keturah bears six sons, Jacob and Esau are born, and Abraham blesses Jacob.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 20
summaryBullets: And in the forty-second jubilee, in the first year of the seventh week, Abraham called Ishmael, [2052 (2045?) A.M.] and his twelve sons, and Isaac and his two sons, and the six sons of Keturah, and their sons. (20:1).

And he commanded them that they should observe the way of the Lord; that they should work righteousness, and love each his neighbour, and act on this manner amongst all men; that they should each so walk with regard to them as to do judgment and righteousness on the earth. (20:2).

That they should circumcise their sons, according to the covenant which He had made with them, and not deviate to the right hand or the left of all the paths which the Lord had commanded us; and that we should keep ourselves from all fornication and uncleanness, [and renounce from amongst us all fornication and uncleanness]. (20:3).

And if any woman or maid commit fornication amongst you, burn her with fire and let them not commit fornication with her after their eyes and their heart; and let them not take to themselves wives from the daughters of Canaan; for the seed of Canaan will be rooted out of the land. (20:4).

And he told them of the judgment of the giants, and the judgment of the Sodomites, how they had been judged on account of their wickedness, and had died on account of their fornication, and uncleanness, and mutual corruption through fornication. I implore you, my sons, love the God of heaven And cleave you to all His commandments. crossRefs: Genesis 18:19: Abraham is chosen so that he will command his children and his household after him to keep the way of the LORD, the charge this chapter shows him carrying out.
Genesis 25:5-6: Abraham gives all that he has to Isaac and sends the sons of the concubines away eastward with gifts while he is still alive.
Genesis 24:3-4: Abraham makes his servant swear to take no wife for Isaac from the daughters of the Canaanites but to go to his own country and kindred.
Leviticus 21:9: The daughter of a priest who profanes herself by playing the harlot is burned with fire, the penalty this chapter applies far more widely.
Leviticus 19:18: You shall love your neighbour as yourself, the command this chapter has Abraham lay on all his sons at once.

translationNotes.note: Counted as six at 20:1, the same six as Genesis 25:2. At 20:12-13 the book says they and Ishmael's sons settled together from Paran to the approaches of Babylon, mixed with one another, and were called Arabs and Ishmaelites. Genesis 25:18 places Ishmael's people from Havilah to Shur, on the edge of Egypt.

At 20:4 the penalty for a woman found in fornication is burning. The law of Moses prescribes burning in two cases only: a priest's daughter who plays the harlot, Leviticus 21:9, and a man who takes both a woman and her mother, Leviticus 20:14. Genesis 38:24 has Judah order Tamar burned before he learns the child is his. This chapter applies the penalty more widely than the law does.

Both words cover sexual union outside marriage, and both are also used of marrying outside the covenant. That is the sin this chapter keeps returning to at 20:3-6, tied back to the giants before the flood and to Sodom. Deuteronomy 7:3-4 gives the stated reason for the marriage rule: the foreign spouse turns the son away to serve other gods.

Two different kinds of idol. A massekhah is poured, metal melted and cast in a mould, like the calf at Exodus 32:4. A pesel is carved out of wood or stone. Exodus 20:4 forbids the carved kind by name, and Habakkuk 2:18-19 mocks both: the man trusts a thing he made himself, and tells a block of wood to wake up.

The stretch named at 20:12 runs from the Sinai desert across northern Arabia to the lower Euphrates, which is the caravan country. Isaiah 60:6-7 names Midian, Ephah, Sheba, Kedar and Nebaioth together as the peoples of that route, coming up with gold and incense and flocks.

stories.keyTakeaway: Abraham gathers every son and grandson and charges them to keep the way of the Lord, to circumcise their sons, to take no Canaanite wives and to keep clear of all fornication, and to serve no idol. He sends Ishmael and Keturah's sons east with gifts and gives everything to Isaac.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 21
summaryBullets: And in the sixth year of the seventh week of this jubilee Abraham called Isaac his son, and [2057 (2050?) A.M.] commanded him: saying, 'I am become old, and know not the day of my death, and am full of my days. (21:1).

And behold, I am one hundred and seventy-five years old, and throughout all the days of my life I have remembered the Lord, and sought with all my heart to do His will, and to walk uprightly in all His ways. (21:2).
My soul has hated idols, <and I have despised those that served them, and I have given my heart and spirit> that I might observe to do the will of Him who created me. (21:3).

For He is the living God, and He is holy and faithful, and He is righteous beyond all, and there is with Him no accepting of (men's) persons and no accepting of gifts; for God is righteous, and executeth judgment on all those who transgress His commandments and despise His covenant. (21:4).
And do you, my son, observe His commandments and His ordinances and His judgments, and walk not after the abominations and after the graven images and after the molten images. (21:5).
And eat no blood at all of animals or cattle, or of any bird which flies in the heaven. (21:6).

And if you do slay a victim as an acceptable peace offering, slay you it, and pour out its blood upon the altar, and all the fat of the offering offer on the altar with fine flour and the meat offering mingled with oil, with its drink offering -offer them all together on the altar of burnt offering; it is a sweet savour before the Lord. (21:7).

And you will offer the fat of the sacrifice of thank offerings on the fire which is upon the altar, and the fat which is on the belly, and all the fat on the inwards and the two kidneys, and all the fat that is upon them, and upon the loins and liver you will remove, together with the kidneys. (21:8).
And offer all these for a sweet savour acceptable before the Lord, with its meat-offering and with its drink- offering, for a sweet savour, the bread of the offering to the Lord. (21:9).

And eat its meat on that day and on the second day, and let not the sun on the second day go down upon it till it is eaten, and let nothing be left over for the third day; for it is not acceptable [for it is not approved] and let it no longer be eaten, and all who eat thereof will bring sin upon themselves; for thus I have found it written in the books of my forefathers, and in the words of Enoch, and in the words of Noah. (21:10).
And on all your oblations you will strew salt, and let not the salt of the covenant be lacking in all your oblations before the Lord. (21:11).

And as regards the wood of the sacrifices, beware lest you bring (other) wood for the altar in addition to these: cypress, bay, almond, fir, pine, cedar, savin, fig, olive, myrrh, laurel, aspalathus. (21:12).

And of these kinds of wood lay upon the altar under the sacrifice, such as have been tested as to their appearance, and do not lay (thereon) any split or dark wood, (but) hard and clean, without fault, a sound and new growth; and do not lay (thereon) old wood, [for its fragrance is gone] for there is no longer fragrance in it as before. (21:13).
Besides these kinds of wood there is none other that you will place (on the altar), for the fragrance is dispersed, and the smell of its fragrance goes not up to heaven. (21:14).
Observe this commandment and do it, my son, that you mayst be upright in all your deeds. (21:15).

And at all times be clean in your body, and wash yourself with water before you approachest to offer on the altar, and wash your hands and your feet before you drawest near to the altar; and when you are done sacrificing, wash again your hands and your feet. (21:16).
And let no blood appear upon you nor upon your clothes; be on your guard, my son, against blood, be on your guard exceedingly; cover it with dust. (21:17).
And do not eat any blood for it is the soul; eat no blood whatever. (21:18).

And take no gifts for the blood of man, lest it be shed with impunity, without judgment; for it is the blood that is shed that causes the earth to sin, and the earth cannot be cleansed from the blood of man save by the blood of him who shed it. (21:19).

And take no present or gift for the blood of man: blood for blood, that you may be accepted before the Lord, the Most High God; for He is the defence of the good: and that you may be preserved from all evil, and that He may save you from every kind of death. I see, my son, That all the works of the children of men are sin and wickedness, And all their deeds are uncleanness and an abomination and a pollution, And there is no righteousness with them. Beware, lest you shouldest walk in their ways And tread in their paths, And sin a sin to death before the Most High God. Else He will [hide His face from you And] give you back into the hands of your transgression, And root you out of the land, and your seed likewise from under heaven, And your name and your seed shall perish from the whole earth. Turn away from all their deeds and all their uncleanness, And observe the ordinance of the Most High God, And do His will and be upright in all things. And He will bless you in all your deeds, And will raise up from you a plant of righteousness through all the earth, throughout all generations of the earth, And my name and your name shall not be forgotten under heaven for ever. Go, my son in peace. May the Most High God, my God and your God, strengthen you to do His will, And may He bless all your seed and the residue of your seed for the generations for ever, with all righteous blessings, That you may be a blessing on all the earth.' And he went out from him rejoicing. (21:20).

crossRefs: Leviticus 3:14-17: The fat of the offering, the two kidneys, the fat on the loins and the caul above the liver are burned on the altar, and Israel is to eat neither fat nor blood.

Leviticus 7:15-18: A thank offering is eaten the day it is offered, a vow or freewill offering may run to the second day, and anything left to the third is refused and counts against the man who eats it.
Leviticus 2:13: Every meal offering is seasoned with salt, and the salt of the covenant of your God is never to be left out, the rule this chapter repeats almost word for word.
Exodus 30:17-21: Aaron and his sons wash their hands and their feet at the basin before they come near the altar, on pain of death, the washing Abraham commands here.
Numbers 35:31-33: No ransom may be taken for the life of a murderer, because blood pollutes the land and the land cannot be cleansed of it except by the blood of the man who shed it.

translationNotes.note: Leviticus 2:13 requires salt on every grain offering and names it the salt of the covenant, and Numbers 18:19 calls the priests' portion a covenant of salt forever. Salt preserves and does not spoil, and eating salt together sealed an agreement in that world, so a covenant of salt is one meant to hold. At 21:11 Abraham lays the rule on Isaac long before Sinai.

Chelev is the hard suet packed around the organs, not the fat running through the meat. The list at 21:8 matches Leviticus 3:14-16 piece for piece: the fat on the belly, the fat on the inwards, the two kidneys with the fat on them, and the covering above the liver. Leviticus 3:17 makes it a perpetual statute that Israel eat neither fat nor blood.

At 21:12 Abraham names the only woods permitted under a sacrifice: cypress, bay, almond, fir, pine, cedar, savin, fig, olive, myrrh, laurel and aspalathus. All are resinous or aromatic. Savin is a juniper, and aspalathus is a thorny fragrant shrub used in perfume, named among the sweet spices at Sirach 24:15. At 21:13-14 the wood must be sound and new, since old wood has lost its fragrance. The law of Moses sets no such list.

A kofer is a ransom, a payment taken instead of a penalty. Numbers 35:31 forbids taking one for the life of a murderer, and Numbers 35:33 says blood pollutes the land and the land is not cleansed except by the blood of the man who shed it. At 21:19-20 Abraham repeats both, which shuts the door on buying your way out of a killing.

At 21:10 Abraham says he found these sacrificial rules already written, in the books of his forefathers and the words of Enoch and Noah. The book has already had Enoch write at 4:17-19 and Noah write his medical book at 10:13-14, so it describes an unbroken written chain from Enoch to Noah to Abraham. Genesis mentions no such books.

stories.keyTakeaway: Abraham at a hundred and seventy-five charges Isaac to serve no idol and to eat no blood. He sets out how a peace offering is cut, burned and eaten within two days, orders salt on every oblation, names the woods allowed on the altar, and forbids taking any payment for a man's blood.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 22
summaryBullets: And it came to pass in the first week in the forty-fourth jubilee, in the second year, that is, the year in which Abraham died, that Isaac and Ishmael came from the Well of the Oath to celebrate the feast of weeks -that is, the feast of the first fruits of the harvest-to Abraham, their father, and Abraham rejoiced because his two sons had come. (22:1).
For Isaac had many possessions in Beersheba, and Isaac was wont to go and see his possessions and to return to his father. (22:2).

And in those days Ishmael came to see his father, and they both came together, and Isaac offered a sacrifice for a burnt offering, and presented it on the altar of his father which he had made in Hebron. (22:3).

And he offered a thank offering and made a feast of joy before Ishmael, his brother: and Rebecca made new cakes from the new grain, and gave them to Jacob, her son, to take them to Abraham, his father, from the first fruits of the land, that he might eat and bless the Creator of all things before he died. (22:4).
And Isaac, too, sent by the hand of Jacob to Abraham a best thank offering, that he might eat and drink. (22:5).

And he eat and drank, and blessed the Most High God, Who has created heaven and earth, Who has made all the fat things of the earth, And given them to the children of men That they might eat and drink and bless their Creator. 'And now I give thanks to You, my God, because you have caused me to see this day: behold, I am one hundred three score and fifteen years, an old man and full of days, and all my days have been to me peace. The sword of the adversary has not overcome me in all that You have given me and my children all the days of my life until this day. My God, may Your mercy and Your peace be upon Your servant, and upon the seed of his sons, that they may be to You a chosen nation and an inheritance from amongst all the nations of the earth from henceforth to all the days of the generations of the earth, to all the ages.' And he called Jacob and said: 'My son Jacob, may the God of all bless you and strengthen you to do righteousness, and His will before Him, and may He choose you and your seed that you may become a people for His inheritance according to His will alway. And do you, my son, Jacob, draw near and kiss me.' And he drew near and kissed him, and he said: 'Blessed be my son Jacob And all the sons of God Most High, to all the ages: May God give to you a seed of righteousness; And some of your sons may He sanctify in the midst of the whole earth; May nations serve you, And all the nations bow themselves before your seed. Be strong in the presence of men, And exercise authority over all the seed of Seth. Then your ways and the ways of your sons will be justified, So that they shall become a holy nation. May the Most High God give you all the blessings With which He has blessed me And with which He blessed Noah and Adam; May they rest on the sacred head of your seed from generation to generation for ever. And may He cleanse you from all unrighteousness and impurity, That you may be forgiven all the transgressions; which you have committed ignorantly. And may He strengthen you, And bless you. And may you inherit the whole earth, And may He renew His covenant with you. That you may be to Him a nation for His inheritance for all the ages, And that He may be to you and to your seed a God in truth and righteousness throughout all the days of the earth. And do you, my son Jacob, remember my words, And observe the commandments of Abraham, your father: Separate yourself from the nations, And eat not with them: And do not according to their works, And become not their associate; For their works are unclean, And all their ways are a Pollution and an abomination and uncleanness. They offer their sacrifices to the dead And they worship evil spirits, And they eat over the graves, And all their works are vanity and nothingness. They have no heart to understand And their eyes do not see what their works are, And how they err in saying to a piece of wood: 'You are my God,' And to a stone: 'You are my Lord and you are my deliverer.' [And they have no heart.] And as for you, my son Jacob, May the Most High God help you And the God of heaven bless you And remove you from their uncleanness and from all their error. Be you ware, my son Jacob, of taking a wife from any seed of the daughters of Canaan; For all his seed is to be rooted out of the earth. For, owing to the transgression of Ham, Canaan erred, And all his seed shall be destroyed from off the earth and all the residue thereof, And none springing from him shall be saved on the day of judgment. And as for all the worshippers of idols and the profane (b) There shall be no hope for them in the land of the living; (c) And there shall be no remembrance of them on the earth; (c) For they shall descend into Sheol, (d) And into the place of condemnation shall they go, As the children of Sodom were taken away from the earth So will all those who worship idols be taken away. Fear not, my son Jacob, And be not dismayed, O son of Abraham: May the Most High God preserve you from destruction, And from all the paths of error may he deliver you. This house have I built for myself that I might put my name upon it in the earth: [it is given to you and to your seed for ever], and it will be named the house of Abraham; it is given to you and to your seed for ever; for you will build my house and establish my name before God for ever: your seed and your name will stand throughout all generations of the earth.' And he ceased commanding him and blessing him. And the two lay together on one bed, and Jacob slept in the bosom of Abraham, his father's father and he kissed him seven times, and his affection and his heart rejoiced over him. crossRefs: Leviticus 23:15-21: Seven weeks are counted from the sheaf and two loaves of new grain are brought as firstfruits, the offering this chapter brings to an old man rather than an altar.
Deuteronomy 26:1-11: The firstfruits are carried in a basket to the priest with a recital of what God did for the fathers, the shape of the feast this chapter describes.
Isaiah 65:4: A people who sit among the graves and lodge in the vaults, eating what is unclean, the practice this chapter charges the nations with.
Psalm 106:28: They joined themselves to Baal of Peor and ate the sacrifices of the dead, the same charge in almost the same words.
Genesis 27:29: Let peoples serve you and nations bow down to you, cursed be everyone who curses you and blessed be everyone who blesses you, the blessing Abraham speaks over Jacob here.

translationNotes.note: At 22:17 the nations are charged with offering sacrifice to the dead, eating over graves and worshipping evil spirits. Feeding the dead at the tomb was ordinary practice among Israel's neighbours, and the law addresses it head on: Deuteronomy 26:14 makes the Israelite declare he has given none of the tithe for the dead, and Psalm 106:28 says Israel ate the sacrifices of the dead at Baal of Peor.

translationNotes.term: New cakes from the new grain
translationNotes.note: Bikkurim are firstfruits, the first of a crop given up before any of the rest may be used. Leviticus 23:17 has two loaves of new grain baked with leaven and waved before the LORD at the feast of weeks. At 22:4 Rebecca bakes new cakes from the new grain and sends them by Jacob so that Abraham may eat and bless the Creator before he dies.

Badal means to divide or set apart. It is the verb used when God divides the light from the darkness at Genesis 1:4 and when Israel is told to divide clean from unclean at Leviticus 20:25. At 22:16 the charge is pushed as far as the table: do not eat with them and do not become their associate. Leviticus 20:26 gives the ground, that Israel is separated from the peoples to be God's.

At 22:12 Jacob is blessed to exercise authority over all the seed of Seth. Seth is Adam's third son, born after Abel was killed, Genesis 4:25, and every person alive after the flood descends through him by way of Noah, Genesis 5:6-32. The phrase therefore means the whole human race, not one nation among others.

At 22:26 Abraham kisses Jacob seven times and the two lie on one bed. Seven runs through the whole book as the number of a completed thing, from the six days and the seventh to the weeks of years, so an act done seven times is done in full measure. Genesis records no meeting between Abraham and Jacob at all.

stories.keyTakeaway: Isaac and Ishmael come to Abraham for the feast of weeks with the firstfruits, and Rebecca sends new cakes by Jacob. Abraham blesses Jacob, tells him to keep clear of nations that sacrifice to the dead and eat over graves, warns him off a Canaanite wife, and Jacob sleeps in his arms.

summaryBullets: And he placed two fingers of Jacob on his eyes, and he blessed the God of gods, and he covered his face and stretched out his feet and slept the sleep of eternity, and was gathered to his fathers. (23:1).
And notwithstanding all this Jacob was lying in his bosom, and knew not that Abraham, his father's father, was dead. (23:2).
And Jacob awoke from his sleep, and behold Abraham was cold as ice, and he said 'Father, father'; but there was none that spoke, and he knew that he was dead. (23:3).

And he arose from his bosom and ran and told Rebecca, his mother; and Rebecca went to Isaac in the night, and told him; and they went together, and Jacob with them, and a lamp was in his hand, and when they had gone in they found Abraham lying dead. (23:4).
And Isaac fell on the face of his father and wept and kissed him. (23:5).

And the voices were heard in the house of Abraham, and Ishmael his son arose, and went to Abraham his father, and wept over Abraham his father, he and all the house of Abraham, and they wept with a great weeping. (23:6).

And his sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the double cave, near Sarah his wife, and they wept for him forty days, all the men of his house, and Isaac and Ishmael, and all their sons, and all the sons of Keturah in their places; and the days of weeping for Abraham were ended. (23:7).
And he lived three jubilees and four weeks of years, one hundred and seventy-five years, and completed the days of his life, being old and full of days. (23:8).

For the days of the forefathers, of their life, were nineteen jubilees; and after the Flood they began to grow less than nineteen jubilees, and to decrease in jubilees, and to grow old quickly, and to be full of their days by reason of manifold tribulation and the wickedness of their ways, with the exception of Abraham. (23:9).

For Abraham was perfect in all his deeds with the Lord, and well-pleasing in righteousness all the days of his life; and behold, he did not complete four jubilees in his life, when he had grown old by reason of the wickedness, and was full of his days. (23:10).

And all the generations which shall arise from this time until the day of the great judgment shall grow old quickly, before they complete two jubilees, and their knowledge shall forsake them by reason of their old age Land all their know- ledge shall vanish away]. (23:11).

And in those days, if a man live a jubilee and a-half of years, they shall say regarding him: 'He has lived long, and the greater part of his days are pain and sorrow and tribulation, and there is no peace: (23:12).

For calamity follows on calamity, and wound on wound, and tribulation on tribulation, and evil tidings on evil tidings, and illness on illness, and all evil judgments such as these, one with another, illness and overthrow, and snow and frost and ice, and fever, and chills, and torpor, and famine, and death, and sword, and captivity, and all kinds of calamities and pains.' (23:13).
And all these shall come on an evil generation, which transgresses on the earth: their works are uncleanness and fornication, and pollution and abominations. (23:14).

Then they shall say: 'The days of the forefathers were many (even), to a thousand years, and were good; but behold, the days of our life, if a man has lived many, are three score years and ten, and, if he is strong, four score years, and those evil, and there is no peace in the days of this evil generation.' (23:15).

And in that generation the sons shall convict their fathers and their elders of sin and unrighteousness, and of the words of their mouth and the great wickednesses which they perpetrate, and concerning their forsaking the covenant which the Lord made between them and Him, that they should observe and do all His commandments and His ordinances and all His laws, without departing either to the right hand or the left. (23:16).
For all have done evil, and every mouth speaks iniquity and all their works are an uncleanness and an abomination, and all their ways are pollution, uncleanness and destruction. (23:17).

Behold the earth shall be destroyed on account of all their works, and there shall be no seed of the vine, and no oil; for their works are altogether faithless, and they shall all perish together, beasts and cattle and birds, and all the fish of the sea, on account of the children of men. (23:18).

And they shall strive one with another, the young with the old, and the old with the young, the poor with the rich, the lowly with the great, and the beggar with the prince, on account of the law and the covenant; for they have forgotten commandment, and covenant, and feasts, and months, and Sabbaths, and jubilees, and all judgments. (23:19).
And they shall stand <with bows and> swords and war to turn them back into the way; but they shall not return until much blood has been shed on the earth, one by another. (23:20).

And those who have escaped shall not return from their wickedness to the way of righteousness, but they shall all exalt themselves to deceit and wealth, that they may each take all that is his neighbour's, and they shall name the great name, but not in truth and not in righteousness, and they shall defile the holy of holies with their uncleanness and the corruption of their pollution. (23:21).
And a great punishment shall befall the deeds of this generation from the Lord, and He will give them over to the sword and to judgment and to captivity, and to be plundered and devoured. (23:22).

And He will wake up against them the sinners of the Gentiles, who have neither mercy nor compassion, and who shall respect the person of none, neither old nor young, nor any one, for they are more wicked and strong to do evil than all the children of men. And they shall use violence against Israel and transgression against Jacob, And much blood shall be shed upon the earth, And there shall be none to gather and none to bury. In those days they shall cry aloud, And call and pray that they may be saved from the hand of the sinners, the Gentiles; But none shall be saved. And the heads of the children shall be white with grey hair, And a child of three weeks shall appear old like a man of one hundred years, And their stature shall be destroyed by tribulation and oppression. And in those days the children shall begin to study the laws, And to seek the commandments, And to return to the path of righteousness. And the days shall begin to grow many and increase amongst those children of men Till their days draw near to one thousand years. And to a greater number of years than (before) was the number of the days. And there shall be no old man Nor one who is <not> satisfied with his days, For all shall be (as) children and youths. And all their days they shall complete and live in peace and in joy, And there shall be no Satan nor any evil destroyer; For all their days shall be days of blessing and healing. And at that time the Lord will heal His servants, And they shall rise up and see great peace, And drive out their adversaries. And the righteous shall see and be thankful, And rejoice with joy for ever and ever, And shall see all their judgments and all their curses on their enemies. crossRefs: Genesis 25:7-10: Abraham dies at a hundred and seventy-five, old and full of years, and Isaac and Ishmael bury him in the cave of Machpelah beside Sarah.
Psalm 90:10: The days of our years are threescore and ten, or fourscore by reason of strength, and their span is labour and sorrow, the figure this chapter quotes.
Isaiah 65:20-22: No infant of days nor an old man who has not filled out his days, for a man dying at a hundred will count as a child, and they shall long enjoy the work of their hands.
Deuteronomy 32:24-25: Wasting hunger, burning heat and bitter destruction, the sword outside and terror within, the same piling of calamity on calamity this chapter uses.
Daniel 12:2-3: Many who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, and those who are wise shall shine like the brightness of the firmament.

translationNotes.note: At 23:7 the household weeps forty days for Abraham. Genesis 50:3 gives forty days for embalming Jacob with seventy days of Egyptian mourning; Numbers 20:29 gives thirty days for Aaron and Deuteronomy 34:8 thirty for Moses. Forty is the standard long count in Scripture, used for the rain, for the days on the mountain and for the years in the wilderness.

At 23:15 the coming generation says a long life is seventy years, eighty if a man is strong, and those evil, which is Psalm 90:10 almost exactly. The chapter sets that against the forefathers at nineteen jubilees, over nine hundred years, and against Abraham who did not reach four jubilees, which on this reckoning is a hundred and ninety-six.

At 23:12 a man who reaches a jubilee and a half is spoken of as having lived long. A jubilee here is forty-nine years, so the figure is seventy-three and a half, which lands on the same span Psalm 90:10 names. Reading this book's numbers means doing the multiplication every time.

translationNotes.term: No Satan nor any evil destroyer
translationNotes.note: Satan is an ordinary Hebrew noun meaning adversary or accuser before it is ever used as a name. At Numbers 22:22 the angel of the LORD stands in the road as a satan against Balaam, and at Job 1:6 the definite form ha-satan means the accuser. At 23:29 the book says that in the days to come there will be no satan and no destroyer left.

translationNotes.term: Bones in the earth, spirits in joy
translationNotes.note: At 23:31 the dead are described with the bones resting in the ground and the spirits rejoicing. Daniel 12:2 speaks of many who sleep in the dust of the earth awaking, and Isaiah 26:19 says the dead shall live and those who dwell in dust shall awake and sing. The chapter states the expectation and does not explain how it works.

stories.keyTakeaway: Abraham dies with Jacob asleep in his arms and is buried in the double cave, mourned forty days. The chapter then looks forward: lifespans shrink to seventy or eighty years and a generation forgets the covenant, until children study the law again and the days lengthen toward a thousand years.

Genesis 26:1-33: Isaac is told not to go down to Egypt, sows and reaps a hundredfold at Gerar, re-digs the wells the Philistines had stopped, and swears an oath with Abimelech at Beersheba.

translationNotes.note: The firstborn's portion: a double share of the inheritance and headship of the family after the father. Deuteronomy 21:15-17 fixes the double share in law and forbids a man to hand it to a favourite's son instead. At 24:3-7 Esau trades it for a meal, and the chapter says Jacob became the elder and Esau was brought down from his dignity.

Adom means red, and Genesis 25:30 has Esau ask for that red, red stuff, so the name Edom sticks to him and then to the nation from him. The dish is lentils, adashim, a cheap staple boiled down to a thick red-brown mush. Edom's country is the red sandstone highland south of the Dead Sea.

Gerar lies in the western Negev between Gaza and Beersheba, on the edge of the grain country, which is why famine drives Isaac there rather than to Egypt. Genesis 26:1 calls Abimelech king of the Philistines at Gerar. The later Philistine power held five cities on the coastal plain, Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod, Ekron and Gath, listed at Joshua 13:3.

A dug well is capital in that country: months of labour cut through rock, and the difference between grazing land and desert. Filling an enemy's wells with earth was a standard act of war, which is what Genesis 26:15 says the Philistines did once Abraham was dead. At 24:19-20 each re-dug well is named after the fight over it, Perversity, Enmity and then Room.

Kittim first names Kition on Cyprus, then widens to mean the seafaring powers out of the west. Numbers 24:24 has ships from the coast of Kittim afflicting Asshur, and Daniel 11:30 has ships of Kittim turn back a king of the north. At 24:28-29 the curse on the Philistines is put into the hands of the sinners of the Gentiles and the Kittim.

stories.keyTakeaway: Esau sells his birthright for red pottage and is called Edom for it. Famine drives Isaac to Gerar, where God tells him not to go down to Egypt; he reaps a hundredfold, re-digs his father's stopped wells and names them after the quarrels, swears to Abimelech, then curses the Philistines.

crossRefs: Genesis 27:46: Rebekah tells Isaac she is weary of her life because of the daughters of Heth, and asks what good her life will be if Jacob takes a wife like them.
Genesis 26:34-35: Esau takes Judith and Basemath, both Hittite women, and they are a grief of mind to Isaac and to Rebekah.
Genesis 28:1-4: Isaac charges Jacob to take no wife of the daughters of Canaan but to go to the house of Bethuel, and blesses him with the blessing of Abraham.
Deuteronomy 7:3-4: Do not make marriages with them, for they will turn your son away from following Me to serve other gods, which is the stated reason for the rule.
Ezra 9:1-2: The people and the priests had taken foreign wives and mixed the holy seed with the peoples of the lands, the breach this chapter is guarding against in advance.

translationNotes.note: At 25:4 Jacob gives his age as nine weeks of years. A week of years is seven, so he is sixty-three. The book counts ages the same way it counts dates, so a reader has to multiply to get the plain number Genesis would simply state.

At 25:4 Jacob says he has not betrothed himself to anyone. Betrothal was not an engagement in the modern sense but a binding legal step: Deuteronomy 22:23-24 treats a betrothed woman as already a wife for purposes of law. The wedding came later, when the man took her into his house.

At 25:14 Rebecca puts both hands on Jacob's head. Laying hands on a head transfers what is being said or given: Genesis 48:14 has Jacob cross his hands over Ephraim and Manasseh, and Leviticus 16:21 has the high priest lay both hands on the goat's head and confess Israel's sins over it before it is sent away.

The same rule is given three times in six chapters, by Abraham at 20:4, by Rebecca here, and by Isaac at 27:9-10. Genesis puts it in the mouth of Abraham at Genesis 24:3 and of Isaac at Genesis 28:1. Deuteronomy 7:3-4 states what is at stake: the foreign spouse turns the child away to other gods.

stories.keyTakeaway: Rebecca tells Jacob to take no wife from the daughters of Canaan but from her father's house. Jacob answers that at nine weeks of years he has touched no woman and has refused Esau's urging for twenty-two years, and he swears it. Rebecca lays both hands on his head and blesses him.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 26
summaryBullets: And in the seventh year of this week Isaac called Esau, his elder Son, and said to him: ' I am [2114 A.M.] old, my son, and behold my eyes are dim in seeing, and I know not the day of my death. (26:1).

And now take your hunting weapons your quiver and your bow, and go out to the field, and hunt and catch me (venison), my son, and make me savoury meat, such as my soul loveth, and bring it to me that I may eat, and that my soul may bless you before I die.' (26:2).
But Rebecca heard Isaac speaking to Esau. (26:3).
And Esau went forth early to the field to hunt and catch and bring home to his father. (26:4).
And Rebecca called Jacob, her son, and said to him: 'Behold, I heard Isaac, your father, speak to Esau, your brother, saying: "Hunt for me, and make me savoury meat, and bring (it) to me that (26:5).

I may eat and bless you before the Lord before I die." And now, my son, obey my voice in that which I command you: Go to your flock and fetch me two good kids of the goats, and I will make them savoury meat for your father, such as he loves, and you will bring (it) to your father that he may eat and bless you before the Lord before he die, and that you mayst be blessed.' (26:6).

And Jacob said to Rebecca his mother: 'Mother, I shall not withhold anything which my father would eat, and which would please him: only I fear, my mother, that he will recognise my voice and wish to touch me. (26:7).

And you know that I am smooth, and Esau, my brother, is hairy, and I shall appear before his eyes as an evildoer, and shall do a deed which he had not commanded me, and he will be wroth with me, and I shall bring upon myself a curse, and not a blessing.' (26:8).
And Rebecca, his mother, said to him: 'Upon me be your curse, my son, only obey my voice.' (26:9).

And Jacob obeyed the voice of Rebecca, his mother, and went and fetched two good and fat kids of the goats, and brought them to his mother, and his mother made them ~savoury meat~ such as he loved. (26:10).

And Rebecca took the goodly rainment of Esau, her elder son, which was with her in the house, and she clothed Jacob, her younger son, (with them), and she put the skins of the kids upon his hands and on the exposed parts of his neck. (26:11).
And she gave the meat and the bread which she had prepared into the hand of her son Jacob. (26:12).
And Jacob went in to his father and said: 'I am your son: I have done according as you badest me: arise and sit and eat of that which I have caught, father, that your soul may bless me.' (26:13).
And Isaac said to his son: 'How have you found so quickly, my son? (26:14).
'And Jacob said: 'Because <the Lord> your God caused me to find.' (26:15).
And Isaac said to him: Come near, that I may feel you, my son, if you are my son Esau or not.' (26:16).
And Jacob went near to Isaac, his father, and he felt him and said: 'The voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau,' (26:17).

and he discerned him not, because it was a dispensation from heaven to remove his power of perception and Isaac discerned not, for his hands were hairy as his brother Esau's, so that he blessed him. (26:18).
And he said: 'Art you my son Esau? ' and he said: 'I am your son': and he said, 'Bring near to me that I may eat of that which you have caught, my son, that my soul may bless you.' (26:19).
And he brought near to him, and he did eat, and he brought him wine and he drank. (26:20).
And Isaac, his father, said to him: 'Come near and kiss me, my son. (26:21).

And he came near and kissed him. And he smelled the smell of his raiment, and he blessed him and said: 'Behold, the smell of my son is as the smell of a <full> field which the Lord has blessed. And may the Lord give you of the dew of heaven And of the dew of the earth, and plenty of corn and oil: Let nations serve you, And peoples bow down to you. Be lord over your brethren, And let your mother's sons bow down to you; And may all the blessings with which the Lord has blessed me and blessed Abraham, my father; Be imparted to you and to your seed for ever: Cursed be he that curseth you, And blessed be he that blesseth you.' And it came to pass as soon as Isaac had made an end of blessing his son Jacob, and Jacob had gone forth from Isaac his father he hid himself and Esau, his brother, came in from his hunting. And he also made savoury meat, and brought (it) to his father, and said to his father: 'Let my father arise, and eat of my venison that your soul may bless me.' And Isaac, his father, said to him: 'Who are you? 'And he said to him: 'I am your first born, your son Esau: I have done as you have commanded me.' And Isaac was very greatly astonished, and said: 'Who is he that has hunted and caught and brought (it) to me, and I have eaten of all before you camest, and have blessed him: (and) he shall be blessed, and all his seed for ever.' And it came to pass when Esau heard the words of his father Isaac that he cried with an exceeding great and bitter cry, and said to his father: 'Bless me, (even) me also, father.' And he said to him: 'Your brother came with guile, and has taken away your blessing.'
