crossRefs: Genesis 27:1-40: Isaac's dim eyes, the savoury meat, the kid skins, the voice of Jacob and the hands of Esau, the blessing given and the bitter cry that comes too late.
Genesis 25:23: Two nations are in your womb, and the elder shall serve the younger, spoken to Rebekah before the twins were born.
Hebrews 11:20: By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning things to come.
Malachi 1:2-3: I loved Jacob and I hated Esau, and I laid his mountains waste, said of the two nations long after the two men.
Obadiah 1:10-14: Edom is charged with standing by while strangers carried Jacob's people off, and with standing at the crossroads to cut down those who escaped.

translationNotes.note: A father's deathbed blessing was treated as an act with force, not a good wish: once spoken it stood and could not be called back, which is why Genesis 27:33 has Isaac say of Jacob that he shall be blessed. That is also why Esau's demand at 26:29-32 cannot simply be answered with a second copy of the same words.

The word means tasty things, dishes made to suit one man's palate. Esau is sent out for wild game; at 26:10 Rebecca substitutes two kids from the flock and cooks them the way Isaac likes, which is the hinge of the whole switch. The deception works through food, clothing and skin rather than through words alone.

At 26:11 Rebecca puts kid skins on Jacob's hands and on the bare part of his neck. The goats of that country are black and coarse-haired, quite unlike sheep, so the hide passes for a hairy man's arm under a blind man's hand. Genesis 25:25 says Esau came out red and hairy all over like a garment.

The name sounds like aqev, heel, and like the verb aqav, to seize the heel and so to trip or cheat. Genesis 25:26 has him born with his hand gripping Esau's heel, and at 26:30 Esau says he now knows why his brother is called Jacob, having supplanted him twice. Hosea 12:3 uses the same play, that he took his brother by the heel in the womb.

In a country with no summer rain the heavy night dew off the sea carries vines and grain through the dry months, so dew in a blessing means the crop will live. At 26:23 Jacob is given the dew of heaven with corn and oil; at 26:33 Esau is set far from it, which places him in the dry country of Seir.

stories.keyTakeaway: Isaac, blind, sends Esau out to hunt the meal he will eat before he blesses him. Rebecca dresses Jacob in Esau's clothes with kid skins on his hands and neck and sends him in first. Isaac blesses him, Esau comes and cries out, and Esau plans to kill his brother once their father dies.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 27
summaryBullets: And the words of Esau, her elder son, were told to Rebecca in a dream, and Rebecca sent and called Jacob her younger son, (27:1).
and said to him: 'Behold Esau your brother will take vengeance on you so as to kill you. (27:2).

Now, therefore, my son, obey my voice, and arise and flee you to Laban, my brother, to Haran, and tarry with him a few days until your brother's anger turns away, and he remove his anger from you, and forget all that you have done; then I will send and fetch you from from there.' (27:3).
And Jacob said: 'I am not afraid; if he wishes to kill me, I will kill him.' (27:4).
But she said to him: 'Let me not be bereft of both my sons on one day.' (27:5).

And Jacob said to Rebecca his mother: 'Behold, you know that my father has become old, and does not see because his eyes are dull, and if I leave him it will be evil in his eyes, because I leave him and go away from you, and my father will be angry, and will curse me. I will not go; when he sends me, then only will I go.' (27:6).
And Rebecca said to Jacob: 'I will go in and speak to him, and he will send you away.' (27:7).

And Rebecca went in and said to Isaac: 'I loathe my life because of the two daughters of Heth, whom Esau has taken him as wives; and if Jacob take a wife from among the daughters of the land such as these, for what purpose do I further live, for the daughters of Canaan are evil.' (27:8).
And Isaac called Jacob and blessed him, and admonished him and said to him: 'Do not take you a wife of any of the daughters of Canaan; (27:9).
arise and go to Mesopotamia, to the house of Bethuel, your mother's father, and take you a wife from from there of the daughters of Laban, your mother's brother. (27:10).

And God Almighty bless you and increase and multiply you that you may become a company of nations, and give you the blessings of my father Abraham, to you and to your seed after you, that you may inherit the land of your sojournings and all the land which God gave to Abraham: go, my son, in peace.' (27:11).
And Isaac sent Jacob away, and he went to Mesopotamia, to Laban the son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebecca, Jacob's mother. (27:12).
And it came to pass after Jacob had arisen to go to Mesopotamia that the spirit of Rebecca was grieved after her son, and she wept. (27:13).
And Isaac said to Rebecca: 'My sister, weep not on account of Jacob, my son; for he goes in peace, and in peace will he return. (27:14).
The Most High God will preserve him from all evil, and will be with him; for He will not forsake him all his days; (27:15).
For I know that his ways will be prospered in all things wherever he goes, until he return in peace to us, and we see him in peace. (27:16).
Fear not on his account, my sister, for he is on the upright path and he is a perfect man: and he is faithful and will not perish. Weep not.' (27:17).
And Isaac comforted Rebecca on account of her son Jacob, and blessed him. (27:18).

And Jacob went from the Well of the Oath to go to Haran on the first year of the second week in the forty-fourth jubilee, and he came to Luz on the mountains, that is, Bethel, on the new moon of the first month of this week, [2115 A.M.] and he came to the place at even and turned from the way to the west of the road that night: and he slept there; for the sun had set. (27:19).
And he took one of the stones of that place and laid <it at his head> under the tree, and he was journeying alone, and he slept. (27:20).

And he dreamt that night, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven, and behold, the angels of the Lord ascended and descended on it: and behold, the Lord stood upon it. (27:21).
And he spoke to Jacob and said: 'I am the Lord God of Abraham, your father, and the God of Isaac; the land whereon you are sleeping, to you will I give it, and to your seed after you. (27:22).

And your seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and you will increase to the west and to the east, to the north and the south, and in you and in your seed shall all the families of the nations be blessed. (27:23).

And behold, I will be with you, and will keep you whithersoever you goest, and I will bring you again into this land in peace; for I will not leave you until I do everything that I told you of.' (27:24).

And Jacob awoke from his sleep, and said, 'Truly this place is the house of the Lord, and I knew it not.' And he was afraid and said: 'Dreadful is this place which is none other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.' (27:25).

And Jacob arose early in the morning, and took the stone which he had put under his head and set it up as a pillar for a sign, and he poured oil upon the top of it. And he called the name of that place Bethel; but the name of the place was Luz at the first. (27:26).

And Jacob vowed a vow to the Lord, saying: 'If the Lord will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and give me bread to eat and raiment to put on, so that I come again to my father's house in peace, then shall the Lord be my God, and this stone which I have set up as a pillar for a sign in this place, shall be the Lord's house, and of all that you givest me, I shall give the tenth to you, my God.' (27:27).
crossRefs: Genesis 28:10-22: Jacob leaves Beersheba for Haran, dreams of the ladder set on the earth with its top in heaven, wakes calling the place the house of God and the gate of heaven, and vows the tenth.
Genesis 27:46: Rebekah tells Isaac she is weary of her life because of the daughters of Heth, which is the reason she gives him for sending Jacob away.
Genesis 31:11-13: The angel of God tells Jacob in a dream, I am the God of Bethel where you anointed a pillar and vowed a vow to Me, now arise and go back to the land of your kindred.
Genesis 35:1-7: God tells Jacob to go up to Bethel and make an altar to the God who appeared to him when he fled from Esau, and he builds it and names the place El-bethel.
John 1:51: You shall see heaven opened and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man, spoken with this ladder in view.

translationNotes.note: Luz was the town's old name; Bethel means house of God, the name Jacob gives the place at 27:26, as at Genesis 28:19. It stands on the central ridge road about ten miles north of Jerusalem. Judges 1:23-26 records the later taking of Luz and repeats that its name was Bethel.

A matsevah is a standing stone set upright to mark a place or an agreement. At 27:26 Jacob sets one up and pours oil on the top of it, as at Genesis 28:18. The law later forbids Israel to raise them, Deuteronomy 16:22, because the surrounding cults used standing stones for their own gods.

The word appears only once in the Hebrew Bible, at Genesis 28:12, and it means a stairway or ramp rather than a portable ladder. The angels are going up as well as coming down, so the traffic starts at the earth end too. At 27:21 the Lord stands at the top of it.

A neder is a conditional vow: if God does this, then I will do that, and once the condition is met it binds. Deuteronomy 23:21-23 warns that God will require it of you, and that choosing not to vow is no sin at all. At 27:27 Jacob promises a tenth of everything, which matches the tithe this book makes a standing ordinance at 13:25-27.

stories.keyTakeaway: Rebecca learns of Esau's threat and sends Jacob to Laban at Haran, and Isaac charges him to take no Canaanite wife and blesses him. At Luz he sleeps with a stone under his head, sees a ladder with angels going up and down, sets the stone up as a pillar with oil on it, and vows a tenth.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 28
summaryBullets: And he went on his journey, and came to the land of the east, to Laban, the brother of Rebecca, and he was with him, and served him for Rachel his daughter one week. (28:1).
And in the first year of the third week [2122 A.M.] he said to him: 'Give me my wife, for whom I have served you seven years '; and Laban said to Jacob: 'I will give you your wife.' (28:2).

And Laban made a feast, and took Leah his elder daughter, and gave (her) to Jacob as a wife, and gave her Zilpah his handmaid for an hand- maid; and Jacob did not know, for he thought that she was Rachel. (28:3).

And he went in to her, and behold, she was Leah; and Jacob was angry with Laban, and said to him: 'Why have you dealt thus with me? Did not I serve you for Rachel and not for Leah? Why have you wronged me? (28:4).

Take your daughter, and I will go; for you have done evil to me.' For Jacob loved Rachel more than Leah; for Leah's eyes were weak, but her form was very handsome; but Rachel had beautiful eyes and a beautiful and very handsome form. (28:5).

And Laban said to Jacob: 'It is not so done in our country, to give the younger before the elder.' And it is not right to do this; for thus it is ordained and written in the heavenly tablets, that no one should give his younger daughter before the elder; but the elder, one gives first and after her the younger -and the man who does so, they set down guilt against him in heaven, and none is righteous that does this thing, for this deed is evil before the Lord. (28:6).
And command you the children of Israel that they do not this thing; let them neither take nor give the younger before they have given the elder, for it is very wicked. (28:7).

And Laban said to Jacob: 'Let the seven days of the feast of this one pass by, and I shall give you Rachel, that you mayst serve me another seven years, that you mayst pasture my sheep as you didst in the former week.' (28:8).

And on the day when the seven days of the feast of Leah had passed, Laban gave Rachel to Jacob, that he might serve him another seven years, and he gave to Rachel Bilhah, the sister of Zilpah, as a handmaid. (28:9).
And he served yet other seven years for Rachel, for Leah had been given to him for nothing. (28:10).

And the Lord opened the womb of Leah, and she conceived and bare Jacob a son, and he called his name Reuben, on the fourteenth day of the ninth month, in the first year of the third week. [2122 A.M.] (28:11).
But the womb of Rachel was closed, for the Lord saw that Leah was hated and Rachel loved. (28:12).

And again Jacob went in to Leah, and she conceived, and bare Jacob a second son, and he called his name Simeon, on the twenty-first of the tenth month, and in the third year of this week. [2124 A.M.] (28:13).
And again Jacob went in to Leah, and she conceived, and bare him a third son, and he called his name Levi, in the new moon of the first month in the sixth year of this week. [2127 A.M.] (28:14).

And again Jacob went in to her, and she conceived, and bare him a fourth son, and he called his name Judah, on the fifteenth of the third month, in the first year of the fourth week. [2129 A.M.] (28:15).

And on account of all this Rachel envied Leah, for she did not bear, and she said to Jacob: 'Give me children'; and Jacob said: 'Have I withheld from you the fruits of your womb? Have I forsaken you?' (28:16).

And when Rachel saw that Leah had borne four sons to Jacob, Reuben and Simeon and Levi and Judah, she said to him: 'Go in to Bilhah my handmaid, and she will conceive, and bear a son to me.' (And she gave (him) Bilhah her handmaid to wife). (28:17).
And he went in to her, and she conceived, and bare him a son, and he called his name Dan, on the ninth of the sixth month, in the sixth year of the third week. [2127 A.M.] (28:18).

And Jacob went in again to Bilhah a second time, and she conceived, and bare Jacob another son, and Rachel called his name Napthali, on the fifth of the seventh month, in the second year of the fourth week. [2130 A.M.] (28:19).

And when Leah saw that she had become sterile and did not bear, she envied Rachel, and she also gave her handmaid Zilpah to Jacob to wife, and she conceived, and bare a son, and Leah called his name Gad, on the twelfth of the eighth month, in the third year of the fourth week. [2131 A.M.] (28:20).

And he went in again to her, and she conceived, and bare him a second son, and Leah called his name Asher, on the second of the eleventh month, in the fifth year of the fourth week. [2133 A.M.] (28:21).

And Jacob went in to Leah, and she conceived, and bare a son, and she called his name Issachar, on the fourth of the fifth month, in the fourth year of the fourth week,[2132 A.M.] and she gave him to a nurse. (28:22).

And Jacob went in again to her, and she conceived, and bare two (children), a son and a daughter, and she called the name of the son Zabulon, and the name of the daughter Dinah, in the seventh of the seventh month, in the sixth year of the fourth week. [2134 A.M.] (28:23).

And the Lord was gracious to Rachel, and opened her womb, and she conceived, and bare a son, and she called his name Joseph, on the new moon of the fourth month, in the sixth year in this fourth week. [2134 A.M.] (28:24).

And in the days when Joseph was born, Jacob said to Laban: 'Give me my wives and sons, and let me go to my father Isaac, and let me make me an house; for I have completed the years in which I have served you for your two daughters, and I will go to the house of my father.' (28:25).
And Laban said to Jacob: 'Tarry with me for your wages, and pasture my flock for me again, and take your wages.' (28:26).
And they agreed with one another that he should give him as his wages those of the lambs and kids which were born black and spotted and white, (these) were to be his wages. (28:27).

And all the sheep brought forth spotted and speckled and black, variously marked, and they brought forth again lambs like themselves, and all that were spotted were Jacob's and those which were not were Laban's. (28:28).
And Jacob's possessions multiplied exceedingly, and he possessed oxen and sheep and asses and camels, and menservants and maid-servants. (28:29).
And Laban and his sons envied Jacob, and Laban took back his sheep from him, and he observed him with evil intent. (28:30).
crossRefs: Genesis 29:15-30: Jacob serves seven years for Rachel, Laban gives him Leah in the dark, and he serves another seven for Rachel after the week of the wedding feast.
Genesis 30:25-43: Jacob asks for the speckled and spotted among the flocks as his wages, and his own flocks increase greatly while Laban's do not.
Genesis 35:23-26: The twelve sons of Jacob listed by mother, Leah's six, Rachel's two, and the four born to Bilhah and Zilpah.
Leviticus 18:18: You shall not take a woman as a rival to her sister while her sister is still living, the law that later forbids the very household this chapter describes.
Deuteronomy 21:15-17: If a man has two wives, one loved and one unloved, he may not give the firstborn's portion to the son of the loved one, a case built on exactly this kind of family.

translationNotes.note: At 28:8 Laban tells Jacob to let the seven days of Leah's feast run out before he takes Rachel, as at Genesis 29:27. A wedding ran seven days of feasting, which is why the riddle at Judges 14:12-17 comes with a seven-day deadline. The bride was veiled and brought at night, which is what makes the substitution at 28:3-4 possible.

At 28:6-7 the book takes Laban's local custom and makes it a rule written on the heavenly tablets and binding on Israel: no one may give the younger daughter before the elder. Genesis 29:26 has Laban say only that it is not done so in our country. This is the book turning a reported custom into law.

A shifchah is a female slave attached to her mistress and counted as her property; Zilpah and Bilhah come with Leah and Rachel at 28:3 and 28:9. A child born to the handmaid at the wife's direction was reckoned the wife's, which is why Rachel says at 28:17 that Bilhah will bear a son to her. The same arrangement stands behind Hagar at Genesis 16:2.

At 28:11-24 every child gets a day and a month: Reuben on the fourteenth of the ninth month, Levi on the new moon of the first, Judah on the fifteenth of the third, Joseph on the new moon of the fourth. Genesis 30:1-24 records the same births in the same order with no dates at all. The dating is this book's own work.

Sheep in that country run white and goats run black, so marked animals are the minority in any flock, which is what makes the bargain at 28:27 look safe from Laban's side. Genesis 30:32-43 tells the same arrangement, and Genesis 31:7 has Jacob say Laban changed his wages ten times.

stories.keyTakeaway: Jacob serves seven years for Rachel and is given Leah, and the book turns the rule against giving a younger daughter before the elder into a law on the heavenly tablets. He serves seven more, eleven sons and a daughter are born, each dated to a day and month, and his wages become the marked flock.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 29
summaryBullets: And it came to pass when Rachel had borne Joseph, that Laban went to shear his sheep; for they were distant from him a three days' journey. (29:1).
And Jacob saw that Laban was going to shear his sheep, and Jacob called Leah and Rachel, and spoke kindly to them that they should come with him to the land of Canaan. (29:2).

For he told them how he had seen everything in a dream, even all that He had spoken to him that he should return to his father's house, and they said: 'To every place where you goest we will go with you.' (29:3).

And Jacob blessed the God of Isaac his father, and the God of Abraham his father's father, and he arose and mounted his wives and his children, and took all his possessions and crossed the river, and came to the land of Gilead, and Jacob hid his intention from Laban and told him not. (29:4).

And in the seventh year of the fourth week Jacob turned (his face) toward Gilead in the first month, on the twenty-first thereof. [2135 A.M.] And Laban pursued after him and overtook Jacob in the mountain of Gilead in the third month, on the thirteenth thereof. (29:5).
And the Lord did not suffer him to injure Jacob; for he appeared to him in a dream by night. And Laban spoke to Jacob. (29:6).

And on the fifteenth of those days Jacob made a feast for Laban, and for all who came with him, and Jacob sware to Laban that day, and Laban also to Jacob, that neither should cross the mountain of Gilead to the other with evil purpose. (29:7).
And he made there a heap for a witness; wherefore the name of that place is called: 'The Heap of Witness,' after this heap. (29:8).

But before they used to call the land of Gilead the land of the Rephaim; for it was the land of the Rephaim, and the Rephaim were born (there), giants whose height was ten, nine, eight down to seven cubits. (29:9).
And their habitation was from the land of the children of Ammon to Mount Hermon, and the seats of their kingdom were Karnaim and Ashtaroth, and Edrei, and Misur, and Beon. (29:10).

And the Lord destroyed them because of the evil of their deeds; for they were very malignant, and the Amorites dwelt in their stead, wicked and sinful, and there is no people to-day which has wrought to the full all their sins, and they have no longer length of life on the earth. (29:11).
And Jacob sent away Laban, and he departed into Mesopotamia, the land of the East, and Jacob returned to the land of Gilead. (29:12).

And he passed over the Jabbok in the ninth month, on the eleventh thereof. And on that day Esau, his brother, came to him, and he was reconciled to him, and departed from him to the land of Seir, but Jacob dwelt in tents. (29:13).

And in the first year of the fifth week in this jubilee [2136 A.M.] he crossed the Jordan, and dwelt beyond the Jordan, and he pastured his sheep from the sea of the heap to Bethshan, and to Dothan and to the forest of Akrabbim. (29:14).
And he sent to his father Isaac of all his substance, clothing, and food, and meat, and drink, and milk, and butter, and cheese, and some dates of the valley. (29:15).

And to his mother Rebecca also four times a year, between the times of the months, between ploughing and reaping, and between autumn and the rain (season) and between winter and spring, to the tower of Abraham. (29:16).
For Isaac had returned from the Well of the Oath and gone up to the tower of his father Abraham, and he dwelt there apart from his son Esau. (29:17).

For in the days when Jacob went to Mesopotamia, Esau took to himself a wife Mahalath, the daughter of Ishmael, and he gathered together all the flocks of his father and his wives, and went Up and dwelt on Mount Seir, and left Isaac his father at the Well of the Oath alone. (29:18).
And Isaac went up from the Well of the Oath and dwelt in the tower of Abraham his father on the mountains of Hebron, (29:19).
And there Jacob sent all that he did send to his father and his mother from time to time, all they needed, and they blessed Jacob with all their heart and with all their soul. (29:20).
crossRefs: Genesis 31:17-55: Jacob leaves while Laban is shearing, Laban overtakes him in the mountain of Gilead, and they raise a heap of stones as a witness and swear not to pass it to do harm.
Deuteronomy 3:11: Og king of Bashan was left of the remnant of the Rephaim, and his iron bedstead measured nine cubits by four, the scale this chapter puts on the whole people.
Joshua 12:4-5: Og of Bashan, of the remnant of the Rephaim, dwelt at Ashtaroth and at Edrei and ruled Mount Hermon and Salecah, the towns this chapter names as their seats.
Genesis 32:22-32: Jacob crosses the ford of the Jabbok, wrestles until daybreak, is renamed Israel, and calls the place Peniel.
Genesis 33:1-16: Esau runs to meet Jacob and embraces him, and afterwards Esau goes back to Seir while Jacob travels on.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: גַּלְעֵד (Gal'ed) - Aramaic: יְגַר שָׂהֲדוּתָא (Yegar Sahaduta)
translationNotes.note: Genesis 31:47 has Laban name the heap in Aramaic and Jacob name it in Hebrew, both phrases meaning heap of witness, and the name Gilead is heard in the Hebrew one. A pile of stones was a legal marker standing at the border, and at 29:7-8 both men swear not to pass it against the other.

A people of the country east of the Jordan, remembered for their size. Deuteronomy 3:11 says Og king of Bashan was the last of them and gives his iron bedstead as nine cubits by four, about thirteen and a half feet by six. At 29:9 the book puts their height at ten cubits down to seven, roughly fifteen feet down to ten. Genesis 14:5 places them at Ashteroth-karnaim.

Three towns of Bashan, the high grazing plateau east of the Sea of Galilee. Ashtaroth carries the name of the goddess Ashtoreth. Joshua 12:4 says Og dwelt at Ashtaroth and Edrei, Deuteronomy 3:1 has the battle with Og fought at Edrei, and Amos 6:13 mocks those who boast in Karnaim.

A river running west into the Jordan through a deep gorge, the modern Zarqa, and a natural boundary line across the country east of the river. Genesis 32:22 has Jacob send his household over the ford of the Jabbok and stay behind alone. At 29:13 the crossing is dated to the eleventh of the ninth month.

A migdal is a tower, and in farming country it meant a fortified building for storing the crop and watching the land, as in the vineyard of Isaiah 5:2. At 29:17-19 Isaac leaves Beersheba and lives in Abraham's tower on the hills of Hebron, and Jacob sends supplies four times a year, between ploughing and reaping, between harvest and the rains, and between winter and spring. Genesis records no such tower.

stories.keyTakeaway: Jacob leaves while Laban is shearing, and Laban overtakes him in Gilead; they swear not to cross the heap of witness against one another. The chapter says Gilead had been the land of the Rephaim, giants of seven to ten cubits. Jacob crosses the Jabbok, meets Esau, and sends food to Isaac.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 30
summaryBullets: And in the first year of the sixth week [2143 A.M.] he went up to Salem, to the east of Shechem, in peace, in the fourth month. (30:1).

And there they carried off Dinah, the daughter of Jacob, into the house of Shechem, the son of Hamor, the Hivite, the prince of the land, and he lay with her and defiled her, and she was a little girl, a child of twelve years. (30:2).

And he besought his father and her brothers that she might be given to him to wife. And Jacob and his sons were wroth because of the men of Shechem; for they had defiled Dinah, their sister, and they spoke to them with evil intent and dealt deceitfully with them and beguiled them. (30:3).

And Simeon and Levi came unexpectedly to Shechem and executed judgment on all the men of Shechem, and slew all the men whom they found in it, and left not a single one remaining in it: they slew all in torments because they had dishonoured their sister Dinah. (30:4).

And thus let it not again be done from henceforth that a daughter of Israel be defiled; for judgment is ordained in heaven against them that they should destroy with the sword all the men of the Shechemites because they had wrought shame in Israel. (30:5).

And the Lord delivered them into the hands of the sons of Jacob that they might exterminate them with the sword and execute judgment upon them, and that it might not thus again be done in Israel that a virgin of Israel should be defiled. (30:6).

And if there is any man who wishes in Israel to give his daughter or his sister to any man who is of the seed of the Gentiles he shall surely die, and they shall stone him with stones; for he has wrought shame in Israel; and they shall burn the woman with fire, because she has dishonoured the name of the house of her father, and she shall be rooted out of Israel. (30:7).

And let not an adulteress and no uncleanness be found in Israel throughout all the days of the generations of the earth; for Israel is holy to the Lord, and every man who has defiled (it) shall surely die: they shall stone him with stones. (30:8).
For thus has it been ordained and written in the heavenly tablets regarding all the seed of Israel: he who defileth (it) shall surely die, and he shall be stoned with stones. (30:9).

And to this law there is no limit of days, and no remission, nor any atonement: but the man who has defiled his daughter shall be rooted out in the midst of all Israel, because he has given of his seed to Moloch, and wrought impiously so as to defile it. (30:10).

And do you, Moses, command the children of Israel and exhort them not to give their daughters to the Gentiles, and not to take for their sons any of the daughters of the Gentiles, for this is abominable before the Lord. (30:11).

For this reason I have written for you in the words of the Law all the deeds of the Shechemites, which they wrought against Dinah, and how the sons of Jacob spoke, saying: 'We will not give our daughter to a man who is uncircumcised; for that were a reproach to us.' (30:12).
And it is a reproach to Israel, to those who live, and to those that take the daughters of the Gentiles; for this is unclean and abominable to Israel. (30:13).
And Israel will not be free from this uncleanness if it has a wife of the daughters of the Gentiles, or has given any of its daughters to a man who is of any of the Gentiles. (30:14).

For there will be plague upon plague, and curse upon curse, and every judgment and plague and curse will come upon him : if he do this thing, or hide his eyes from those who commit uncleanness, or those who defile the sanctuary of the Lord, or those who profane His holy name, (then) will the whole nation together be judged for all the uncleanness and profanation of this man. (30:15).

And there will be no respect of persons [and no consideration of persons] and no receiving at his hands of fruits and offerings and burnt-offerings and fat, nor the fragrance of sweet savour, so as to accept it: and so fare every man or woman in Israel who defiles the sanctuary. (30:16).

For this reason I have commanded you, saying: 'Testify this testimony to Israel: see how the Shechemites fared and their sons: how they were delivered into the hands of two sons of Jacob, and they slew them under tortures, and it was (reckoned) to them for righteousness, and it is written down to them for righteousness. (30:17).

And the seed of Levi was chosen for the priesthood, and to be Levites, that they might minister before the Lord, as we, continually, and that Levi and his sons may be blessed for ever; for he was zealous to execute righteousness and judgment and vengeance on all those who arose against Israel. (30:18).
And so they inscribe as a testimony in his favour on the heavenly tablets blessing and righteousness before the God of all: (30:19).

And we remember the righteousness which the man fulfilled during his life, at all periods of the year; until a thousand generations they will record it, and it will come to him and to his descendants after him, and he has been recorded on the heavenly tablets as a friend and a righteous man. (30:20).

All this account I have written for you, and have commanded you to say to the children of Israel, that they should not commit sin nor transgress the ordinances nor break the covenant which has been ordained for them, (but) that they should fulfil it and be recorded as friends. (30:21).

But if they transgress and work uncleanness in every way, they will be recorded on the heavenly tablets as adversaries, and they will be destroyed out of the book of life, and they will be recorded in the book of those who will be destroyed and with those who will be rooted out of the earth. (30:22).

And on the day when the sons of Jacob slew Shechem a writing was recorded in their favour in heaven that they had executed righteousness and uprightness and vengeance on the sinners, and it was written for a blessing. (30:23).

And they brought Dinah, their sister, out of the house of Shechem, and they took captive everything that was in Shechem, their sheep and their oxen and their asses, and all their wealth, and all their flocks, and brought them all to Jacob their father. (30:24).
And he reproached them because they had put the city to the sword for he feared those who dwelt in the land, the Canaanites and the Perizzites. (30:25).
And the dread of the Lord was upon all the cities which are around about Shechem, and they did not rise to pursue after the sons of Jacob; for terror had fallen upon them. (30:26).
crossRefs: Genesis 34:1-31: Dinah goes out to see the daughters of the land, Shechem takes her, the sons of Jacob answer with a deceit about circumcision, and Simeon and Levi kill the men of the city.
Genesis 49:5-7: Jacob curses the anger of Simeon and Levi for what they did at Shechem and says he will divide them in Jacob and scatter them in Israel.
Leviticus 18:21: You shall not give any of your seed to pass through the fire to Molech, the charge this chapter turns on a man who gives his daughter to a Gentile.
Numbers 25:6-13: Phinehas runs a spear through the Israelite and the Midianite woman, and it is counted to him for righteousness and he is given a covenant of an everlasting priesthood.
Malachi 2:4-7: The covenant with Levi was one of life and peace, and the priest's lips are to keep knowledge because he is the messenger of the LORD of hosts.

translationNotes.note: The god to whom children were burned. Leviticus 18:21 and Leviticus 20:2-5 forbid giving seed to Molech and set death for it. Jeremiah 7:31 says they built the high places of Topheth in the valley of the son of Hinnom to burn their sons and daughters in the fire, a thing God never commanded. The Greek name of that valley is Gehenna, the word used for hell in the Gospels. At 30:10 the book applies the same charge to a man who hands his daughter to a Gentile.

At 30:18 the book says the seed of Levi was chosen for the priesthood because Levi was zealous to execute judgment on those who rose against Israel, which makes the killing at Shechem the reason for the office. Genesis 34:30 has Jacob rebuke Simeon and Levi for it, and Genesis 49:5-7 has him curse their anger and scatter them. Numbers 25:11-13 gives a covenant of priesthood to Phinehas for an act of the same kind.

At 30:2 Dinah's age is given as twelve. Genesis 34:1-2 gives no age at all. Twelve was around the age at which a girl could be betrothed in that world, so the number is the book closing an outline that Genesis leaves open.

At 30:22 those who break the covenant are struck out of the book of life and written instead in the book of those who will be destroyed. Exodus 32:32-33 has Moses ask to be blotted out of God's book, Psalm 69:28 asks that the wicked be blotted out of the book of the living, and Revelation 20:15 has anyone not found written in the book of life cast into the lake of fire.

One of the peoples of Canaan, listed at Genesis 10:17 and Exodus 3:8. Hamor and Shechem are called Hivites at Genesis 34:2, and the Gibeonites who trick Joshua into a treaty are Hivites too, Joshua 9:7. Shechem itself is the town in the pass between Ebal and Gerizim on the main north-south road.

stories.keyTakeaway: Dinah is carried into Shechem's house and defiled at twelve years old, and Simeon and Levi kill every man in the town. The chapter turns it into law: no daughter of Israel is to be given to a Gentile, on pain of stoning and burning, and it says Levi's seed was chosen for the priesthood for this.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 31
summaryBullets: And on the new moon of the month Jacob spoke to all the people of his house. saying: 'Purify yourselves and change your garments, and let us arise and go up to Bethel, where I vowed a vow to Him on the day when I fled from the face of Esau my brother, because he has been with me and brought me into this land in peace, and put you away the strange gods that arc among you.' (31:1).

And they gave up the strange gods and that which was in their ears and which was on their necks and the idols which Rachel stole from Laban her father she gave wholly to Jacob. And he burnt and brake them to pieces and destroyed them, and hid them under an oak which is in the land of Shechem. (31:2).

And he went up on the new moon of the seventh month to Bethel. And he built an altar at the place where he had slept, and he set up a pillar there, and he sent word to his father Isaac to come to him to his sacrifice, and to his mother Rebecca. (31:3).
And Isaac said: 'Let my son Jacob come, and let me see him before I die.' (31:4).

And Jacob went to his father Isaac and to his mother Rebecca, to the house of his father Abraham, and he took two of his sons with him, Levi and Judah, and he came to his father Isaac and to his mother Rebecca. (31:5).
And Rebecca came forth from the tower to the front of it to kiss Jacob and embrace him; for her spirit had revived when she heard: 'Behold Jacob your son has come'; and she kissed him. (31:6).

And she saw his two sons, and she recognised them, and said to him: 'Are these your sons, my son?' and she embraced them and kissed them, and blessed them, saying: 'In you shall the seed of Abraham become illustrious, and you will prove a blessing on the earth.' (31:7).

And Jacob went in to Isaac his father, to the chamber where he lay, and his two sons were with him, and he took the hand of his father, and stooping down he kissed him, and Isaac clung to the neck of Jacob his son, and wept upon his neck. (31:8).
And the darkness left the eyes of Isaac, and he saw the two sons of Jacob, Levi, and Judah, and he said: 'Are these your sons, my son? for they are like you.' (31:9).
And he said to him that they were truly his sons: 'And you have truly seen that they are truly my sons'. (31:10).
And they came near to him, and he turned and kissed them and embraced them both together. (31:11).
And the spirit of prophecy came down into his mouth, and he took Levi by his right hand and Judah by his left. (31:12).
And he turned to Levi first, and began to bless him first, and said to him: May the God of all, the very Lord of all the ages, bless you and your children throughout all the ages. (31:13).

And may the Lord give to you and to your seed greatness and great glory, and cause you and your seed, from among all flesh, to approach Him to serve in His sanctuary as the angels of the presence and as the holy ones. (Even) as they, shall the seed of your sons be for glory and greatness and holiness, and may He make them great to all the ages. (31:14).

And they shall be judges and princes, and chiefs of all the seed of the sons of Jacob; They shall speak the word of the Lord in righteousness, And they shall judge all His judgments in righteousness. And they shall declare My ways to Jacob And My paths to Israel. The blessing of the Lord shall be given in their mouths To bless all the seed of the beloved. Your mother has called your name Levi, And justly has she called your name; You will be joined to the Lord And be the companion of all the sons of Jacob; Let His table be yours, And do you and your sons eat thereof; And may your table be full to all generations, And your food fail not to all the ages. And let all who hate you fall down before you, And let all your adversaries be rooted out and perish; And blessed be he that blesses you, And cursed be every nation that curses you.' And to Judah he said: 'May the Lord give you strength and power To tread down all that hate you; A prince shalt you be, you and one of your sons, over the sons of Jacob; May your name and the name of your sons go forth and traverse every land and region. Then shall the Gentiles fear before your face, And all the nations shall quake [And all the peoples shall quake]. In you shall be the help of Jacob, And in you be found the salvation of Israel. And when you sittest on the throne of honour of your righteousness There shall be great peace for all the seed of the sons of the beloved; Blessed be he that blesseth you, And all that hate you and afflict you and curse you Shall be rooted out and destroyed from the earth and be accursed.' And turning he kissed him again and embraced him, and rejoiced greatly; for he had seen the sons of Jacob his son in very truth. And he went forth from between his feet and fell down and bowed down to him, and he blessed them and rested there with Isaac his father that night, and they eat and drank with joy. And he made the two sons of Jacob sleep, the one on his right hand and the other on his left, and it was counted to him for righteousness. And Jacob told his father everything during the night, how the Lord had shown him great mercy, and how he had prospered (him in) all his ways, and protected him from all evil. And Isaac blessed the God of his father Abraham, who had not withdrawn his mercy and his righteousness from the sons of his servant Isaac. And in the morning Jacob told his father Isaac the vow which he had vowed to the Lord, and the vision which he had seen, and that he had built an altar, and that everything was ready for the sacrifice to be made before the Lord as he had vowed, and that he had come to set him on an ass. And Isaac said to Jacob his son: 'I am not able to go with you; for I am old and not able to bear the way: go, my son, in peace; for I am one hundred and sixty-five years this day; I am no longer able to journey; set your mother (on an ass) and let her go with you. And I know, my son, that you have come on my account, and may this day be blessed on which you have seen me alive, and I also have seen you, my son. Mayest you prosper and fulfil the vow which you have vowed; and put not off your vow; for you will be called to account as touching the vow; now therefore make haste to perform it, and may He be pleased who has made all things, to whom you have vowed the vow.' And he said to Rebecca: 'Go with Jacob your son'; and Rebecca went with Jacob her son, and Deborah with her, and they came to Bethel. And Jacob remembered the prayer with which his father had blessed him and his two sons, Levi and Judah, and he rejoiced and blessed the God of his fathers, Abraham and Isaac. And he said: 'Now I know that I have an eternal hope, and my sons also, before the God of all'; and thus is it ordained concerning the two; and they record it as an eternal testimony to them on the heavenly tablets how Isaac blessed them. (31:15).

And Isaac said to Jacob his son: 'I am not able to go with you; for I am old and not able to bear the way: go, my son, in peace; for I am one hundred and sixty-five years this day; I am no longer able to journey; set your mother (on an ass) and let her go with you. And I know, my son, that you have come on my account, and may this day be blessed on which you have seen me alive, and I also have seen you, my son. Mayest you prosper and fulfil the vow which you have vowed; and put not off your vow; for you will be called to account as touching the vow; now therefore make haste to perform it, and may He be pleased who has made all things, to whom you have vowed the vow.' And he said to Rebecca: 'Go with Jacob your son'; and Rebecca went with Jacob her son, and Deborah with her, and they came to Bethel. And Jacob remembered the prayer with which his father had blessed him and his two sons, Levi and Judah, and he rejoiced and blessed the God of his fathers, Abraham and Isaac. And he said: 'Now I know that I have an eternal hope, and my sons also, before the God of all'; and thus is it ordained concerning the two; and they record it as an eternal testimony to them on the heavenly tablets how Isaac blessed them. (31:18).

In you shall be the help of Jacob, And in you be found the salvation of Israel. And when you sittest on the throne of honour of your righteousness There shall be great peace for all the seed of the sons of the beloved; Blessed be he that blesseth you, And all that hate you and afflict you and curse you Shall be rooted out and destroyed from the earth and be accursed.' And turning he kissed him again and embraced him, and rejoiced greatly; for he had seen the sons of Jacob his son in very truth. And he went forth from between his feet and fell down and bowed down to him, and he blessed them and rested there with Isaac his father that night, and they eat and drank with joy. And he made the two sons of Jacob sleep, the one on his right hand and the other on his left, and it was counted to him for righteousness. crossRefs: Genesis 35:1-5: Jacob tells his household to put away the strange gods and change their garments before going up to Bethel, and hides them under the oak by Shechem.
Genesis 31:19: Rachel steals her father's household images when Jacob leaves Padan-aram, which is where this chapter says the buried idols came from.
Deuteronomy 33:8-11: The blessing of Moses on Levi, who teaches Jacob God's judgments and puts incense before Him, the office Isaac hands him here.
Numbers 18:1-7: Aaron and his sons are given charge of the sanctuary and the altar, and the priesthood is described as a service given as a gift.
Genesis 49:8-10: Judah, your brothers shall praise you, and the sceptre shall not depart from Judah, the rule this chapter gives him a generation early.

translationNotes.term: The strange gods and the earrings
translationNotes.note: At 31:2 the household gives up strange gods and what was in their ears and on their necks. Genesis 35:4 has the same two things, foreign gods and the rings in their ears, buried under the oak by Shechem. Genesis 31:19 says Rachel had stolen her father's teraphim, household images used for divination, which this chapter names as part of the pile.

translationNotes.term: The right hand and the left
translationNotes.note: At 31:12 Isaac takes Levi by his right hand and Judah by his left. The right hand carried the greater blessing, which is why Genesis 48:14 makes a point of Jacob crossing his hands to lay the right on the younger boy. Putting Levi at the right sets the priesthood above the throne in this chapter's ordering.

At 31:12 the spirit of prophecy comes down into Isaac's mouth before he speaks, and the book uses the same picture at 25:14 when the spirit of righteousness descends into Rebecca's mouth. Numbers 11:25 has the spirit rest on the seventy elders so that they prophesy. Genesis says nothing of the kind about Isaac.

At 31:16 the blessing plays on the name: your mother called your name Levi, and justly, for you shall be joined to the Lord. The verb lavah means to join or attach. Genesis 29:34 uses the same play when Leah names him, saying now my husband will be joined to me, and Numbers 18:2 uses it again of the Levites joined to Aaron for the service.

At 31:16 Levi is told to eat from the Lord's own table, which is how priests were fed. Numbers 18:8-20 gives them portions of the offerings instead of land and says the LORD Himself is their inheritance. Deuteronomy 18:1-2 repeats it: the priests and Levites have no portion among their brothers, for the offerings made by fire are their portion.

stories.keyTakeaway: Jacob has his household give up the strange gods and the rings in their ears, and buries them under an oak at Shechem before going up to Bethel. Isaac's blindness lifts when he sees Levi and Judah; he takes Levi by the right hand and Judah by the left and blesses the priesthood and the rule.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 32
summaryBullets: And he abode that night at Bethel, and Levi dreamed that they had ordained and made him the priest of the Most High God, him and his sons for ever; and he awoke from his sleep and blessed the Lord. (32:1).

And Jacob rose early in the morning, on the fourteenth of this month, and he gave a tithe of all that came with him, both of men and cattle, both of gold and every vessel and garment, yea, he gave tithes of all. (32:2).

And in those days Rachel became pregnant with her son Benjamin. And Jacob counted his sons from him upwards and Levi fell to the portion of the Lord, and his father clothed him in the garments of the priesthood and filled his hands. (32:3).

And on the fifteenth of this month, he brought to the altar fourteen oxen from amongst the cattle, and twenty-eight rams, and forty-nine sheep, and seven lambs, and twenty-one kids of the goats as a burnt-offering on the altar of sacrifice, well pleasing for a sweet savour before God. (32:4).
This was his offering, in consequence of the vow which he had vowed that he would give a tenth, with their fruit-offerings and their drink- offerings. (32:5).

And when the fire had consumed it, he burnt incense on the fire over the fire, and for a thank-offering two oxen and four rams and four sheep, four he-goats, and two sheep of a year old, and two kids of the goats; and thus he did daily for seven days. (32:6).

And he and all his sons and his men were eating (this) with joy there during seven days and blessing and thanking the Lord, who had delivered him out of all his tribulation and had given him his vow. (32:7).
And he tithed all the clean animals, and made a burnt sacrifice, but the unclean animals he gave (not) to Levi his son, and he gave him all the souls of the men. (32:8).

And Levi discharged the priestly office at Bethel before Jacob his father in preference to his ten brothers, and he was a priest there, and Jacob gave his vow: thus he tithed again the tithe to the Lord and sanctified it, and it became holy to Him. (32:9).

And for this reason it is ordained on the heavenly tablets as a law for the tithing again the tithe to eat before the Lord from year to year, in the place where it is chosen that His name should dwell, and to this law there is no limit of days for ever. (32:10).

This ordinance is written that it may be fulfilled from year to year in eating the second tithe before the Lord in the place where it has been chosen, and nothing shall remain over from it from this year to the year following. (32:11).
For in its year shall the seed be eaten till the days of the gathering of the seed of the year, and the wine till the days of the wine, and the oil till the days of its season. (32:12).
And all that is left thereof and becomes old, let it be regarded as polluted: let it be burnt with fire, for it is unclean. (32:13).
And thus let them eat it together in the sanctuary, and let them not suffer it to become old. (32:14).

And all the tithes of the oxen and sheep shall be holy to the Lord, and shall belong to his priests, which they will eat before Him from year to year; for thus is it ordained and engraven regarding the tithe on the heavenly tablets. (32:15).

And on the following night, on the twenty-second day of this month, Jacob resolved to build that place, and to surround the court with a wall, and to sanctify it and make it holy for ever, for himself and his children after him. (32:16).
And the Lord appeared to him by night and blessed him and said to him: 'Your name shall not be called Jacob, but Israel shall they name your name.' (32:17).

And He said to him again: 'I am the Lord who created the heaven and the earth, and I will increase you and multiply you exceedingly, and kings shall come forth from you, and they shall judge everywhere wherever the foot of the sons of men has trodden. (32:18).

And I will give to your seed all the earth which is under heaven, and they shall judge all the nations according to their desires, and after that they shall get possession of the whole earth and inherit it for ever.' (32:19).
And He finished speaking with him, and He went up from him. and Jacob looked till He had ascended into heaven. (32:20).

And he saw in a vision of the night, and behold an angel descended from heaven with seven tablets in his hands, and he gave them to Jacob, and he read them and knew all that was written therein which would befall him and his sons throughout all the ages. (32:21).

And he showed him all that was written on the tablets, and said to him: 'Do not build this place, and do not make it an eternal sanctuary, and do not dwell here; for this is not the place. Go to the house of Abraham your father and dwell with Isaac your father until the day of the death of your father. (32:22).
For in Egypt you will die in peace, and in this land you will be buried with honour in the sepulchre of your fathers, with Abraham and Isaac. (32:23).
Fear not, for as you have seen and read it, thus shall it all be; and do you write down everything as you have seen and read.' (32:24).
And Jacob said: 'Lord, how can I remember all that I have read and seen? 'And he said to him: 'I will bring all things to your remembrance.' (32:25).
And he went up from him, and he awoke from his sleep, and he remembered everything which he had read and seen, and he wrote down all the words which he had read and seen. (32:26).

And he celebrated there yet another day, and he sacrificed thereon according to all that he sacrificed on the former days, and called its name 'Addition,' for this day was added and the former days he called 'The Feast '. (32:27).

And thus it was manifested that it should be, and it is written on the heavenly tablets: wherefore it was revealed to him that he should celebrate it, and add it to the seven days of the feast. (32:28).
And its name was called 'Addition,' because that it was recorded amongst the days of the feast days, according to the number of the days of the year. (32:29).

And in the night, on the twenty-third of this month, Deborah Rebecca's nurse died, and they buried her beneath the city under the oak of the river, and he called the name of this place, 'The river of Deborah,' and the oak, 'The oak of the mourning of Deborah.' (32:30).
And Rebecca went and returned to her house to his father Isaac, and Jacob sent by her hand rams and sheep and he-goats that she should prepare a meal for his father such as he desired. (32:31).
And he went after his mother till he came to the land of Kabratan, and he dwelt there. (32:32).

And Rachel bare a son in the night, and called his name 'Son of my sorrow '; for she suffered in giving him birth: but his father called his name Benjamin, on the eleventh of the eighth month in the first of the sixth week of this jubilee. [2143 A.M.] (32:33).
And Rachel died there and she was buried in the land of Ephrath, the same is Bethlehem, and Jacob built a pillar on the grave of Rachel, on the road above her grave. (32:34).
crossRefs: Genesis 35:9-15: God appears to Jacob at Bethel, changes his name to Israel, promises kings from his body, and Jacob sets up a pillar and pours out a drink offering and oil on it.
Genesis 48:7: Jacob tells Joseph that Rachel died beside him in the land of Canaan on the road, with only a little way still to Ephrath, and that he buried her there.
Deuteronomy 14:22-27: The second tithe is eaten before the LORD at the place He chooses, or turned into money and spent there, the law this chapter says was written for what Jacob did.
Leviticus 27:30-33: The tithe of the land and of the herd is holy to the LORD, and every tenth animal that passes under the rod is His, with no picking between good and bad.
Numbers 29:35-38: The eighth day is a solemn assembly with offerings of its own after the seven days of booths, the day this chapter names Addition.

translationNotes.note: At 32:9-15 the book separates the tithe handed to the priests from a second tithe the owner eats before the Lord at the chosen place, year by year, with nothing carried into the next year. Deuteronomy 14:22-27 is that law. The book puts the practice in Jacob's hands long before Deuteronomy states it.

The Hebrew idiom for ordaining a priest is to fill his hands, because the ceremony places the portions of the offering into them. Exodus 29:9 and Leviticus 8:33 both use it of Aaron and his sons, where older English says consecrate. At 32:3 Jacob clothes Levi in the priestly garments and fills his hands.

Leviticus 27:32 sets the herd tithe by having the animals pass under the shepherd's staff so that every tenth is holy to the LORD. At 32:3 Jacob counts his sons from the youngest upward, and on that count the tenth falls on Levi, which is how the book makes Levi the Lord's portion by the ordinary rule rather than by preference.

At 32:27-29 Jacob keeps an eighth day of feast and names it Addition, because it was added to the seven. Leviticus 23:36 and Numbers 29:35 both put a solemn assembly on the eighth day after booths, so the day itself is in the law; the name and the story behind it belong to this book.

Ephrath is the older name of Bethlehem, about five miles south of Jerusalem on the ridge road; Genesis 35:19 makes the identification and 32:34 repeats it. Ruth 4:11 calls the townspeople Ephrathites, and Micah 5:2 addresses Bethlehem Ephratah, little among the thousands of Judah.

stories.keyTakeaway: Levi dreams he has been made priest, and Jacob counts his sons from the youngest upward so that Levi falls to the Lord as the tenth and is ordained. Jacob keeps an eighth day of feast and calls it Addition. He is renamed Israel, told not to build a sanctuary there, and Rachel dies bearing Benjamin.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 33
summaryBullets: And Jacob went and dwelt to the south of Magdaladra'ef. And he went to his father Isaac, he and Leah his wife, on the new moon of the tenth month. (33:1).
And Reuben saw Bilhah, Rachel's maid, the concubine of his father, bathing in water in a secret place, and he loved her. (33:2).
And he hid himself at night, and he entered the house of Bilhah [at night], and he found her sleeping alone on a bed in her house. (33:3).

And he lay with her, and she awoke and saw, and behold Reuben was lying with her in the bed, and she uncovered the border of her covering and seized him, and cried out, and discovered that it was Reuben. (33:4).
And she was ashamed because of him, and released her hand from him, and he fled. (33:5).
And she lamented because of this thing exceedingly, and did not tell it to any one. (33:6).

And when Jacob returned and sought her, she said to him: 'I am not clean for you, for I have been defiled as regards you; for Reuben has defiled me, and has lain with me in the night, and I was asleep, and did not discover until he uncovered my skirt and slept with me.' (33:7).
And Jacob was exceedingly wroth with Reuben because he had lain with Bilhah, because he had uncovered his father's skirt. (33:8).
And Jacob did not approach her again because Reuben had defiled her. And as for any man who uncovers his father's skirt his deed is wicked exceedingly, for he is abominable before the Lord. (33:9).

For this reason it is written and ordained on the heavenly tablets that a man should not lie with his father's wife, and should not uncover his father's skirt, for this is unclean: they shall surely die together, the man who lies with his father's wife and the woman also, for they have wrought uncleanness on the earth. (33:10).
And there shall be nothing unclean before our God in the nation which He has chosen for Himself as a possession. (33:11).

And again, it is written a second time: 'Cursed be he who lieth with the wife of his father, for he has uncovered his father's shame'; and all the holy ones of the Lord said 'So be it; so be it.' (33:12).

And do you, Moses, command the children of Israel that they observe this word; for it (entails) a punishment of death; and it is unclean, and there is no atonement for ever to atone for the man who has committed this, but he is to be put to death and slain, and stoned with stones, and rooted out from the midst of the people of our God. (33:13).
For to no man who does so in Israel is it permitted to remain alive a single day on the earth, for he is abominable and unclean. (33:14).

And let them not say: to Reuben was granted life and forgiveness after he had lain with his father's concubine, and to her also though she had a husband, and her husband Jacob, his father, was still alive. (33:15).

For until that time there had not been revealed the ordinance and judgment and law in its completeness for all, but in your days (it has been revealed) as a law of seasons and of days, and an everlasting law for the everlasting generations. (33:16).

And for this law there is no consummation of days, and no atonement for it, but they must both be rooted out in the midst of the nation: on the day whereon they committed it they shall slay them. (33:17).

And do you, Moses, write (it) down for Israel that they may observe it, and do according to these words, and not commit a sin to death; for the Lord our God is judge, who respects not persons and accepts not gifts. (33:18).

And tell them these words of the covenant, that they may hear and observe, and be on their guard with respect to them, and not be destroyed and rooted out of the land; for an uncleanness, and an abomination, and a contamination, and a pollution are all they who commit it on the earth before our God. (33:19).

And there is no greater sin than the fornication which they commit on earth; for Israel is a holy nation to the Lord its God, and a nation of inheritance, and a priestly and royal nation and for (His own) possession; and there shall no such uncleanness appear in the midst of the holy nation. (33:20).
And in the third year of this sixth week [2145 A.M.] Jacob and all his sons went and dwelt in the house of Abraham, near Isaac his father and Rebecca his mother. (33:21).

And these were the names of the sons of Jacob: the first-born Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulon, the sons of Leah; and the sons of Rachel, Joseph and Benjamin; and the sons of Bilhah, Dan and Naphtali; and the sons of Zilpah, Gad and Asher; and Dinah, the daughter of Leah, the only daughter of Jacob. (33:22).

And they came and bowed themselves to Isaac and Rebecca, and when they saw them they blessed Jacob and all his sons, and Isaac rejoiced exceedingly, for he saw the sons of Jacob, his younger son and he blessed them. (33:23).
crossRefs: Genesis 35:22: Reuben went and lay with Bilhah his father's concubine, and Israel heard of it, reported in one line with no penalty attached.
Leviticus 20:11: The man who lies with his father's wife has uncovered his father's nakedness, and both of them are put to death, their blood upon them.
Deuteronomy 27:20: Cursed is he who lies with his father's wife, because he has uncovered his father's skirt, and all the people say Amen, the curse this chapter quotes.
Deuteronomy 22:30: A man shall not take his father's wife nor uncover his father's skirt, the rule stated flatly among the marriage laws.
Genesis 49:3-4: Jacob tells Reuben he is unstable as water and shall not excel, because he went up to his father's bed and defiled it.

translationNotes.note: Kanaf is the corner or skirt of a garment, and spreading a skirt over a woman meant claiming her as a wife, as at Ruth 3:9. Uncovering the father's skirt therefore means taking what is his. Deuteronomy 22:30 and Deuteronomy 27:20 both use the phrase for lying with a father's wife, and 33:8-9 uses it three times over.

A pilegesh is a secondary wife: a real wife of lower standing whose children could inherit but whose position rested on the man. Bilhah is Rachel's handmaid, given to Jacob at 28:9. Taking a father's concubine was a move on his place and not only a sin against her, which is why 33:8 has Jacob treat it as done against himself.

At 33:13 and 33:17 the book says this offence has no atonement at all: no sacrifice covers it and the sentence falls on the day it is done. The law of Moses draws a distinction of the same kind, since Numbers 15:30-31 puts the man who sins with a high hand outside the sacrifices entirely, while Leviticus 4:27-31 provides for sins done unwittingly.

At 33:15-16 the book answers the obvious objection: no one may argue from Reuben's survival that the act can be forgiven, because the law had not yet been revealed in full when he did it. Genesis 35:22 records the act and Israel hearing of it and imposes nothing; Genesis 49:3-4 has Jacob take the firstborn's standing from him for it on his deathbed.

stories.keyTakeaway: Reuben lies with Bilhah, his father's concubine, and she tells Jacob, who never goes near her again. The chapter makes it a capital law on the heavenly tablets that both the man and the woman die with no atonement, and says Reuben was spared only because the law had not yet been given in full.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 34
summaryBullets: And in the sixth year of this week of this forty-fourth jubilee [2148 A.M.] Jacob sent his sons to pasture their sheep, and his servants with them to the pastures of Shechem. (34:1).
And the seven kings of the Amorites assembled themselves together against them, to slay them, hiding themselves under the trees, and to take their cattle as a prey. (34:2).

And Jacob and Levi and Judah and Joseph were in the house with Isaac their father; for his spirit was sorrowful, and they could not leave him: and Benjamin was the youngest, and for this reason remained with his father. (34:3).

And there came the king[s] of Taphu and the king[s] of 'Aresa, and the king[s] of Seragan, and the king[s] of Selo, and the king[s] of Ga'as, and the king of Bethoron, and the king of Ma'anisakir, and all those who dwell in these mountains (and) who dwell in the woods in the land of Canaan. (34:4).
And they announced this to Jacob saying: 'Behold, the kings of the Amorites have surrounded your sons, and plundered their herds.' (34:5).
And he arose from his house, he and his three sons and all the servants of his father, and his own servants, and he went against them with six thousand men, who carried swords. (34:6).

And he slew them in the pastures of Shechem, and pursued those who fled, and he slew them with the edge of the sword, and he slew 'Aresa and Taphu and Saregan and Selo and 'Amani- sakir and Ga[ga]'as, and he recovered his herds. (34:7).
And he prevailed over them, and imposed tribute on them that they should pay him tribute, five fruit products of their land, and he built Robel and Tamnatares. (34:8).
And he returned in peace, and made peace with them, and they became his servants, until the day that he and his sons went down into Egypt. (34:9).
And in the seventh year of this week [2149 A.M.] he sent Joseph to learn about the welfare of his brothers from his house to the land of Shechem, and he found them in the land of Dothan. (34:10).

And they dealt treacherously with him, and formed a plot against him to slay him, but changing their minds, they sold him to Ishmaelite merchants, and they brought him down into Egypt, and they sold him to Potiphar, the eunuch of Pharaoh, the chief of the cooks, priest of the city of 'Elew. (34:11).
And the sons of Jacob slaughtered a kid, and dipped the coat of Joseph in the blood, and sent (it) to Jacob their father on the tenth of the seventh month. (34:12).

And he mourned all that night, for they had brought it to him in the evening, and he became feverish with mourning for his death, and he said: 'An evil beast has devoured Joseph'; and all the members of his house [mourned with him that day, and they] were grieving and mourning with him all that day. (34:13).
And his sons and his daughter rose up to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted for his son. (34:14).
And on that day Bilhah heard that Joseph had perished, and she died mourning him, and she was living in Qafratef, and Dinah also, his daughter, died after Joseph had perished. (34:15).
And there came these three mournings upon Israel in one month. And they buried Bilhah over against the tomb of Rachel, and Dinah also. his daughter, they buried there. (34:16).
And he mourned for Joseph one year, and did not cease, for he said 'Let me go down to the grave mourning for my son'. (34:17).

For this reason it is ordained for the children of Israel that they should afflict themselves on the tenth of the seventh month -on the day that the news which made him weep for Joseph came to Jacob his father- that they should make atonement for themselves thereon with a young goat on the tenth of the seventh month, once a year, for their sins; for they had grieved the affection of their father regarding Joseph his son. (34:18).

And this day has been ordained that they should grieve thereon for their sins, and for all their transgressions and for all their errors, so that they might cleanse themselves on that day once a year. (34:19).

And after Joseph perished, the sons of Jacob took to themselves wives. The name of Reuben's wife is 'Ada; and the name of Simeon's wife is 'Adlba'a, a Canaanite; and the name of Levi's wife is Melka, of the daughters of Aram, of the seed of the sons of Terah; and the name of Judah's wife, Betasu'el, a Canaanite; and the name of Issachar's wife, Hezaqa: and the name of Zabulon's wife, Ni'iman; and the name of Dan's wife, 'Egla; and the name of Naphtali's wife, Rasu'u, of Mesopotamia; and the name of Gad's wife, Maka; and the name of Asher's wife, 'Ijona; and the name of Joseph's wife, Asenath, the Egyptian; and the name of Benjamin's wife, 'Ijasaka. (34:20).
And Simeon repented, and took a second wife from Mesopotamia as his brothers. (34:21).
crossRefs: Genesis 37:12-36: Joseph is sent to his brothers at Shechem, found at Dothan, thrown into the pit and sold to passing traders, and the coat is dipped in goat's blood and carried to his father.
Leviticus 16:29-31: On the tenth day of the seventh month you shall afflict your souls and do no work, for on that day atonement is made to cleanse you from all your sins.
Leviticus 23:26-32: The day of atonement is a holy convocation on the tenth of the seventh month, and anyone who does not afflict himself that day is cut off from his people.
Genesis 48:22: Jacob tells Joseph he gives him one portion above his brothers, taken out of the hand of the Amorite with his sword and his bow, the only trace in Genesis of a battle fought by Jacob.
Genesis 46:8-27: The house of Jacob that came into Egypt, named man by man, the same family this chapter lists through the wives of the twelve sons.

translationNotes.note: The tenth day of the seventh month, when Israel afflicts itself, does no work, and the high priest goes inside the veil, Leviticus 16:29-34. At 34:18-19 this book supplies a cause for the date: it is the day Joseph's bloodied coat reached Jacob, and the fast is kept because the brothers grieved their father. Leviticus gives the day and the ritual and gives no such origin.

The phrase at Leviticus 16:29 and Leviticus 23:27 means to humble or deny yourself, and it is understood as fasting. Isaiah 58:3-5 argues about what such a day really requires, using the same wording about afflicting the soul. It is the only fast the law of Moses commands.

translationNotes.term: Eunuch and chief of the cooks
translationNotes.note: Saris means a court official and can also mean a literal eunuch; Genesis 39:1 uses it of Potiphar, who has a wife. Tabbach means a slaughterer or cook, and chief of the tabbachim is usually rendered captain of the guard, since one word covered the men who killed for the kitchen and the men who killed for the king.

At 34:11 the brothers sell Joseph to Ishmaelite traders. Genesis 37:25 has a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead with spicery, balm and myrrh, bound for Egypt, which is the incense road running up from Arabia to the Nile. Genesis 37:28 calls the same men Midianite traders, and Judges 8:24 notes that Ishmaelites wore gold earrings.

The book calls Potiphar priest of the city of Elew, and at 40:10 names Heliopolis, which is On, the great centre of sun worship north-east of modern Cairo. Genesis 41:45 gives Joseph a wife, Asenath, daughter of Potipherah priest of On. Jeremiah 43:13 speaks of breaking the images of Beth-shemesh, the house of the sun, in the land of Egypt.

stories.keyTakeaway: Seven Amorite kings attack the flocks at Shechem and Jacob puts them down and lays tribute on them. Joseph is sent to his brothers, sold to Ishmaelite traders, and the bloodied coat reaches Jacob on the tenth of the seventh month, which this chapter makes the yearly day of affliction.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 35
summaryBullets: And in the first year of the first week of the forty-fifth jubilee [2157 A.M.] Rebecca called Jacob, her son, and commanded him regarding his father and regarding his brother, that he should honour them all the days of his life. (35:1).
And Jacob said: 'I will do everything as you have commanded me; for this thing will be honour and greatness to me, and righteousness before the Lord, that I should honour them. (35:2).
And you too, mother, know from the time I was born until this day, all my deeds and all that is in my heart, that I always think good concerning all. (35:3).
And how should I not do this thing which you have commanded me, that I should honour my father and my brother! (35:4).
Tell me, mother, what perversity have you seen in me and I shall turn away from it, and mercy will be upon me.' (35:5).

And she said to him: 'My son, I have not seen in you all my days any perverse but (only) upright deeds. And yet I will tell you the truth, my son: I shall die this year, and I shall not survive this year in my life; for I have seen in a dream the day of my death, that I should not live beyond a hundred and fifty-five years: and behold I have completed all the days of my life which I am to live.' (35:6).

And Jacob laughed at the words of his mother. because his mother had said to him that she should die; and she was sitting opposite to him in possession of her strength, and she was not infirm in her strength; for she went in and out and saw, and her teeth were strong, and no ailment had touched her all the days of her life. (35:7).

And Jacob said to her: 'Blessed am I, mother, if my days approach the days of your life, and my strength remain with me thus as your strength: and you will not die, for you are jesting idly with me regarding your death.' (35:8).

And she went in to Isaac and said to him: 'One petition I make to you: make Esau swear that he will not injure Jacob, nor pursue him with enmity; for you know Esau's thoughts that they are perverse from his youth, and there is no goodness in him; for he desires after your death to kill him. (35:9).

And you know all that he has done since the day Jacob his brother went to Haran until this day: how he has forsaken us with his whole heart, and has done evil to us; your flocks he has taken to himself, and carried off all your possessions from before your face. (35:10).
And when we implored and besought him for what was our own, he did as a man who was taking pity on us. (35:11).

And he is bitter against you because you didst bless Jacob your perfect and upright son; for there is no evil but only goodness in him, and since he came from Haran to this day he has not robbed us of aught, for he brings us everything in its season always, and rejoices with all his heart when we take at his hands and he blesses us, and has not parted from us since he came from Haran until this day, and he remains with us continually at home honouring us.' (35:12).

And Isaac said to her: 'I, too, know and see the deeds of Jacob who is with us, how that with all his heart he honours us; but I loved Esau formerly more than Jacob, because he was the firstborn; but now I love Jacob more than Esau, for he has done manifold evil deeds, and there is no righteousness in him, for all his ways are unrighteousness and violence, [and there is no righteousness around him.] (35:13).

And now my heart is troubled because of all his deeds, and neither he nor his seed is to be saved, for they are those who will be destroyed from the earth and who will be rooted out from under heaven, for he has forsaken the God of Abraham and gone after his wives and after their uncleanness and after their error, he and his children. (35:14).
And you do bid me make him swear that he will not slay Jacob his brother; even if he swear he will not abide by his oath, and he will not do good but evil only. (35:15).
But if he desires to slay Jacob, his brother, into Jacob's hands will he be given, and he will not escape from his hands, [for he will descend into his hands.] (35:16).
And fear you not on account of Jacob; for the guardian of Jacob is great and powerful and honoured, and praised more than the guardian of Esau.' (35:17).
And Rebecca sent and called Esau and he came to her, and she said to him: 'I have a petition, my son, to make to you, and do you promise to do it, my son.' (35:18).
And he said: 'I will do everything that you say to me, and I will not refuse your petition.' (35:19).

And she said to him: 'I ask you that the day I die, you will take me in and bury me near Sarah, your father's mother, and that you and Jacob will love each other and that neither will desire evil against the other, but mutual love only, and (so) you will prosper, my sons, and be honoured in the midst of the land, and no enemy will rejoice over you, and you will be a blessing and a mercy in the eyes of all those that love you.' (35:20).
And he said: 'I will do all that you have told me, and I shall bury you on the day you diest near Sarah, my father's mother, as you have desired that her bones may be near your bones. (35:21).

And Jacob, my brother, also, I shall love above all flesh; for I have not a brother in all the earth but him only: and this is no great merit for me if I love him; for he is my brother, and we were sown together in your body, and together came we forth from your womb, and if I do not love my brother, whom shall I love? (35:22).

And I, myself, beg you to exhort Jacob concerning me and concerning my sons, for I know that he will assuredly be king over me and my sons, for on the day my father blessed him he made him the higher and me the lower. (35:23).
And I swear to you that I shall love him, and not desire evil against him all the days of my life but good only.' (35:24).
And he sware to her regarding all this matter. And she called Jacob before the eyes of Esau, and gave him commandment according to the words which she had spoken to Esau. (35:25).
And he said: 'I shall do your pleasure; believe me that no evil will proceed from me or from my sons against Esau, and I shall be first in naught save in love only.' (35:26).

And they eat and drank, she and her sons that night, and she died, three jubilees and one week and one year old, on that night, and her two sons, Esau and Jacob, buried her in the double cave near Sarah, their father's mother. (35:27).
crossRefs: Exodus 20:12: Honour your father and your mother, that your days may be long upon the land the LORD your God gives you, the command Rebecca lays on Jacob here.
Genesis 27:41: Esau says in his heart that the days of mourning for his father are at hand, and then he will kill his brother Jacob, the threat Rebecca is still working against.
Numbers 30:2: When a man swears an oath to bind his soul he shall not break his word but shall do all that comes out of his mouth, the standard Isaac says Esau will fail.
Genesis 49:31: Jacob names those buried in the cave at Machpelah, Abraham and Sarah, Isaac and Rebekah, and Leah, the only notice Genesis gives of Rebekah's burial.
Hebrews 12:16-17: Esau is called profane for selling his birthright and finding no place of repentance afterwards, the character Isaac describes in this chapter.

translationNotes.term: Three jubilees and one week and one year
