translationNotes.note: At 35:27 Rebecca's age at death is given in that form: forty-nine times three, plus seven, plus one, which is a hundred and fifty-five, the number she names herself at 35:6. Genesis records neither her age nor her death, only that she was buried at Machpelah, Genesis 49:31.

Kabbed is built on a root meaning to be heavy, so to honour someone is to treat them as carrying weight. Exodus 20:12 puts it in the fifth commandment with a promise attached, and Leviticus 19:3 pairs fearing mother and father with keeping the sabbaths. At 35:1-4 Rebecca stretches the duty to cover a brother as well.

At 35:17 Isaac tells Rebecca that the guardian of Jacob is greater and more honoured than the guardian of Esau. That matches this book's arrangement at 15:31-32, where spirits are set over the nations while God rules Israel Himself. Daniel 10:13-21 speaks the same way of a prince standing for one kingdom against another.

At 35:20-21 Rebecca asks Esau to bury her beside Sarah so that her bones lie near hers, and at 35:27 both sons carry her to the double cave. Genesis 49:31 lists who is there. Being laid with the family dead was the whole point of buying that field, Genesis 23:19-20.

stories.keyTakeaway: Rebecca charges Jacob to honour his father and his brother, and tells him she has seen the day of her death. She asks Isaac to put Esau under oath not to harm Jacob, and Isaac answers that Esau will not keep it. Esau swears anyway, and Rebecca dies that night and is buried in the double cave.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 36
summaryBullets: And in the sixth year of this week [2162 A.M.] Isaac called his two sons Esau and Jacob, and they came to him, and he said to them: 'My sons, I am going the way of my fathers, to the eternal house where my fathers are. (36:1).

Wherefore bury me near Abraham my father, in the double cave in the field of Ephron the Hittite, where Abraham purchased a sepulchre to bury in; in the sepulchre which I digged for myself, there bury me. (36:2).

And this I command you, my sons, that you practise righteousness and uprightness on the earth, so that the Lord may bring upon you all that the Lord said that he would do to Abraham and to his seed. (36:3).

And love one another, my sons, your brothers as a man who loves his own soul, and let each seek in what he may benefit his brother, and act together on the earth; and let them love each other as their own souls. (36:4).

And concerning the question of idols, I command and admonish you to reject them and hate them, and love them not, for they are full of deception for those that worship them and for those that bow down to them. (36:5).

Remember you, my sons, the Lord God of Abraham your father, and how I too worshipped Him and served Him in righteousness and in joy, that He might multiply you and increase your seed as the stars of heaven in multitude, and establish you on the earth as the plant of righteousness which will not be rooted out to all the generations for ever. (36:6).

And now I shall make you swear a great oath -for there is no oath which is greater than it by the name glorious and honoured and great and splendid and wonderful and mighty, which created the heavens and the earth and all things together- that you will fear Him and worship Him. (36:7).

And that each will love his brother with affection and righteousness, and that neither will desire evil against his brother from henceforth for ever all the days of your life so that you may prosper in all your deeds and not be destroyed. (36:8).

And if either of you devises evil against his brother, know that from henceforth everyone that devises evil against his brother shall fall into his hand, and shall be rooted out of the land of the living, and his seed shall be destroyed from under heaven. (36:9).

But on the day of turbulence and execration and indignation and anger, with flaming devouring fire as He burnt Sodom, so likewise will He burn his land and his city and all that is his, and he shall be blotted out of the book of the discipline of the children of men, and not be recorded in the book of life, but in that which is appointed to destruction, and he shall depart into eternal execration; so that their condemnation may be always renewed in hate and in execration and in wrath and in torment and in indignation and in plagues and in disease for ever. (36:10).
I say and testify to you, my sons, according to the judgment which shall come upon the man who wishes to injure his brother. (36:11).

And he divided all his possessions between the two on that day and he gave the larger portion to him that was the first-born, and the tower and all that was about it, and all that Abraham possessed at the Well of the Oath. (36:12).
And he said: 'This larger portion I will give to the firstborn.' (36:13).
And Esau said, 'I have sold to Jacob and given my birthright to Jacob; to him let it be given, and I have not a single word to say regarding it, for it is his.' (36:14).

And Isaac said, May a blessing rest upon you, my sons, and upon your seed this day, for you have given me rest, and my heart is not pained concerning the birthright, lest you shouldest work wickedness on account of it. (36:15).
May the Most High God bless the man that worketh righteousness, him and his seed for ever.' (36:16).

And he ended commanding them and blessing them, and they eat and drank together before him, and he rejoiced because there was one mind between them, and they went forth from him and rested that day and slept. (36:17).

And Isaac slept on his bed that day rejoicing; and he slept the eternal sleep, and died one hundred and eighty years old. He completed twenty-five weeks and five years; and his two sons Esau and Jacob buried him. (36:18).
And Esau went to the land of Edom, to the mountains of Seir, and dwelt there. (36:19).

And Jacob dwelt in the mountains of Hebron, in the tower of the land of the sojournings of his father Abraham, and he worshipped the Lord with all his heart and according to the visible commands according as He had divided the days of his generations. (36:20).

And Leah his wife died in the fourth year of the second week of the forty-fifth jubilee, [2167 A.M.] and he buried her in the double cave near Rebecca his mother to the left of the grave of Sarah, his father's mother (36:21).
and all her sons and his sons came to mourn over Leah his wife with him and to comfort him regarding her, for he was lamenting her for he loved her exceedingly after Rachel her sister died; (36:22).

for she was perfect and upright in all her ways and honoured Jacob,and all the days that she lived with him he did not hear from her mouth a harsh word, for she was gentle and peaceable and upright and honourable. (36:23).
And he remembered all her deeds which she had done during her life and he lamented her exceedingly; for he loved her with all his heart and with all his soul. (36:24).
crossRefs: Genesis 35:27-29: Isaac dies at Mamre at a hundred and eighty years old, old and full of days, and his sons Esau and Jacob bury him.
Genesis 36:6-8: Esau takes his household and all his goods and moves away from his brother Jacob, and dwells in Mount Seir.
Leviticus 19:17-18: Do not hate your brother in your heart, take no vengeance and bear no grudge, but love your neighbour as yourself, the charge this chapter puts under oath.
Genesis 19:24-25: The LORD rained fire and brimstone on Sodom and Gomorrah and overthrew those cities and all the plain, the judgment Isaac names in the curse.
Psalm 69:28: Let them be blotted out of the book of the living and not be written with the righteous, the sentence this chapter passes on the one who breaks the oath.

translationNotes.note: At 36:7 Isaac makes his sons swear by the name that created heaven and earth, and says there is no greater oath. Deuteronomy 6:13 permits swearing by God's name and Leviticus 19:12 forbids swearing falsely by it. The next two chapters test this one, since 37:13 says Esau forgot the oath and 38:2 has Jacob kill him.

At 36:1 Isaac says he is going the way of his fathers to the eternal house where they are, meaning the grave and the company of the dead. Ecclesiastes 12:5 uses the same phrase of dying, that man goes to his long home. The family tomb at Machpelah is its physical form, which is why the burial instruction comes next.

At 36:12-14 Isaac gives the larger share to the firstborn, and Esau answers that he sold it and has nothing to say about it. Deuteronomy 21:17 fixes that share at double, twice what any other son receives. The tower at Hebron and everything Abraham held at the Well of the Oath go with it.

translationNotes.term: The book of the discipline of men
translationNotes.note: At 36:10 the book names two registers, one of life and one appointed to destruction, and moves the oath-breaker from the first to the second. Exodus 32:32-33 and Psalm 69:28 speak of being blotted out of God's book, and Daniel 12:1 says everyone found written in the book shall be delivered.

stories.keyTakeaway: Isaac calls both sons, tells them where to bury him, and puts them under a great oath to love one another and to reject idols, with destruction named for whichever devises evil. He divides his goods, Esau gives up the elder's portion, and Isaac dies at a hundred and eighty. Leah dies after him.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 37
summaryBullets: And on the day that Isaac the father of Jacob and Esau died, [2162 A.M.] the sons of Esau heard that Isaac had given the portion of the elder to his younger son Jacob and they were very angry. (37:1).
And they strove with their father, saying 'Why has your father given Jacob the portion of the elder and passed over you, although you are the elder and Jacob the younger?' (37:2).

And he said to them 'Because I sold my birthright to Jacob for a small mess of lentils, and on the day my father sent me to hunt and catch and bring him something that he should eat and bless me, he came with guile and brought my father food and drink, and my father blessed him and put me under his hand. (37:3).

And now our father has caused us to swear, me and him, that we shall not mutually devise evil, either against his brother, and that we shall continue in love and in peace each with his brother and not make our ways corrupt.' (37:4).

And they said to him, 'We shall not hearken to you to make peace with him; for our strength is greater than his strength, and we are more powerful than he; we shall go against him and slay him, and destroy him and his sons. And if you will not go with us, we shall do hurt to you also. (37:5).

And now hearken to us: Let us send to Aram and Philistia and Moab and Ammon, and let us choose for ourselves chosen men who are ardent for battle, and let us go against him and do battle with him, and let us exterminate him from the earth before he grows strong.' (37:6).
And their father said to them, 'Do not go and do not make war with him lest you fall before him.' (37:7).
And they said to him, 'This too, is exactly your mode of action from your youth until this day, and you are putting your neck under his yoke. (37:8).
We shall not hearken to these words.' And they sent to Aram, and to 'Aduram to the friend of their father, and they hired along with them one thousand fighting men, chosen men of war. (37:9).

And there came to them from Moab and from the children of Ammon, those who were hired, one thousand chosen men, and from Philistia, one thousand chosen men of war, and from Edom and from the Horites one thousand chosen fighting men, and from the Kittim mighty men of war. (37:10).
And they said to their father: Go forth with them and lead them, else we shall slay you.' (37:11).
And he was filled with wrath and indignation on seeing that his sons were forcing him to go before (them) to lead them against Jacob his brother. (37:12).

But afterward he remembered all the evil which lay hidden in his heart against Jacob his brother; and he remembered not the oath which he had sworn to his father and to his mother that he would devise no evil all his days against Jacob his brother. (37:13).

And notwithstanding all this, Jacob knew not that they were coming against him to battle, and he was mourning for Leah, his wife, until they approached very near to the tower with four thousand warriors and chosen men of war. (37:14).

And the men of Hebron sent to him saying, 'Behold your brother has come against you, to fight you, with four thousand girt with the sword, and they carry shields and weapons'; for they loved Jacob more than Esau. So they told him; for Jacob was a more liberal and merciful man than Esau. (37:15).
But Jacob would not believe until they came very near to the tower. (37:16).

And he closed the gates of the tower; and he stood on the battlements and spoke to his brother Esau and said, 'Noble is the comfort with which you have come to comfort me for my wife who has died. Is this the oath that you didst swear to your father and again to your mother before they died? You have broken the oath, and on the moment that you didst swear to your father wast you condemned.' (37:17).

And then Esau answered and said to him, 'Neither the children of men nor the beasts of the earth have any oath of righteousness which in swearing they have sworn (an oath valid) for ever; but every day they devise evil one against another, and how each may slay his adversary and foe. (37:18).
And you do hate me and my children for ever. And there is no observing the tie of brotherhood with you. (37:19).

Hear these words which I declare to you, If the boar can change its skin and make its bristles as soft as wool, Or if it can cause horns to sprout forth on its head like the horns of a stag or of a sheep, Then will I observe the tie of brotherhood with you And if the breasts separated themselves from their mother, for you have not been a brother to me. And if the wolves make peace with the lambs so as not to devour or do them violence, And if their hearts are towards them for good, Then there shall be peace in my heart towards you And if the lion becomes the friend of the ox and makes peace with him And if he is bound under one yoke with him and ploughs with him, Then will I make peace with you. And when the raven becomes white as the raza, Then know that I have loved you And shall make peace with you You will be rooted out, And your sons shall be rooted out, And there shall be no peace for you' And when Jacob saw that he was (so) evilly disposed towards him with his heart, and with all his soul as to slay him, and that he had come springing like the wild boar which comes upon the spear that pierces and kills it, and recoils not from it; then he spoke to his own and to his servants that they should attack him and all his companions. (37:20).

And if the wolves make peace with the lambs so as not to devour or do them violence, And if their hearts are towards them for good, Then there shall be peace in my heart towards you And if the lion becomes the friend of the ox and makes peace with him And if he is bound under one yoke with him and ploughs with him, Then will I make peace with you. And when the raven becomes white as the raza, Then know that I have loved you And shall make peace with you You will be rooted out, And your sons shall be rooted out, And there shall be no peace for you' And when Jacob saw that he was (so) evilly disposed towards him with his heart, and with all his soul as to slay him, and that he had come springing like the wild boar which comes upon the spear that pierces and kills it, and recoils not from it; then he spoke to his own and to his servants that they should attack him and all his companions. (37:21).
And if the lion becomes the friend of the ox and makes peace with him And if he is bound under one yoke with him and ploughs with him, Then will I make peace with you. (37:22).

And when the raven becomes white as the raza, Then know that I have loved you And shall make peace with you You will be rooted out, And your sons shall be rooted out, And there shall be no peace for you' And when Jacob saw that he was (so) evilly disposed towards him with his heart, and with all his soul as to slay him, and that he had come springing like the wild boar which comes upon the spear that pierces and kills it, and recoils not from it; then he spoke to his own and to his servants that they should attack him and all his companions. (37:23).

And when Jacob saw that he was (so) evilly disposed towards him with his heart, and with all his soul as to slay him, and that he had come springing like the wild boar which comes upon the spear that pierces and kills it, and recoils not from it; (37:24).
then he spoke to his own and to his servants that they should attack him and all his companions. (37:25).
crossRefs: Genesis 36:9-19: The sons and chiefs descended from Esau in Mount Seir, the men this chapter says forced their father into the war.
Jeremiah 13:23: Can the Ethiopian change his skin or the leopard his spots, then may you also do good who are used to doing evil, the same form of impossible condition Esau uses.
Isaiah 11:6-7: The wolf shall dwell with the lamb and the lion shall eat straw like the ox, the peace between predator and prey Esau names as the thing that will never come.
Amos 1:11: Edom pursued his brother with the sword and cast off all pity, and his anger tore perpetually, the charge a prophet brings against this people later.
Numbers 20:14-21: Edom refuses Israel passage through his country and comes out against him with a strong hand, the same refusal of kinship generations on.

translationNotes.note: The fight in this chapter is a siege of the fortified farm tower on the Hebron hills where Isaac had lived and Jacob now lives, 29:19 and 36:20. At 37:16-17 Jacob shuts the gates and stands on the battlements to answer his brother. A tower like this was the strong point a household ran to, as in the tower of Shechem at Judges 9:46-49.

At 37:9-10 Esau's sons hire a thousand men from Aram, a thousand from Moab and Ammon and a thousand from Philistia, plus fighters from Edom, the Horites and the Kittim, and 37:14 puts four thousand at the tower. Paid soldiers were ordinary in that world; Judges 9:4 has Abimelech hire men with silver taken out of a temple treasury.

The people who held Seir before Esau's line took it. Deuteronomy 2:12 says the Horites dwelt in Seir and the children of Esau succeeded them and destroyed them from before them, and Genesis 36:20-30 lists their chiefs by name. At 37:10 they are still supplying a thousand fighters to Esau's army.

translationNotes.term: If the boar can change its skin
translationNotes.note: At 37:20-23 Esau lists conditions that cannot happen: the boar softening its bristles into wool, horns sprouting on its head, wolves at peace with lambs, a lion yoked beside an ox at the plough, a raven turning white. Jeremiah 13:23 uses the same device with the leopard's spots, and Isaiah 11:6-7 uses the wolf and the lamb for what only God brings about.

stories.keyTakeaway: Esau's sons refuse the peace and force their father to lead an army against Jacob, hiring fighting men out of Aram, Moab, Ammon, Philistia, Edom and the Kittim. Four thousand come to the tower at Hebron, and Jacob calls the broken oath down on Esau from the battlements.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 38
summaryBullets: And after that Judah spoke to Jacob, his father, and said to him: 'Bend your bow, father, and send forth your arrows and cast down the adversary and slay the enemy; and mayst you have the power, for we shall not slay your brother, for he is such as you, and he is like you let us give him (this) honour.' (38:1).
Then Jacob bent his bow and sent forth the arrow and struck Esau, his brother (on his right breast) and slew him. (38:2).
And again he sent forth an arrow and struck 'Adoran the Aramaean, on the left breast, and drove him backward and slew him. (38:3).
And then went forth the sons of Jacob, they and their servants, dividing themselves into companies on the four sides of the tower. (38:4).

And Judah went forth in front, and Naphtali and Gad with him and fifty servants with him on the south side of the tower, and they slew all they found before them, and not one individual of them escaped. (38:5).
And Levi and Dan and Asher went forth on the east side of the tower, and fifty (men) with them, and they slew the fighting men of Moab and Ammon. (38:6).
And Reuben and Issachar and Zebulon went forth on the north side of the tower, and fifty men with them, and they slew the fighting men of the Philistines. (38:7).

And Simeon and Benjamin and Enoch, Reuben's son, went forth on the west side of the tower, and fifty (men) with them, and they slew of Edom and of the Horites four hundred men, stout warriors; and six hundred fled, and four of the sons of Esau fled with them, and left their father lying slain, as he had fallen on the hill which is in 'Aduram. (38:8).
And the sons of Jacob pursued after them to the mountains of Seir. And Jacob buried his brother on the hill which is in 'Aduram, and he returned to his house. (38:9).
And the sons of Jacob pressed hard upon the sons of Esau in the mountains of Seir, and bowed their necks so that they became servants of the sons of Jacob. (38:10).
And they sent to their father (to inquire) whether they should make peace with them or slay them. (38:11).

And Jacob sent word to his sons that they should make peace, and they made peace with them, and placed the yoke of servitude upon them, so that they paid tribute to Jacob and to his sons always. (38:12).
And they continued to pay tribute to Jacob until the day that he went down into Egypt. (38:13).
And the sons of Edom have not got quit of the yoke of servitude which the twelve sons of Jacob had imposed on them until this day. (38:14).
And these are the kings that reigned in Edom before there reigned any king over the children of Israel [until this day] in the land of Edom. (38:15).
And Balaq, the son of Beor, reigned in Edom, and the name of his city was Danaba. (38:16).
And Balaq died, and Jobab, the son of Zara of Boser, reigned in his stead. (38:17).
And Jobab died, and 'Asam, of the land of Teman, reigned in his stead. (38:18).
And 'Asam died, and 'Adath, the son of Barad, who slew Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his stead, and the name of his city was Avith. (38:19).
And 'Adath died, and Salman, from 'Amaseqa, reigned in his stead. (38:20).
And Salman died,and Saul of Ra'aboth (by the) river, reigned in his stead. (38:21).
And Saul died, and Ba'elunan, the son of Achbor, reigned in his stead. (38:22).
And Ba'elunan, the son of Achbor died, and 'Adath reigned in his stead, and the name of his wife was Maitabith, the daughter of Matarat, the daughter of Metabedza'ab. (38:23).
These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom. (38:24).
crossRefs: Genesis 36:31-39: The kings who reigned in the land of Edom before any king reigned over the children of Israel, the same list this chapter repeats with its own spellings.
Genesis 27:40: By your sword shall you live and you shall serve your brother, and when you break loose you shall shake his yoke from off your neck, the word this chapter treats as coming due.
Numbers 24:18: Edom shall be a possession and Seir also shall be a possession for his enemies, while Israel does valiantly.
Obadiah 1:18: The house of Jacob shall be a fire and the house of Esau stubble, and there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau.
Deuteronomy 2:4-5: Israel is told to take good heed and not meddle with the children of Esau, for the LORD has given Mount Seir to Esau as a possession, which is the opposite instruction.

translationNotes.note: At 38:2 Jacob kills Esau with an arrow and at 38:9 buries him on the hill at Aduram. Genesis reports nothing of it. The last Genesis shows of the two brothers together is Genesis 35:29, where Esau and Jacob bury their father, and Genesis 36:6-8 has Esau move to Seir of his own accord for want of room.

An ol is the wooden yoke laid across a plough animal's neck, and it is the standing image for one nation holding another down. Genesis 27:40 tells Esau he will serve his brother and will one day break the yoke off his neck. At 38:10-14 the book puts Edom under that yoke and says it has never been shaken off.

Mas is forced labour or a levy taken from a subject people rather than a tax on citizens. At 34:8 Jacob imposes it on the Amorite towns, five products of their land, and at 38:12-13 on Edom until the family goes down to Egypt. Exodus 1:11 uses the same word for what Egypt then does to Israel, setting taskmasters over them.

At 38:15-24 the list matches Genesis 36:31-39 man for man, though the Ethiopic spellings differ: Balaq for Bela son of Beor at Dinhabah, Jobab of Bozrah, Husham of Teman, and the Hadad who struck Midian in the field of Moab. Both lists open with the same point, that Edom had kings before Israel did.

stories.keyTakeaway: At Judah's urging Jacob bends his bow and kills Esau with one arrow, and his sons go out on the four sides of the tower and break the hired army. Edom is put under tribute to Jacob's sons and stays there. The chapter closes with the list of kings who reigned in Edom before Israel had a king.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 39
summaryBullets: And Jacob dwelt in the land of his father's sojournings in the land of Canaan. These are the generations of Jacob. (39:1).
And Joseph was seventeen years old when they took him down into the land of Egypt, and Potiphar, an eunuch of Pharaoh, the chief cook bought him. (39:2).
And he set Joseph over all his house and the blessing of the Lord came upon the house of the Egyptian on account of Joseph, and the Lord prospered him in all that he did. (39:3).
And the Egyptian committed everything into the hands of Joseph; for he saw that the Lord was with him, and that the Lord prospered him in all that he did. (39:4).
And Joseph's appearance was comely [and very beautiful was his appearance], and his master's wife lifted up her eyes and saw Joseph, and she loved him and besought him to lie with her. (39:5).

But he did not surrender his soul, and he remembered the Lord and the words which Jacob, his father, used to read from amongst the words of Abraham, that no man should commit fornication with a woman who has a husband; that for him the punishment of death has been ordained in the heavens before the Most High God, and the sin will be recorded against him in the eternal books continually before the Lord. (39:6).
And Joseph remembered these words and refused to lie with her. (39:7).
And she besought him for a year, but he refused and would not listen. (39:8).

But she embraced him and held him fast in the house in order to force him to lie with her, and closed the doors of the house and held him fast; but he left his garment in her hands and broke through the door and fled without from her presence. (39:9).

And the woman saw that he would not lie with her, and she calumniated him in the presence of his lord, saying 'Your Hebrew servant, whom you lovest, sought to force me so that he might lie with me; and it came to pass when I lifted up my voice that he fled and left his garment in my hands when I held him, and he brake through the door.' (39:10).

And the Egyptian saw the garment of Joseph and the broken door, and heard the words of his wife, and cast Joseph into prison into the place where the prisoners were kept whom the king imprisoned. (39:11).

And he was there in the prison; and the Lord gave Joseph favour in the sight of the chief of the prison guards and compassion before him, for he saw that the Lord was with him, and that the Lord made all that he did to prosper. (39:12).
And he committed all things into his hands, and the chief of the prison guards knew of nothing that was with him, for Joseph did every thing, and the Lord perfected it. (39:13).

And he remained there two years. And in those days Pharaoh, king of Egypt was wroth against his two eunuchs, against the chief butler, and against the chief baker, and he put them in ward in the house of the chief cook, in the prison where Joseph was kept. (39:14).
And the chief of the prison guards appointed Joseph to serve them; and he served before them. (39:15).
And they both dreamed a dream, the chief butler and the chief baker, and they told it to Joseph. (39:16).
And as he interpreted to them so it befell them, and Pharaoh restored the chief butler to his office and the (chief) baker he slew, as Joseph had interpreted to them. (39:17).
But the chief butler forgot Joseph in the prison, although he had informed him what would befall him, and did not remember to inform Pharaoh how Joseph had told him, for he forgot. (39:18).
crossRefs: Genesis 39:1-20: Potiphar buys Joseph and sets him over his house, his master's wife speaks to him day by day, he leaves his garment in her hand and flees, and he is put into the prison.
Genesis 40:1-23: The chief butler and the chief baker dream in prison, Joseph reads both dreams, the butler is restored and the baker hanged, and the butler forgets him.
Leviticus 20:10: The man who commits adultery with another man's wife shall surely be put to death, both the adulterer and the adulteress, the sentence this chapter says Joseph had read.
Exodus 20:14: You shall not commit adultery, the seventh commandment, given at Sinai long after the refusal described here.
Proverbs 6:32-35: The man who commits adultery destroys his own soul, and the husband's jealousy will take no ransom and will not spare in the day of vengeance.

translationNotes.term: The words of Abraham that Jacob read
translationNotes.note: At 39:6 Joseph refuses because he remembers words Jacob used to read out of the writings of Abraham, that a man who lies with a married woman stands under a decree of death in heaven and the sin is written against him in eternal books. Genesis 39:9 has him give a different answer, that this would be a great wickedness and a sin against God. The written source is this book's addition.

Genesis 39:20 calls it the round house or fortress where the king's prisoners were held, and Genesis 40:3 places it in the house of the captain of the guard, which is Potiphar's own establishment, so Joseph never leaves his master's compound. Psalm 105:18 says his feet were hurt with fetters and he was laid in iron.

The mashqeh is the cupbearer, the man who hands the king his cup and therefore stands nearest him and is trusted with his life; Nehemiah 1:11 names that office as his own before a Persian king. The opheh is the chief baker. Both are senior household officers, which is why their disgrace lands them in the same prison as Joseph.

At 39:14 Joseph is two years in prison before the butler and baker arrive, and Genesis 41:1 counts two more full years after their dreams before Pharaoh dreams. Genesis 37:2 makes Joseph seventeen when he is taken down and Genesis 41:46 thirty when he stands before Pharaoh, so thirteen years pass between the pit and the ring.

stories.keyTakeaway: Joseph is bought by Potiphar and set over his house. His master's wife presses him for a year and he refuses, remembering a written word of Abraham that death is decreed for the man who takes another man's wife. She keeps his garment and accuses him, and in prison he reads two dreams.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 40
summaryBullets: And in those days Pharaoh dreamed two dreams in one night concerning a famine which was to be in all the land, and he awoke from his sleep and called all the interpreters of dreams that were in Egypt, and magicians, and told them his two dreams, and they were not able to declare (them). (40:1).
And then the chief butler remembered Joseph and spoke of him to the king, and he brought him forth from the prison, and he to]d his two dreams before him. (40:2).

And he said before Pharaoh that his two dreams were one, and he said to him: 'Seven years shall come (in which there shall be) plenty over all the land of Egypt, and after that seven years of famine, such a famine as has not been in all the land. (40:3).

And now let Pharaoh appoint overseers in all the land of Egypt, and let them store up food in every city throughout the days of the years of plenty, and there will be food for the seven years of famine, and the land will not perish through the famine, for it will be very severe.' (40:4).

And the Lord gave Joseph favour and mercy in the eyes of Pharaoh, and Pharaoh said to his servants. We shall not find such a wise and discreet man as this man, for the spirit of the Lord is with him.' (40:5).
And he appointed him the second in all his kingdom and gave him authority over all Egypt, and caused him to ride in the second chariot of Pharaoh. (40:6).

And he clothed him with byssus garments, and he put a gold chain upon his neck, and (a herald) proclaimed before him ' 'El 'El wa 'Abirer,' and placed a ring on his hand and made him ruler over all his house, and magnified him, and said to him. 'Only on the throne shall I be greater than you.' (40:7).

And Joseph ruled over all the land of Egypt, and all the princes of Pharaoh, and all his servants, and all who did the king's business loved him, for he walked in uprightness, for he was without pride and arrogance, and he had no respect of persons, and did not accept gifts, but he judged in uprightness all the people of the land. (40:8).

And the land of Egypt was at peace before Pharaoh because of Joseph, for the Lord was with him, and gave him favour and mercy for all his generations before all those who knew him and those who heard concerning him, and Pharaoh's kingdom was well ordered, and there was no Satan and no evil person (therein). (40:9).
And the king called Joseph's name Sephantiphans, and gave Joseph to wife the daughter of Potiphar, the daughter of the priest of Heliopolis, the chief cook. (40:10).
And on the day that Joseph stood before Pharaoh he was thirty years old [when he stood before Pharaoh]. (40:11).

And in that year Isaac died. And it came to pass as Joseph had said in the interpretation of his two dreams, according as he had said it, there were seven years of plenty over all the land of Egypt, and the land of Egypt abundantly produced, one measure (producing) eighteen hundred measures. (40:12).
And Joseph gathered food into every city until they were full of corn until they could no longer count and measure it for its multitude. (40:13).
crossRefs: Genesis 41:1-36: Pharaoh's two dreams of the cattle and the ears of grain, the failure of the magicians and wise men, and Joseph's reading of seven plentiful years followed by seven of famine.
Genesis 45:4-8: Joseph tells his brothers that God sent him ahead of them to preserve life, and has made him a father to Pharaoh, lord of all his house, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.
Daniel 2:1-13: Nebuchadnezzar's dream troubles him and the magicians and Chaldeans cannot tell it, the same failure of the court experts before a foreigner reads it.
Psalm 105:17-22: God sent a man before them, Joseph sold as a slave, until his word came to pass, and the king made him lord of his house and ruler of all his substance.
Genesis 47:13-26: The famine years fall out as Joseph said, and Egypt buys grain until the land itself belongs to Pharaoh, with a fifth part fixed as the levy.

translationNotes.note: Byssus is fine white linen, the Egyptian luxury cloth, spun so fine that it was traded at very high prices and used to wrap the dead. Genesis 41:42 has Pharaoh dress Joseph in it. The same fabric makes the curtains of the tabernacle at Exodus 26:1 and the priestly garments at Exodus 28:39.

The ring carried the king's seal, and pressing it into clay or wax made a document the king's own act, so handing it over hands over the power to issue orders. Genesis 41:42 gives Joseph Pharaoh's ring, Esther 8:2 turns on the same object, and Genesis 38:18 has Judah leave his own seal as a pledge.

translationNotes.term: An Egyptian name and an Egyptian wife
translationNotes.note: Genesis 41:45 gives Joseph both, the wife being the daughter of the priest of On. Each is a mark of being taken fully into the court. This book spells the name Sephantiphans at 40:10 and names the city Heliopolis, which is On, the centre of sun worship north-east of modern Cairo.

At 40:12 the yield in the plenty years is given as one measure producing eighteen hundred. Genesis 26:12 treats a hundredfold at Gerar as a mark of blessing, and the sower's good ground at Matthew 13:8 returns thirty, sixty and a hundredfold, so this figure is far past anything reported elsewhere. Genesis 41:47-49 says only that the earth brought forth by handfuls and the grain could not be measured.

stories.keyTakeaway: Pharaoh dreams twice in one night and nobody in Egypt can read it. Joseph tells him the two dreams are one, seven years of plenty and then seven of famine, and says to store grain. Pharaoh sets him over Egypt with the ring, the gold chain and the second chariot, and the years of plenty come in.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 41
summaryBullets: And in the forty-fifth jubilee, in the second week, (and) in the second year, [2165 A.M.] Judah took for his first-born Er, a wife from the daughters of Aram, named Tamar. (41:1).

But he hated, and did not lie with her, because his mother was of the daughters of Canaan, and he wished to take him a wife of the kinsfolk of his mother, but Judah, his father, would not permit him. (41:2).
And this Er, the first-born of Judah, was wicked, and the Lord slew him. (41:3).
And Judah said to Onan, his brother 'Go in to your brother's wife and perform the duty of a husband's brother to her, and raise up seed to your brother.' (41:4).

And Onan knew that the seed would not be his, (but) his brother's only, and he went into the house of his brother's wife, and spilt the seed on the ground, and he was wicked in the eyes of the Lord, and He slew him. (41:5).
And Judah said to Tamar, his daughter-in-law: 'Remain in your father's house as a widow till Shelah my son be grown up, and I shall give you to him to wife.' (41:6).
And he grew up; but Bedsu'el, the wife of Judah, did not permit her son Shelah to marry. And Bedsu'el, the wife of Judah, died [2168 A.M.] in the fifth year of this week. (41:7).
And in the sixth year Judah went up to shear his sheep at Timnah. [2169 A.M.] And they told Tamar: 'Behold your father-in-law goes up to Timnah to shear his sheep.' (41:8).
And she put off her widow's clothes, and put on a veil, and adorned herself, and sat in the gate adjoining the way to Timnah. (41:9).
And as Judah was going along he found her, and thought her to be an harlot, and he said to her: 'Let me come in to you'; and she said to him Come in,' and he went in. (41:10).
And she said to him: 'Give me my hire'; and he said to her: 'I have nothing in my hand save my ring that is on my finger, and my necklace, and my staff which is in my hand.' (41:11).

And she said to him 'Give them to me until you do send me my hire', and he said to her: 'I will send to you a kid of the goats'; and he gave them to her, and he went in to her , and she conceived by him. (41:12).
And Judah went to his sheep, and she went to her father's house. (41:13).

And Judah sent a kid of the goats by the hand of his shepherd, an Adullamite, and he found her not; and he asked the people of the place, saying: 'Where is the harlot who was here?' And they said to him; 'There is no harlot here with us.' (41:14).
And he returned and informed him, and said to him that he had not found her: 'I asked the people of the place, and they said to me: "There is no harlot here." ' (41:15).

And he said: 'Let her keep (them) lest we become a cause of derision.' And when she had completed three months, it was manifest that she was with child, and they told Judah, saying: 'Behold Tamar, your daughter-in-law, is with child by whoredom.' (41:16).
And Judah went to the house of her father, and said to her father and her brothers: 'Bring her forth, and let them burn her, for she has wrought uncleanness in Israel.' (41:17).

And it came to pass when they brought her forth to burn her that she sent to her father-in-law the ring and the necklace, and the staff, saying: 'Discern whose are these, for by him am I with child.' (41:18).
And Judah acknowledged, and said: 'Tamar is more righteous than I am. (41:19).
And therefore let them burn her not' And for that reason she was not given to Shelah, and he did not again approach her. (41:20).
And after that she bare two sons, Perez [2170 A.M.] and Zerah, in the seventh year of this second week. (41:21).
And thereupon the seven years of fruitfulness were accomplished, of which Joseph spoke to Pharaoh. (41:22).

And Judah acknowledged that the deed which he had done was evil, for he had lain with his daughter-in-law, and he esteemed it hateful in his eyes, and he acknowledged that he had transgressed and gone astray, for he had uncovered the skirt of his son, and he began to lament and to supplicate before the Lord because of his transgression. (41:23).
And we told him in a dream that it was forgiven him because he supplicated earnestly, and lamented, and did not again commit it. (41:24).

And he received forgiveness because he turned from his sin and from his ignorance, for he transgressed greatly before our God; and every one that acts thus, every one who lies with his mother-in-law, let them burn him with fire that he may burn therein, for there is uncleanness and pollution upon them, with fire let them burn them. (41:25).

And do you command the children of Israel that there be no uncleanness amongst them, for every one who lies with his daughter-in-law or with his mother-in-law has wrought uncleanness; with fire let them burn the man who has lain with her, and likewise the woman, and He will turn away wrath and punishment from Israel. (41:26).
And to Judah we said that his two sons had not lain with her, and for this reason his seed was stablished for a second generation, and would not be rooted out. (41:27).
For in singleness of eye he had gone and sought for punishment, namely, according to the judgment of Abraham, which he had commanded his sons, Judah had sought to burn her with fire. (41:28).
crossRefs: Genesis 38:1-30: Er and Onan die, Tamar is kept waiting for Shelah, she sits veiled by the road to Timnah, Judah leaves his signet and cord and staff, and Perez and Zerah are born.
Deuteronomy 25:5-10: The brother of a man who dies childless is to take the widow and raise up seed to his brother, and the widow may shame in public the brother who refuses.
Leviticus 18:15: You shall not uncover the nakedness of your daughter-in-law, she is your son's wife, the law this chapter says Judah broke without knowing it.
Leviticus 20:14: If a man takes a wife and her mother it is wickedness, and they shall be burned with fire, the penalty this chapter extends to the case it describes.
Matthew 1:3: Judah fathered Perez and Zerah by Tamar, and the line runs on from Perez in the genealogy that opens the Gospel.

translationNotes.term: The duty of a husband's brother
translationNotes.note: Levirate marriage: when a man dies childless his brother takes the widow, and the first son counts as the dead man's, so his name and his land stay in the family. Deuteronomy 25:5-10 sets it out and gives the widow a public remedy against a brother who refuses. At 41:5 Onan goes in but spills the seed, taking the wife while refusing the duty.

An eravon is a deposit handed over to guarantee a payment still owed. At 41:11 Judah leaves his ring, his necklace and his staff, matching Genesis 38:18, and those are exactly the items that identify a man: a seal ring and a carved staff worked as a signature. That is why the pledge convicts him at 41:18.

A town in the low hills between the Judean highlands and the Philistine plain. Sheep shearing was the year's payday and was kept as a feast with drinking, which is why Tamar times her move to it. At 41:8-9 she takes off her widow's clothes, veils herself and sits at the gate on the Timnah road.

At 41:17 Judah orders Tamar burned, as at Genesis 38:24. The law of Moses prescribes burning in two cases: the priest's daughter who plays the harlot, Leviticus 21:9, and a man who takes a woman and her mother, Leviticus 20:14. At 41:25-26 this book extends the penalty to a man who lies with his daughter-in-law or his mother-in-law, and to the woman with him.

Genesis 38:28-30 names them from the birth itself: Zerah's hand comes out first with a scarlet thread tied on it, then Perez breaks out ahead of him, and perets means a breach. Ruth 4:18-22 traces David's line through Perez, and Matthew 1:3 carries the same line forward.

stories.keyTakeaway: Judah's first two sons die and Tamar is left waiting for Shelah, so she veils herself and sits by the road to Timnah. Judah takes her for a harlot and leaves his ring, necklace and staff as a pledge, and when she is brought out to be burned she produces them. She bears Perez and Zerah.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 42
summaryBullets: And in the first year of the third week of the forty-fifth jubilee the famine began to come into the [2171 A.M.] land, and the rain refused to be given to the earth, for none whatever fell. (42:1).
And the earth grew barren, but in the land of Egypt there was food, for Joseph had gathered the seed of the land in the seven years of plenty and had preserved it. (42:2).
And the Egyptians came to Joseph that he might give them food, and he opened the store-houses where was the grain of the first year, and he sold it to the people of the land for gold. (42:3).

<Now the famine was very sore in the land of Canaan>, and Jacob heard that there was food in Egypt, and he sent his ten sons that they should procure food for him in Egypt; but Benjamin he did not send, and <the ten sons of Jacob> arrived <in Egypt> among those that went (there). (42:4).

And Joseph recognised them, but they did not recognise him, and he spoke to them and questioned them, and he said to them; 'Are you not spies and have you not come to explore the approaches of the land? 'And he put them in ward. (42:5).
And after that he set them free again, and detained Simeon alone and sent off his nine brothers. (42:6).
And he filled their sacks with corn, and he put their gold in their sacks, and they did not know. (42:7).
And he commanded them to bring their younger brother, for they had told him their father was living and their younger brother. (42:8).

And they went up from the land of Egypt and they came to the land of Canaan; and they told their father all that had befallen them, and how the lord of the country had spoken roughly to them, and had seized Simeon till they should bring Benjamin. (42:9).
And Jacob said: 'Me have you bereaved of my children! Joseph is not and Simeon also is not, and you will take Benjamin away. On me has your wickedness come. (42:10).

'And he said: 'My son will not go down with you lest perchance he fall sick; for their mother gave birth to two sons, and one has perished, and this one also you will take from me. If perchance he took a fever on the road, you would bring down my old age with sorrow to death.' (42:11).
For he saw that their money had been returned to every man in his sack, and for this reason he feared to send him. (42:12).

And the famine increased and became sore in the land of Canaan, and in all lands save in the land of Egypt, for many of the children of the Egyptians had stored up their seed for food from the time when they saw Joseph gathering seed together and putting it in storehouses and preserving it for the years of famine. (42:13).
And the people of Egypt fed themselves thereon during the first year of their famine. (42:14).
But when Israel saw that the famine was very sore in the land, and that there was no deliverance, he said to his sons: 'Go again, and procure food for us that we die not.' (42:15).
And they said: 'We shall not go; unless our youngest brother go with us, we shall not go.' (42:16).
And Israel saw that if he did not send him with them, they should all perish by reason of the famine (42:17).
And Reuben said: 'Give him into my hand, and if I do not bring him back to you, slay my two sons instead of his soul.' (42:18).

And he said to him: 'He shall not go with you.' And Judah came near and said: 'Send him with me, and if I do not bring him back to you, let me bear the blame before you all the days of my life.' (42:19).

And he sent him with them in the second year of this week on the [2172 A.m.] first day of the month, and they came to the land of Egypt with all those who went, and (they had) presents in their hands, stacte and almonds and terebinth nuts and pure honey. (42:20).

And they went and stood before Joseph, and he saw Benjamin his brother, and he knew him, and said to them: Is this your youngest brother?' And they said to him: 'It is he.' And he said The Lord be gracious to you, my son!' (42:21).
And he sent him into his house and he brought forth Simeon to them and he made a feast for them, and they presented to him the gift which they had brought in their hands. (42:22).
And they eat before him and he gave them all a portion, but the portion of Benjamin was seven times larger than that of any of theirs. (42:23).
And they eat and drank and arose and remained with their asses. (42:24).

And Joseph devised a plan whereby he might learn their thoughts as to whether thoughts of peace prevailed amongst them, and he said to the steward who was over his house: 'Fill all their sacks with food, and return their money to them into their vessels, and my cup, the silver cup out of which I drink, put it in the sack of the youngest, and send them away.' (42:25).
crossRefs: Genesis 42:1-38: Jacob sends ten sons for grain, Joseph charges them with spying, Simeon is bound before their eyes, the money is returned in their sacks, and Reuben offers his own two sons as surety.
Genesis 43:1-34: Jacob at last sends Benjamin with a present and double money, Simeon is brought out to them, and Benjamin's portion at the meal is far larger than the others'.
Genesis 44:1-13: The steward hides the silver cup in Benjamin's sack, overtakes them on the road, and finds it when he searches from the eldest down to the youngest.
Genesis 37:5-11: Joseph's two dreams of the sheaves and of the sun, moon and eleven stars bowing down, which his brothers are now acting out without knowing it.
Genesis 47:4: The sons of Jacob tell Pharaoh they have come to sojourn because the famine is heavy in Canaan and there is no pasture left for their flocks.

translationNotes.note: Egypt's eastern frontier was guarded and travellers were logged, so the charge at 42:5 is a plausible one and not a bare pretext: men arriving out of Canaan in a famine year could be scouting the approaches. Genesis 42:9 has Joseph put it as coming to see the nakedness of the land, meaning where it is undefended.

At 42:23 Benjamin's share at the meal is seven times the others'; Genesis 43:34 says five times. Both describe the same custom, in which the guest of honour is given a visibly larger portion at the host's own direction. The number is one of the small places where this book and Genesis do not read alike.

A minchah is the customary gift that opens a meeting with a superior, not a payment. The list at 42:20 matches Genesis 43:11, the best fruits of the land: stacte, almonds, terebinth nuts and honey. All are light, durable and valuable by weight, which is what makes them fit for a long journey by donkey.

To stand surety is to put yourself in the other man's place if he fails. Reuben offers his own two sons at 42:18 and Judah offers himself at 42:19, and at 43:13 Judah asks to remain a bondsman instead of Benjamin. Proverbs 6:1-5 warns against giving surety for a stranger precisely because the obligation is absolute.

Genesis 44:5 has the steward say his master both drinks from the cup and divines by it, a practice of reading omens from what moves in liquid poured into a bowl. At 42:25 this book mentions only that Joseph drinks from it. Stealing a great man's own drinking vessel was a serious matter in itself, which is what makes the trap work.

stories.keyTakeaway: The famine reaches Canaan and Jacob sends ten sons to Egypt for grain. Joseph knows them, charges them with spying, holds Simeon and sends the rest home with their money back in the sacks. Judah stands surety for Benjamin, and Joseph has his silver cup hidden in the boy's sack.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 43
summaryBullets: And he did as Joseph had told him, and filled all their sacks for them with food and put their money in their sacks, and put the cup in Benjamin's sack. (43:1).

And early in the morning they departed, and it came to pass that, when they had gone from from there, Joseph said to the steward of his house: 'Pursue them, run and seize them, saying, "For good you have requited me with evil; you have stolen from me the silver cup out of which my lord drinks." And bring back to me their youngest brother, and fetch (him) quickly before I go forth to my seat of judgment.' (43:2).
And he ran after them and said to them according to these words. (43:3).

And they said to him: 'God forbid that your servants should do this thing, and steal from the house of your lord any utensil, and the money also which we found in our sacks the first time, we your servants brought back from the land of Canaan. (43:4).

How then should we steal any utensil? Behold here are we and our sacks search, and wherever you findest the cup in the sack of any man amongst us, let him be slain, and we and our asses will serve your lord.' (43:5).
And he said to them: 'Not so, the man with whom I find, him only shall I take as a servant, and you will return in peace to your house.' (43:6).
And as he was searching in their vessels, beginning with the eldest and ending with the youngest, it was found in Benjamin's sack. (43:7).
And they rent their garments, and laded their asses, and returned to the city and came to the house of Joseph, and they all bowed themselves on their faces to the ground before him. (43:8).

And Joseph said to them: 'You have done evil.' And they said: 'What shall we say and how shall we defend ourselves? Our lord has discovered the transgression of his servants; behold we are the servants of our lord, and our asses also. (43:9).

'And Joseph said to them: 'I too fear the Lord; as for you, go you to your homes and let your brother be my servant, for you have done evil. Know you not that a man delights in his cup as I with this cup? And yet you have stolen it from me.' (43:10).

And Judah said: 'O my lord, let your servant, I pray you, speak a word in my lord's ear two brothers did your servant's mother bear to our father: one went away and was lost, and has not been found, and he alone is left of his mother, and your servant our father loves him, and his life also is bound up with the life of this (lad). (43:11).
And it will come to pass, when we go to your servant our father, and the lad is not with us, that he will die, and we shall bring down our father with sorrow to death. (43:12).

Now rather let me, your servant, abide instead of the boy as a bondsman to my lord, and let the lad go with his brethren, for I became surety for him at the hand of your servant our father, and if I do not bring him back, your servant will hear the blame to our father for ever.' (43:13).
And Joseph saw that they were all accordant in goodness one with another, and he could not refrain himself, and he told them that he was Joseph. (43:14).
And he conversed with them in the Hebrew tongue and fell on their neck and wept. (43:15).

But they knew him not and they began to weep. And he said to them: 'Weep not over me, but hasten and bring my father to me; and you see that it is my mouth that speaketh and the eyes of my brother Benjamin see. (43:16).
For behold this is the second year of the famine, and there are still five years without harvest or fruit of trees or ploughing. (43:17).

Come down quickly you and your households, so that you perish not through the famine, and do not be grieved for your possessions, for the Lord sent me before you to set things in order that many people might live. (43:18).
And tell my father that I am still alive, and you, behold, you see that the Lord has made me as a father to Pharaoh, and ruler over his house and over all the land of Egypt. (43:19).
And tell my father of all my glory, and all the riches and glory that the Lord has given me.' (43:20).
And by the command of the mouth of Pharaoh he gave them chariots and provisions for the way, and he gave them all many-coloured raiment and silver. (43:21).
And to their father he sent raiment and silver and ten asses which carried corn, and he sent them away. (43:22).
And they went up and told their father that Joseph was alive, and was measuring out corn to all the nations of the earth, and that he was ruler over all the land of Egypt. (43:23).

And their father did not believe it, for he was beside himself in his mind; but when he saw the wagons which Joseph had sent, the life of his spirit revived, and he said: 'It is enough for me if Joseph lives; I will go down and see him before I die.' (43:24).
crossRefs: Genesis 44:14-34: Judah stands before Joseph and rehearses the whole matter, offering to stay as a slave in the boy's place so that his father is not brought down with sorrow to the grave.
Genesis 45:1-15: Joseph cannot refrain himself, sends every Egyptian out of the room, tells his brothers who he is, and says God sent him ahead of them to preserve life.
Genesis 42:23: Joseph had been speaking with his brothers through an interpreter, which is what makes his speaking Hebrew in this chapter the proof of who he is.
Genesis 37:26-27: Judah proposes selling Joseph to the passing traders rather than killing him, the act his offer in this chapter answers.
Genesis 50:19-21: Joseph tells his brothers not to fear, since they meant evil against him but God meant it for good, to save many people alive.

translationNotes.note: At 43:15 Joseph speaks to his brothers in Hebrew, and that is the proof of identity. Genesis 42:23 says he had been using an interpreter, so the brothers had no reason to think the Egyptian governor understood a word they said in front of him. This book has already made Hebrew the tongue of creation, given back to Abram at 12:25-26.

At 43:13 Judah offers to remain a bondsman in Benjamin's place because he had become surety for him to his father, Genesis 43:9. That offer is the point of the whole test: the brother who proposed selling Joseph at Genesis 37:26-27 now offers to be sold himself in place of Rachel's other son.

At 43:17 Joseph says this is the second year of the famine with five still to run, matching Genesis 45:6. The seven-year cycle announced at 40:3 is being counted off exactly, which is how this book keeps its chronology tight; the family reaches Goshen in the third year, 45:1.

At 43:21-22 Joseph sends his brothers home with many-coloured clothing and silver, and Genesis 45:22 says he gave Benjamin five changes of raiment and three hundred pieces of silver. A change of clothes was a substantial gift and a public mark of favour. A garment of that kind started the trouble, the long coat of Genesis 37:3 that his brothers stripped off him.

stories.keyTakeaway: The steward overtakes the brothers and the cup is found in Benjamin's sack. Judah offers himself as a bondsman in the boy's place, and Joseph cannot hold back any longer; he tells them who he is and speaks to them in Hebrew. He sends them home with wagons, and Jacob's spirit revives at the sight.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 44
summaryBullets: And Israel took his journey from Haran from his house on the new moon of the third month, and he went on the way of the Well of the Oath, and he offered a sacrifice to the God of his father Isaac on the seventh of this month. (44:1).
And Jacob remembered the dream that he had seen at Bethel, and he feared to go down into Egypt. (44:2).

And while he was thinking of sending word to Joseph to come to him, and that he would not go down, he remained there seven days, if perchance he could see a vision as to whether he should remain or go down. (44:3).

And he celebrated the harvest festival of the first-fruits with old grain, for in all the land of Canaan there was not a handful of seed [in the land], for the famine was over all the beasts and cattle and birds, and also over man. (44:4).

And on the sixteenth the Lord appeared to him, and said to him, 'Jacob, Jacob'; and he said, 'Here am I.' And He said to him: 'I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham and Isaac; fear not to go down into Egypt, for I will there make of you a great nation I will go down with you, and I will bring you up (again), and in this land shalt you be buried, and Joseph shall put his hands upon your eyes. (44:5).
Fear not; go down into Egypt.' (44:6).
And his sons rose up, and his sons' sons, and they placed their father and their possessions upon wagons. (44:7).
And Israel rose up from the Well of the Oath on the sixteenth of this third month, and he went to the land of Egypt. (44:8).
And Israel sent Judah before him to his son Joseph to examine the Land of Goshen, for Joseph had told his brothers that they should come and dwell there that they might be near him. (44:9).
And this was the goodliest (land) in the land of Egypt, and near to him, for all (of them) and also for the cattle. (44:10).
And these are the names of the sons of Jacob who went into Egypt with Jacob their father. (44:11).
Reuben, the First-born of Israel; and these are the names of his sons Enoch, and Pallu, and Hezron and Carmi-five. (44:12).
Simeon and his sons; and these are the names of his sons: Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul, the son of the Zephathite woman-seven. (44:13).
Levi and his sons; and these are the names of his sons: Gershon, and Kohath, and Merari-four. (44:14).
Judah and his sons; and these are the names of his sons: Shela, and Perez, and Zerah-four. (44:15).
Issachar and his sons; and these are the names of his sons: Tola, and Phua, and Jasub, and Shimron-five. (44:16).
Zebulon and his sons; and these are the names of his sons: Sered, and Elon, and Jahleel-four. (44:17).

And these are the sons of Jacob and their sons whom Leah bore to Jacob in Mesopotamia, six, and their one sister, Dinah and all the souls of the sons of Leah, and their sons, who went with Jacob their father into Egypt, were twenty-nine, and Jacob their father being with them, they were thirty. (44:18).
And the sons of Zilpah, Leah's handmaid, the wife of Jacob, who bore to Jacob Gad and Ashur. (44:19).
And these are the names of their sons who went with him into Egypt. The sons of Gad: Ziphion, and Haggi, and Shuni, and Ezbon, <and Eri>, and Areli, and Arodi-eight. (44:20).
And the sons of Asher: Imnah, and Ishvah, <and Ishvi>, and Beriah, and Serah, their one sister-six. (44:21).
All the souls were fourteen, and all those of Leah were forty-four. (44:22).
And the sons of Rachel, the wife of Jacob: Joseph and Benjamin. (44:23).
And there were born to Joseph in Egypt before his father came into Egypt, those whom Asenath, daughter of Potiphar priest of Heliopolis bare to him, Manasseh, and Ephraim-three. (44:24).
And the sons of Benjamin: Bela and Becher and Ashbel, Gera, and Naaman, and Ehi, and Rosh, and Muppim, and Huppim, and Ard-eleven. (44:25).
And all the souls of Rachel were fourteen. (44:26).
And the sons of Bilhah, the handmaid of Rachel, the wife of Jacob, whom she bare to Jacob, were Dan and Naphtali. (44:27).
And these are the names of their sons who went with them into Egypt. And the sons of Dan were Hushim, and Samon, and Asudi. and 'Ijaka, and Salomon-six. (44:28).
And they died the year in which they entered into Egypt, and there was left to Dan Hushim alone. (44:29).
And these are the names of the sons of Naphtali Jahziel, and Guni and Jezer, and Shallum, and 'Iv. (44:30).
And 'Iv, who was born after the years of famine, died in Egypt. (44:31).
And all the souls of Rachel were twenty-six. (44:32).

And all the souls of Jacob which went into Egypt were seventy souls. These are his children and his children's children, in all seventy, but five died in Egypt before Joseph, and had no children. (44:33).

And in the land of Canaan two sons of Judah died, Er and Onan, and they had no children, and the children of Israel buried those who perished, and they were reckoned among the seventy Gentile nations. (44:34).
crossRefs: Genesis 46:1-7: Israel offers sacrifices at Beersheba, God speaks to him in the visions of the night and tells him not to fear to go down, promising to go with him and to bring him up again.
Genesis 45:9-13: Joseph tells his brothers to hurry to his father and bring him down to dwell in the land of Goshen, near him, with his children and his flocks and all that he has.
Exodus 1:1-5: The sons of Israel who came into Egypt with Jacob, all the souls that came out of his loins being seventy, with Joseph already in Egypt.
Deuteronomy 10:22: Your fathers went down into Egypt with seventy persons, and now the LORD your God has made you as the stars of heaven for multitude.
Acts 7:14: Joseph sends and calls his father and all his kindred to him, and Stephen gives the number as seventy-five souls, the count carried in the Greek Old Testament.

translationNotes.note: Genesis 46:27, Exodus 1:5 and Deuteronomy 10:22 all give seventy, and 44:33 gives seventy while adding that five of them died in Egypt childless. Stephen says seventy-five at Acts 7:14, the number in the Greek Old Testament, which counts further sons of Joseph. At 44:34 the book sets the figure against the seventy nations of the earth.

The eastern Delta grazing country, watered and good for flocks, and set apart from the main Egyptian population. Genesis 46:34 has Joseph coach his brothers to say they are keepers of cattle, since every shepherd is an abomination to the Egyptians, which is how the family lands Goshen. Exodus 9:26 says there was no hail in the land of Goshen.

translationNotes.term: Waiting seven days for a vision
translationNotes.note: At 44:3-5 Jacob stays seven days at the Well of the Oath hoping for a word before he commits himself, and the answer comes on the sixteenth of the third month. Genesis 46:2-4 gives the vision with no wait attached and no dates. The waiting, the dates and the feast kept there are this book's additions.

At 44:4 Jacob keeps the harvest feast of firstfruits with old grain, because there was not a handful of seed left in Canaan. Leviticus 23:14 forbids eating any of the new crop until the sheaf has been brought, and Leviticus 26:10 speaks of eating old store and clearing out the old for the new. In a failed year last season's grain is all there is.

stories.keyTakeaway: Jacob goes to the Well of the Oath, offers sacrifice, and waits seven days for a word because he is afraid to go down to Egypt. On the sixteenth God tells him not to fear, promising to go down with him and bring him up again. The chapter then lists the seventy souls who went into Egypt.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 45
summaryBullets: And Israel went into the country of Egypt, into the land of Goshen, on the new moon of the fourth [2172 A.M]. month, in the second year of the third week of the forty-fifth jubilee. (45:1).
And Joseph went to meet his father Jacob, to the land of Goshen, and he fell on his father's neck and wept. (45:2).

And Israel said to Joseph: 'Now let me die since I have seen you, and now may the Lord God of Israel be blessed the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac who has not withheld His mercy and His grace from His servant Jacob. (45:3).
It is enough for me that I have seen your face whilst I am yet alive; yea, true is the vision which I saw at Bethel. Blessed be the Lord my God for ever and ever, and blessed be His name.' (45:4).

And Joseph and his brothers eat bread before their father and drank wine, and Jacob rejoiced with exceeding great joy because he saw Joseph eating with his brothers and drinking before him, and he blessed the Creator of all things who had preserved him, and had preserved for him his twelve sons. (45:5).

And Joseph had given to his father and to his brothers as a gift the right of dwelling in the land of Goshen and in Rameses and all the region round about, which he ruled over before Pharaoh. And Israel and his sons dwelt in the land of Goshen, the best part of the land of Egypt and Israel was one hundred and thirty years old when he came into Egypt. (45:6).
And Joseph nourished his father and his brethren and also their possessions with bread as much as sufficed them for the seven years of the famine. (45:7).

And the land of Egypt suffered by reason of the famine, and Joseph acquired all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh in return for food, and he got possession of the people and their cattle and everything for Pharaoh. (45:8).

And the years of the famine were accomplished, and Joseph gave to the people in the land seed and food that they might sow (the land) in the eighth year, for the river had overflowed all the land of Egypt. (45:9).

For in the seven years of the famine it had (not) overflowed and had irrigated only a few places on the banks of the river, but now it overflowed and the Egyptians sowed the land, and it bore much corn that year. (45:10).
And this was the first year of [2178 A.M.] the fourth week of the forty-fifth jubilee. (45:11).

And Joseph took of the corn of the harvest the fifth part for the king and left four parts for them for food and for seed, and Joseph made it an ordinance for the land of Egypt until this day. (45:12).

And Israel lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years, and all the days which he lived were three jubilees, one hundred and forty-seven years, and he died in the fourth [2188 A.M.] year of the fifth week of the forty-fifth jubilee. (45:13).

And Israel blessed his sons before he died and told them everything that would befall them in the land of Egypt; and he made known to them what would come upon them in the last days, and blessed them and gave to Joseph two portions in the land. (45:14).

And he slept with his fathers, and he was buried in the double cave in the land of Canaan, near Abraham his father in the grave which he dug for himself in the double cave in the land of Hebron. (45:15).
And he gave all his books and the books of his fathers to Levi his son that he might preserve them and renew them for his children until this day. (45:16).
crossRefs: Genesis 46:28-34: Joseph goes up to Goshen to meet his father and falls on his neck and weeps a good while, then tells the family what to say to Pharaoh so that they may settle there.
Genesis 47:13-26: Joseph buys the land and the people of Egypt for Pharaoh in return for bread, and fixes the fifth part for the king as a law that stands to this day.
Genesis 49:28-33: Jacob blesses the twelve, charges them to bury him in the cave of Machpelah with his fathers, gathers his feet into the bed and is gathered to his people.
Genesis 48:21-22: Jacob gives Joseph one portion above his brothers, which is how Joseph's two sons come to hold two shares of the land between them.
Genesis 50:12-13: His sons carry him into the land of Canaan and bury him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, exactly as he had commanded them.

translationNotes.note: At 45:12 Joseph takes a fifth of the harvest for the king and leaves four parts for food and seed, calling it an ordinance in Egypt to this day, which follows Genesis 47:24-26. The rate is twenty percent. Genesis 47:22 notes that the priests' land was exempt, because they drew an allowance from Pharaoh and did not have to sell.

Ye'or is the Hebrew word for the Nile, used throughout Genesis and Exodus, as at Exodus 1:22. Egypt's whole crop depended on the yearly flood spreading water and silt over the fields, so a run of low floods is a famine. At 45:9-10 the river had not overflowed through the seven years and then rose again, and the land bore heavily.

A city and district in the eastern Delta, named at 45:6 as part of what Joseph gave his family and at Genesis 47:11 as the land where they were settled. Exodus 1:11 names Raamses as one of the two store cities Israel later built as slaves, so the same ground appears at both ends of the sojourn.

At 45:16 Jacob hands his own books and his fathers' books to Levi to keep and to copy afresh. That closes a chain the book has been building throughout: Enoch writes at 4:17-19, Noah at 10:13-14, and Abraham's writings are being read aloud at 39:6. Genesis records none of it.

stories.keyTakeaway: Israel comes into Goshen and Joseph meets him there. Joseph buys all Egypt for Pharaoh with food, and when the river floods again he fixes the fifth part as the king's share. Israel lives seventeen years in Egypt, dies at a hundred and forty-seven, and leaves all his books to Levi.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 46
summaryBullets: And it came to pass that after Jacob died the children of Israel multiplied in the land of Egypt, and they became a great nation, and they were of one accord in heart, so that brother loved brother and every man helped his brother, and they increased abundantly and multiplied exceedingly, ten [2242 A.M.] weeks of years, all the days of the life of Joseph. (46:1).

And there was no Satan nor any evil all the days of the life of Joseph which he lived after his father Jacob, for all the Egyptians honoured the children of Israel all the days of the life of Joseph. (46:2).

And Joseph died being a hundred and ten years old; seventeen years he lived in the land of Canaan, and ten years he was a servant, and three years in prison, and eighty years he was under the king, ruling all the land of Egypt. (46:3).
And he died and all his brethren and all that generation. (46:4).
And he commanded the children of Israel before he died that they should carry his bones with them when they went forth from the land of Egypt. (46:5).

And he made them swear regarding his bones, for he knew that the Egyptians would not again bring forth and bury him in the land of Canaan, for Makamaron, king of Canaan, while dwelling in the land of Assyria, fought in the valley with the king of Egypt and slew him there, and pursued after the Egyptians to the gates of 'Ermon. (46:6).

But he was not able to enter, for another, a new king, had become king of Egypt, and he was stronger than he, and he returned to the land of Canaan, and the gates of Egypt were closed, and none went out and none came into Egypt. (46:7).
And Joseph died in the forty-sixth jubilee, in the sixth week, in the second year, and they buried him in the land of Egypt, and [2242 A.M.] all his brethren died after him. (46:8).

And the king of Egypt went forth to war with the king of Canaan [2263 A.M.] in the forty-seventh jubilee, in the second week in the second year, and the children of Israel brought forth all the bones of the children of Jacob save the bones of Joseph, and they buried them in the field in the double cave in the mountain. (46:9).
And the most (of them) returned to Egypt, but a few of them remained in the mountains of Hebron, and Amram your father remained with them. (46:10).
And the king of Canaan was victorious over the king of Egypt, and he closed the gates of Egypt. (46:11).

And he devised an evil device against the children of Israel of afflicting them and he said to the people of Egypt: 'Behold the people of the children of Israel have increased and multiplied more than we. (46:12).

Come and let us deal wisely with them before they become too many, and let us afflict them with slavery before war come upon us and before they too fight against us; else they will join themselves to our enemies and get them up out of our land, for their hearts and faces are towards the land of Canaan.' (46:13).

And he set over them taskmasters to afflict them with slavery; and they built strong cities for Pharaoh, Pithom, and Raamses and they built all the walls and all the fortifications which had fallen in the cities of Egypt. (46:14).
And they made them serve with rigour, and the more they dealt evilly with them, the more they increased and multiplied. (46:15).
And the people of Egypt abominated the children of Israel (46:16).
crossRefs: Genesis 50:22-26: Joseph lives a hundred and ten years, makes the children of Israel swear to carry his bones up with them, dies and is put in a coffin in Egypt.
Exodus 1:6-14: Joseph and all his brothers and that generation die, Israel multiplies, a new king who did not know Joseph sets taskmasters over them, and they build Pithom and Raamses.
Exodus 13:19: Moses takes the bones of Joseph with him, because Joseph had bound the children of Israel by an oath concerning them.
Joshua 24:32: The bones of Joseph are buried at Shechem in the plot of ground Jacob bought from the sons of Hamor, and it became the inheritance of Joseph's children.
Hebrews 11:22: By faith Joseph, when his end was near, spoke of the departure of the children of Israel and gave instructions about his bones.

translationNotes.note: At 46:5-6 Joseph makes Israel swear to carry his bones out, and the book explains why he could not be taken to Canaan straight away: war had closed the frontier. Genesis 50:26 has him embalmed and laid in a coffin in Egypt, Exodus 13:19 has Moses take the bones along, and Joshua 24:32 has them buried at Shechem generations later.

At 46:6-11 a war between the king of Canaan and the king of Egypt shuts the frontier so that nobody goes in or out, and that is this book's account of how Israel came to be trapped. Exodus 1:8-10 gives a different reason, a new king who did not know Joseph and feared how many Israel had become. The war is the book's; Exodus does not carry it.

Two store cities in the eastern Delta, named at Exodus 1:11 and again at 46:14. A store city was a fortified granary and supply depot for a frontier army, which is why the labour was heavy and why the sites sit where they do, on the road out of Egypt toward Canaan.

Literally chiefs of the levies, the officers set over gangs of forced labour. Exodus 1:11 uses the phrase, and Exodus 5:6-14 shows the system working, with Egyptian officers over Israelite foremen who were beaten when the brick quota fell short. At 46:14-15 the book records the same arrangement and the same result: the harder the pressure, the faster they multiplied.

stories.keyTakeaway: Israel multiplies in Egypt and lives at peace as long as Joseph is alive. Joseph dies at a hundred and ten and makes them swear about his bones. War between Egypt and Canaan closes the frontier, and a stronger king sets taskmasters over Israel, who build Pithom and Raamses under forced labour.

stories.title: 📜 Jubilees 47
summaryBullets: And in the seventh week, in the seventh year, in the forty-seventh jubilee, your father went forth [2303 A.M.] from the land of Canaan, and you wast born in the fourth week, in the sixth year thereof, in the [2330 A.M.] forty-eighth jubilee; this was the time of tribulation on the children of Israel. (47:1).
And Pharaoh, king of Egypt, issued a command regarding them that they should cast all their male children which were born into the river. (47:2).
And they cast them in for seven months until the day that you wast born (47:3).

And your mother hid you for three months, and they told regarding her. And she made an ark for you, and covered it with pitch and asphalt, and placed it in the flags on the bank of the river, and she placed you in it seven days, and your mother came by night and suckled you, and by day Miriam, your sister, guarded you from the birds. (47:4).
